definition_zh: 预先取得；预先准备、提前处理；预防、先发制人；预知；期待、期盼；先兆、预尝；（音乐）提前音；（修辞）预辩
definition_en: the act of taking, doing, or knowing something in advance: prior possession, preparation, forestalling, foreknowledge, or expectation
core_image: 一只手在别人伸手之前，先把桌上的东西拢进自己怀里
scene: In anticipation of the winter fair, a stallholder claims the corner spot and stacks firewood behind the counter.
sceneCN: 这里 anticipation 是「提前占有、预先准备」（第 1 个义项：预先取得）；句意：为了冬季集市，摊主提前占下角落的位置，并在柜台后码好柴火。图中可辨识物件：空摊位、角落标记、成捆柴火、摊主的手、尚未开门的集市棚架。

pos.zh: 预先取得；预先准备；预知；期待；（音乐）提前音；（修辞）预辩

collocations.zh: 提前偿付（在到期日之前付款）

derivatives.zh: 预料；预期；提前处理；先发制人
预期的；提前准备的；先发制人的
有预期倾向的；提前行动的
未预料到的；出乎意料的

senses.title: Taking beforehand: getting something into your hands early
senses.titleCN: 先取：提前把东西拿到手
senses.definition: the act of taking possession of or taking up something before the expected time
senses.definitionCN: 在预期时间之前先占有或取用某物
senses.example: Their anticipation of the best seats left the latecomers standing.
senses.exampleCN: 他们抢先占下了最好的座位，迟到的人只好站着。
senses.why: Latin anticipatio renders anticipare, literally 'taking into possession beforehand' (anti- 'before' + capere 'to take'). The noun names the completed act of getting there first.
senses.whyCN: 拉丁语 anticipatio 对应 anticipare，字面是“提前拿进占有”（anti-“在前”+ capere“拿取”）。这个名词命名的就是“抢先到手”这一完成的动作。

senses.title: Preparing ahead: taking care of something in advance
senses.titleCN: 预先安排：提前把事办妥
senses.definition: the act of arranging for or attending to something before it is needed
senses.definitionCN: 在某事需要之前就安排或照料好它
senses.example: The preparation of the accounts in anticipation of the audit saved the company a week.
senses.exampleCN: 为审计提前整理账目，为公司省下了一周时间。
senses.why: Once 'taking' is applied to duties rather than objects, what is taken is care. Latin anticipare could mean 'take care of ahead of time', so the noun moves from possession to prior arrangement.
senses.whyCN: 当“拿取”的对象从物件变成责任，被拿到的就是“照料”。拉丁语 anticipare 可表“提前照料”，于是名词从“占有”转向“预先安排”。

senses.title: Forestalling: acting before something can happen
senses.titleCN: 先发制人：抢在事情发生之前动手
senses.definition: the act of preventing or pre-empting an event by acting first
senses.definitionCN: 通过抢先行动来阻止或预先化解某件事
senses.example: The troops moved in anticipation of the attack and seized the ridge first.
senses.exampleCN: 部队为防敌军进攻而先发制人，抢先占领了山脊。
senses.why: If you take the ground before the other side arrives, the event cannot unfold as planned. Around 1600 the noun acquired this sense of pre-emption, still alive in military and medical 'in anticipation of'.
senses.whyCN: 若在对方到达前先占住地面，事情就无法按原计划展开。约 1600 年，这个词获得了“先发制人”的含义，至今仍活在军事和医学的 in anticipation of 中。

senses.title: Foreknowledge: knowing before it happens
senses.titleCN: 预知：事情发生前先知道
senses.definition: knowledge of an event before it occurs
senses.definitionCN: 在某事件发生之前就掌握关于它的知识
senses.example: Her anticipation of the market crash came from reading the same data everyone else ignored.
senses.exampleCN: 她对市场崩盘的预知，来自阅读那些被别人忽略的同一批数据。
senses.why: In the 1640s the word moved from acting ahead to knowing ahead: the mind takes the future into itself before the event arrives. The underlying gesture is still capere, to grasp.
senses.whyCN: 17 世纪 40 年代，这个词从“提前行动”移到“提前知道”：心智在事件到来之前先把未来抓进来。底层动作仍是 capere“抓取”。

senses.title: Expectation: awaiting something with hope or fear
senses.titleCN: 期待：怀着希望或不安等待
senses.definition: the state of expecting something to happen, especially with pleasure or anxiety
senses.definitionCN: 预期某事将会发生的心态，尤带喜悦或焦虑
senses.example: The children's anticipation grew as the first snow clouds appeared.
senses.exampleCN: 初雪的云一出现，孩子们的期待就更浓了。
senses.why: The 'expectation' sense appears in 1749. It keeps the 'before' of the root but drops active preparation, leaving the mind already holding the future. Etymologically it is not the same as expect, which looks outward (ex- + spectare).
senses.whyCN: “期待”义出现于 1749 年。它保留了词根的“在前”，却丢掉了主动准备，只剩下心智提前握有未来。词源上它并不等于 expect——后者是“向外看”（ex- + spectare）。

senses.title: A foretaste: an advance hint of what is coming
senses.titleCN: 预尝：先尝到未来的一小口
senses.definition: a partial experience or preview of something before the full event
senses.definitionCN: 在完整事件到来之前，对它的部分体验或预先领略
senses.example: The first chapter is an anticipation of the themes developed later.
senses.exampleCN: 第一章是对后文展开的主题的一次预尝。
senses.why: The noun can name the thing taken early as well as the act: a small portion of the future is sampled in advance, like a foretaste of a meal.
senses.whyCN: 这个名词既能指“提前拿取的动作”，也能指“被提前拿到的东西”：未来的一小部分被预先品尝，就像饭前的一口试味。

senses.title: Early payment: discharging a debt before it is due
senses.titleCN: 提前偿付：在到期前还清款项
senses.definition: the payment of money before the due date, often at a discount
senses.definitionCN: 在到期日之前付款，常因此获得折扣
senses.example: The invoice offered a 2 percent discount for anticipation of payment.
senses.exampleCN: 发票给出提前付款可享 2% 的折扣。
senses.why: In commerce, 'taking before' becomes paying before: the debtor takes the due date out of the future. This is a narrow technical branch of the same 'beforehand' idea.
senses.whyCN: 在商业里，“提前拿取”变成“提前支付”：债务人把到期日从未来挪走。这是同一个“在前”观念下的一条狭窄技术分支。

senses.title: Music: a note sounded before its harmony arrives
senses.titleCN: 音乐中的提前音：比和声早到一拍
senses.definition: in harmony and counterpoint, a tone that enters one beat before the chord it belongs to
senses.definitionCN: 在和声与对位中，比它所属和弦早一拍进入的音
senses.example: The violin's anticipation slips in a beat before the downbeat chord.
senses.exampleCN: 小提琴的提前音在和弦落下前的一拍滑了进来。
senses.why: Here the 'before' is measured in beats. The note is taken up early and held until the harmony catches up, so the musical term is a literal local use of the core image.
senses.whyCN: 这里的“在前”以拍子计量。音被提前拿起来，一直保持到和声赶上，因此这个音乐术语是核心意象的一次字面化局部使用。

senses.title: Rhetoric: answering an objection before it is raised
senses.titleCN: 修辞中的预辩：抢在质疑之前先答
senses.definition: the rhetorical figure of raising and answering a possible objection in advance (prolepsis)
senses.definitionCN: 提前提出并回答可能出现的反对意见的修辞手法（预辩法）
senses.example: The essay's anticipation of the counterargument made the conclusion harder to resist.
senses.exampleCN: 这篇文章预先答驳了相反论点，使结论更难被抗拒。
senses.why: In rhetoric the speaker takes the opponent's point into the argument first, disarming it before it is spoken. The Latin noun was already used for this figure, so the branch is ancient rather than modern.
senses.whyCN: 在修辞中，说话者先把对方的论点拿进自己的论证里，在它被说出口之前就卸掉它的力。拉丁语名词早已用于这一辞格，所以这条分支很古老，并非现代新义。

intro.en: Anticipation is a Latin action noun that reached English through French; the verb anticipate was probably back-formed from it, though it may also come directly from Latin anticipatus. Dates are approximate, and the noun is older in English than the verb.
intro.cn: anticipation 是经法语进入英语的拉丁语动作名词；动词 anticipate 一般认为由它逆构，也可能直接取自拉丁语 anticipatus，这一步来源不确定。年代为大致估计；在英语里名词比动词更早。

items.en: The sense 'expectation' is recorded. It is the newest layer and must not be read back into the older senses.
items.cn: “期待”义见于记载。这是最新的一层，不能反向套到更早的义项上。

items.en: The sense 'foreknowledge, knowing beforehand' appears, moving the word from action to knowledge.
items.cn: “预知、提前知道”义出现，这个词从行动转向知识。

items.en: The sense 'prevention, forestalling' is recorded, from acting before an event can take its course.
items.cn: “预防、先发制人”义见于记载，来自抢在事件展开之前行动。

items.en: The verb anticipate is recorded, either back-formed from the noun anticipation or taken from Latin anticipatus, the past participle of anticipare.
items.cn: 动词 anticipate 见于记载，或由名词 anticipation 逆构，或直接取自拉丁语 anticipatus——anticipare 的过去分词。

items.en: Latin anticipatio is the action noun of anticipare 'take (care of) ahead of time', literally 'taking into possession beforehand'. The English suffix -ion comes from Latin -ionem, which names an action or its result.
items.cn: 拉丁语 anticipatio 是 anticipare“提前（照料）”的动作名词，字面为“提前拿进占有”。英语后缀 -ion 来自拉丁语 -ionem，表示动作或其结果。

items.en: anticipare joins anti-, an old form of ante 'before' (from PIE *ant- 'front, forehead'), with capere 'to take' (from PIE *kap- 'to grasp'). The 'before' is spatial first, then temporal.
items.cn: anticipare 由 anti-（ante“在前”的古形，出自原始印欧语 *ant-“前面、额头”）加 capere“拿取”（出自 PIE *kap-“抓握”）构成。“在前”先是空间义，后转为时间义。

note.en: The first group separates accidental spelling neighbours from the real family; the second group compares words that share part of the meaning.
note.cn: 第一组把偶然撞形的词与真正的同族词分开；第二组比较只共享部分含义的词。

entries.definition: the ancient past, or an object from it. It begins with anti- by accident; its root is antiquus 'old', not ante 'before'.
entries.definitionCN: 古代；古物。它只是碰巧以 anti- 开头，词根是 antiquus“古老的”，不是 ante“在前”。

entries.definition: a strong dislike. The anti- here is Greek anti 'against', and the second element is pathos 'feeling', not capere.
entries.definitionCN: 强烈的反感。这里的 anti- 是希腊语 anti“反对”，第二部分是 pathos“情感”，与 capere 无关。

entries.definition: the verb recorded in the 1530s, back-formed from anticipation or taken from Latin anticipatus. In English the noun came first.
entries.definitionCN: 1530 年代记录的动词，由 anticipation 逆构或取自拉丁语 anticipatus。在英语里名词先出现。

entries.definition: the belief that something will happen. It stresses the waiting mind, while anticipation often adds prior preparation.
entries.definitionCN: 认为某事会发生的信念。它强调等待的心态，而 anticipation 常另含提前准备。

entries.definition: careful thinking about what will happen before acting. It stresses deliberate planning, where anticipation may be mere foreknowledge.
entries.definitionCN: 行动前对将发生之事的仔细考虑。它强调有意的筹划，而 anticipation 可能只是预知。

entries.definition: the act of acting before another can, especially to block them. It is the legal and military edge of anticipation's forestalling sense.
entries.definitionCN: 抢在别人之前行动，尤指使其无法行动。它是 anticipation“先发制人”义在法律和军事上的锐化版。

normalIntro.en: Normal associations use the real parts of the word and its real relatives, not invented rhymes.
normalIntro.cn: 正常联想只使用这个词真实的构成成分和真实同族词，不用编造的顺口溜。

normal.en: anticipate is a back-formation from anticipation, so in English the noun is older than the verb.
normal.cn: anticipate 是由 anticipation 逆构的，所以在英语里名词比动词年长。

normal.en: The anti- in anticipation is not 'against' but an old form of ante 'before', the same 'before' in ante meridiem (a.m.).
normal.cn: anticipation 里的 anti- 不是“反对”，而是 ante“在前”的古形，和 ante meridiem（a.m. 上午）里的“在前”相同。

normal.en: capere 'to take' also gives capture, capable and capacity: anticipation is literally 'taking first'.
normal.cn: capere“拿取”还给出 capture、capable、capacity：anticipation 字面上就是“先拿”。

normal.en: In anticipation of is the everyday phrase: it means 'before, and in preparation for'.
normal.cn: in anticipation of 是日常短语，意思是“在……之前，并为……做准备”。

normal.en: Expectation is only the newest layer (1749); beneath it lie possession, prevention and foreknowledge.
normal.cn: “期待”只是最新的一层（1749）；它下面还压着占有、预防和预知。

abstract.en: Picture a hand reaching across a table and pulling an object toward itself before anyone else moves.
abstract.cn: 想象一只手越过桌面，在别人动手之前先把东西拢向自己。

abstract.en: The same hand can take a duty, take ground before an enemy, take the future into the mind, or take a note into the bar early.
abstract.cn: 同一只手可以接下责任、抢在敌人前占住地面、把未来拿进心里，或把一个音符提前放进小节。

abstract.en: All nine senses keep the prefix 'before' and vary only what is taken: goods, care, ground, knowledge, a foretaste, money, a beat, an argument.
abstract.cn: 九个义项都保留“在前”，变化的只是被拿取的东西：货物、照料、地面、知识、预尝、金钱、拍子、论点。

examples.en: Scientists collected data in anticipation of the drought.
examples.cn: 科学家们为防备干旱而提前收集了数据。

examples.en: The audience waited in anticipation as the curtain rose.
examples.cn: 幕布升起时，观众满怀期待地等待着。

examples.en: The law's anticipation of fraud made the contract void from the start.
examples.cn: 法律对欺诈的预先防范使这份合同自始无效。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「俺替谁赔身」——俺替谁赔这身衣裳？事先就料到要赔，早做了准备 → anticipation 预料、预先准备

root: 拉丁语 anticipare“提前取得、提前照料”＝anti-（ante“在前”的古形）+ capere“拿取”；anticipation 经拉丁动作名词 anticipatio 与法语进入英语，核心是“抢先拿到手、提前处理”。

sensesIntro.en: Nine senses of anticipation all keep one prefix: something is taken before its time. What is taken changes — goods, care, ground, knowledge, a foretaste, money, a musical beat, an opponent's argument.
sensesIntro.cn: anticipation 的九个义项都保留同一个“在前”：某物在它的时间之前被拿取。变化的只是被拿的东西——货物、照料、地面、知识、预尝、金钱、音乐拍子、对方的论点。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a hand takes an object before anyone else reaches it.
core.cn: 核心意象：一只手赶在别人伸手之前把东西拿走。

branches.en: POSSESSION AND CARE: first the goods are taken early, then the duty is taken care of early.
branches.cn: 占有与照料：先提前拿到货物，再提前把责任办妥。

branches.en: FORESTALLING: taking the ground first prevents the event from taking its course.
branches.cn: 先发制人：先占住地面，使事件无法按原样展开。

branches.en: KNOWING AHEAD: the mind grasps the future, and a small part of it can be tasted in advance.
branches.cn: 提前知道：心智抓住未来，而未来的一小部分可以提前品尝。

branches.en: EXPECTATION: the active preparation fades, leaving the mind holding what has not yet arrived.
branches.cn: 期待：主动准备淡去，只剩心智握有尚未到来之物。

branches.en: FORMAL EARLY ARRIVALS: money paid before the due date, a note before its chord, an answer before the objection.
branches.cn: 形式化的提前到达：到期前付的钱、和弦前的音、质疑前的回答。

intro.en: Anticipation is Latin anticipat- plus -ion. The suffix -ion, from Latin -ionem, turns an action verb into the name of the action or its result; English then builds the verb and adjectives around this noun.
intro.cn: anticipation 是拉丁词干 anticipat- 加 -ion。后缀 -ion 出自拉丁语 -ionem，把动作动词变成“动作或其结果”的名称；英语随后围绕这个名词构造动词和形容词。

latinIntro.en: The two Latin pieces are ante/anti- 'before' and capere 'to take, grasp'. capere supplies the stems capt- and cip-, visible in capture, captive, accept and participate.
latinIntro.cn: 两个拉丁成分是 ante/anti-“在前”和 capere“拿取、抓握”。capere 提供 capt- 与 cip- 词干，见于 capture、captive、accept、participate。

items.meaning: the act of taking or knowing in advance, or its result
items.meaningCN: 提前拿取或预知的行为，及其结果（-ion 构成动作／结果名词）
items.example: The announcement was met with anticipation rather than alarm.
items.exampleCN: 这项公告引来的是期待，而非惊慌。

items.meaning: to expect, foresee, or deal with in advance
items.meaningCN: 预料；预见；提前处理
items.example: We anticipate a rise in demand next quarter.
items.exampleCN: 我们预计下季度需求会上升。

items.meaning: done in preparation for something expected
items.meaningCN: 为预期之事做准备的；预支的（-ory 构成形容词）
items.example: The bank imposed an anticipatory penalty on early repayment.
items.exampleCN: 银行对提前还款收取预先设定的罚金。

items.meaning: tending to expect or act in advance
items.meaningCN: 倾向于预期或提前行动的（-ive 构成形容词）
items.example: Her anticipative habits kept the team supplied.
items.exampleCN: 她凡事提前准备的习惯让团队物资不断。

items.meaning: not expected or allowed for
items.meaningCN: 未预料到的；未考虑到的（un- 否定 + -ed 形容词）
items.example: An unanticipated delay doubled the cost.
items.exampleCN: 一场未预料到的延误使成本翻倍。

items.meaning: a person who expects or acts beforehand
items.meaningCN: 预想者；提前行动的人（-or 表示施动者）
items.example: The early buyer was an anticipator of the shortage.
items.exampleCN: 那位早早买入的人预见了短缺。

items.meaning: able to hold or take in; having the power to do
items.meaningCN: 有能力的；能容纳的（cap-“拿、容纳”+ -able）
items.example: The tank is capable of holding ten thousand litres.
items.exampleCN: 这个罐子能装一万升。

items.meaning: the power to hold, receive, or do
items.meaningCN: 容量；能力（-ity 构成性质／状态名词）
items.example: The hall has a capacity of eight hundred people.
items.exampleCN: 这个大厅可容纳八百人。

items.meaning: the act of catching and holding something
items.meaningCN: 捕获；俘获（-ure 构成动作／结果名词）
items.example: The capture of the escaped horse took three hours.
items.exampleCN: 花了三个小时才抓住那匹逃跑的马。

items.meaning: to take something offered to oneself
items.meaningCN: 接受（字面“拿向自己”）；承认
items.example: She accepted the invitation without hesitation.
items.exampleCN: 她毫不犹豫地接受了邀请。

latinEntries.meaning: to take beforehand, take care of ahead of time
a taking beforehand; the action noun behind anticipation
latinEntries.meaningCN: 提前拿取；anticipation 所本的拉丁动作名词

definition_zh: 明显地、看得见地（古义）；显然；表面上看来、似乎；据判断、就所能判断而言；据说；反讽用法（嘴上说如此）
definition_en: in a way that is visible or evident; also, as it seems from appearances or from the available evidence, whether or not it is true
core_image: 一扇擦得太亮的玻璃：人人都看得见后面的东西，却看不出那层玻璃本身
scene: Apparently the bridge is closed, yet the barrier has been pushed aside and fresh footprints lead across it.
sceneCN: 这里 apparently 是「表面上看来、据说如此」（第 3 个义项：外表如此但未必为真）；句意：看样子桥是封了的，可路障已被推开，桥上有新鲜的脚印。图中可辨识物件：封闭路障、被推开的挡板、桥上的脚印、远处仍在走的人、桥头的告示牌。

pos.zh: 明显地；显然；看来；据说；就所能判断而言

collocations.zh: 表面上健康的；表观健康的

derivatives.zh: 明显的；表面上的；显而易见的

senses.title: Visibly: in a way that can be seen
senses.titleCN: 看得见地：以肉眼可见的方式
senses.definition: in a manner that is open to sight, so that others can see it
senses.definitionCN: 以肉眼可见、旁人能看到的方式
senses.example: The crack was apparently visible from the far side of the room.
senses.exampleCN: 那道裂缝从房间另一头就看得见。
senses.why: The word is recorded in the late 14c. as 'visibly, openly'. It is apparent + -ly, and apparent at that date meant 'clearly understood' as well as 'easily seen'. The starting point is simply the eye.
senses.whyCN: 这个词在 14 世纪晚期记录为“看得见地、公开地”。它是 apparent + -ly，而当时的 apparent 既有“清楚易懂”也有“容易看见”之义。起点就是眼睛。

senses.title: Evidently: clear to the mind
senses.titleCN: 显然：对心智而言清楚明白
senses.definition: in a way that is clearly true or clearly to be understood
senses.definitionCN: 以明显为真、或明显可以被理解的方式
senses.example: He was apparently the only person who had read the report.
senses.exampleCN: 显然他是唯一读过那份报告的人。
senses.why: By the 1550s apparently meant 'evidently'. The light has moved from the eye to the understanding: what can be seen plainly is taken as plainly true.
senses.whyCN: 到 16 世纪 50 年代，apparently 已表“显然”。光从眼睛移到了理解：能看得清清楚楚的，就被当作明明白白为真。

senses.title: To all appearances: as it seems, perhaps falsely
senses.titleCN: 表面上看来：外表如此，未必为真
senses.definition: according to outward appearance, with the implication that the reality may be different
senses.definitionCN: 依照外在表象而言，并暗示实情可能不同
senses.example: Apparently the door was locked, but the key turned without resistance.
senses.exampleCN: 表面上那扇门是锁着的，可钥匙一转就开了。
senses.why: In the 1560s the word took on 'to all appearances'. Once sight is separated from truth, the same visible surface becomes a mask: apparent can mean 'seeming' as opposed to 'real'.
senses.whyCN: 16 世纪 60 年代，这个词获得“就外表看来”之义。一旦“看见”与“真实”被分开，同一个可见的表面就成了面具：apparent 可以指“表面的”而非“真实的”。

senses.title: As far as can be judged: from the available evidence
senses.titleCN: 据判断：根据现有证据看来
senses.definition: so far as one can tell from the evidence available, without claiming certainty
senses.definitionCN: 根据手头证据所能判断的范围而言，并不宣称确定
senses.example: Apparently the two events are connected, though no record proves it.
senses.exampleCN: 从现有材料看，这两件事是有关联的，尽管没有记录能证明。
senses.why: The 1846 sense 'so far as can be judged' turns the word into an explicit limit on knowledge. It says: this is what the evidence shows, not what is certainly the case.
senses.whyCN: 1846 年出现的“就所能判断而言”把这个词变成对知识范围的明确限定。它说的是“证据显示如此”，而不是“事实必定如此”。

senses.title: Reportative: it is said that
senses.titleCN: 传闻性用法：据说
senses.definition: used at the start of a clause to report what is said or believed without endorsing it
senses.definitionCN: 用于句首，转述所说或所信之事，而说话者并不背书
senses.example: Apparently, the whole department is moving to the new building.
senses.exampleCN: 据说整个部门都要搬到新楼去。
senses.why: This is the 'as it seems' branch applied to hearsay: the speaker has not seen the event, only its appearance in talk. The word marks the source as second-hand.
senses.whyCN: 这是“看来”分支用在传闻上：说话者没有亲见事件，只见到它在言谈中的“样子”。这个词把信息来源标为二手。

senses.title: Ironic: 'so I am told', said with doubt
senses.titleCN: 反讽用法：嘴上说如此，心里并不买账
senses.definition: used to repeat a claim with scepticism or mild mockery, implying the speaker does not accept it
senses.definitionCN: 带着怀疑或轻微嘲讽重复某种说法，暗示说话者并不接受
senses.example: Apparently I was wrong, although the figures still say otherwise.
senses.exampleCN: 据说是我错了，尽管数字仍然显示并非如此。
senses.why: Irony reverses the evidential hedge: the word still says 'this is how it appears', but the tone adds 'and appearance is not enough'. The 1560s gap between seeming and being becomes a rhetorical weapon.
senses.whyCN: 反讽把这种“证据限定”倒转过来：词面仍说“看起来如此”，语气却加上“光看起来还不够”。16 世纪 60 年代“表象”与“实存”之间的缝隙，在这里成了修辞武器。

senses.title: Apparently + adjective: on the surface of it
senses.titleCN: apparently + 形容词：表面上显得……
senses.definition: used before an adjective to say that something seems to have that quality, especially in medicine or description
senses.definitionCN: 置于形容词前，表示某物看来具有该性质，尤用于医学或描述性语境
senses.example: The apparently healthy trees were already hollow inside.
senses.exampleCN: 那些看起来健康的树，内里其实已经空了。
senses.why: Here -ly modifies the adjective rather than the verb: 'apparently healthy' means 'healthy in appearance'. The suffix keeps its 'seeming' value and narrows it to one visible property.
senses.whyCN: 这里 -ly 修饰的是形容词而非动词：apparently healthy 意为“表面上健康”。后缀保留“看来”之义，并把它收窄到某一可见属性上。

senses.title: Scientific hedge: indicated but not established
senses.titleCN: 科学写作中的限定：有迹象但尚未确证
senses.definition: in academic or scientific writing, used for a result that the evidence suggests but does not prove
senses.definitionCN: 在学术或科学写作中，用于证据提示但尚未证明的结果
senses.example: The treatment is apparently effective in mice, but no human trial has been run.
senses.exampleCN: 这种疗法在小鼠身上看来有效，但尚未进行人体试验。
senses.why: This is the 1846 evidential sense sharpened into a methodological rule: appearance is a claim about observed data, and the word keeps the conclusion short of proof. It is the opposite of the unhedged obviously.
senses.whyCN: 这是 1846 年证据义在方法学上的锐化：表象只是关于观察数据的断言，这个词让结论停在证明之前。它正是不加保留的 obviously 的反面。

intro.en: Apparently is not a regular derivative of the verb appear. It is apparent + -ly, with -ly from Old English -lice. The history is a drift from 'visibly' to 'evidently' to 'seemingly', and dates are approximate.
intro.cn: apparently 并不是动词 appear 的规则派生词，而是 apparent + -ly，其中 -ly 来自古英语 -lice。它的历史是一次从“看得见”到“显然”再到“表面上看来”的漂移，年代为大致估计。

items.en: apparently is first recorded, meaning 'visibly, openly'. It is formed from apparent plus the adverb suffix -ly.
items.cn: apparently 最早记录，意为“看得见地、公开地”。它由 apparent 加副词后缀 -ly 构成。

items.en: apparent itself means 'indisputable, clearly understood' in the late 14c., and by c.1400 'easily seen or perceived'. The adjective already carries both the mental and the visual sense.
items.cn: apparent 本身在 14 世纪晚期表“无可争辩、清楚易懂”，到约 1400 年又表“容易看见或感知”。这个形容词同时带着心智与视觉两义。

items.en: apparent comes from Old French aparant, the present participle of aparoir 'to appear'.
items.cn: apparent 来自古法语 aparant，是 aparoir“出现”的现在分词。

items.en: Latin apparentem, accusative of apparens, is the present participle of apparere 'appear, come in sight', from ad- 'to' + parere 'come in sight'.
items.cn: 拉丁语 apparentem（apparens 的宾格）是 apparere“出现、进入视野”的现在分词，由 ad-“向”+ parere“进入视野”构成。

items.en: The meaning passes through 'evidently' (1550s), 'to all appearances, but perhaps not truly' (1560s), and 'so far as can be judged' (1846).
items.cn: 词义依次经过“显然”（16 世纪 50 年代）、“就外表看来，但未必为真”（16 世纪 60 年代），以及“就所能判断而言”（1846 年）。

items.en: The suffix -ly goes back to Old English -lice, an adverb-forming ending. Because apparently is built on the adjective, it is not the same formation as appear + -ly, which does not exist.
items.cn: 后缀 -ly 可追溯到古英语 -lice，是构成副词的词尾。因为 apparently 建于形容词之上，它与并不存在的 appear + -ly 不是同一种构造。

note.en: The first group holds spelling and family neighbours that are easily confused with apparently; the second group holds adverbs of similar meaning.
note.cn: 第一组是与 apparently 容易混淆的拼写和词族近邻；第二组是意思相近的副词。

entries.definition: the adjective from which apparently is formed: 'clearly visible' or 'seeming'. The adverb adds -ly to this, not to the verb appear.
entries.definitionCN: 构成 apparently 的形容词：“清晰可见的”或“表面上的”。副词是在这个形容词后加 -ly，而不是加在动词 appear 后。

entries.definition: a ghostly appearance or sudden sight. It comes from the same Latin apparere, but through a different noun suffix, so it is a cousin rather than a form of apparently.
entries.definitionCN: 幽灵般的显现或突然出现的景象。它同出拉丁语 apparere，但走的是另一条名词后缀路径，因此只是远亲，不是 apparently 的变形。

entries.definition: allowing light through, so that what is behind can be seen. It shares Latin parere 'come in sight' with apparent, but the prefix trans- changes the image.
entries.definitionCN: 透明的，能看见后面的东西。它与 apparent 共享拉丁语 parere“进入视野”，但前缀 trans- 改变了意象。

entries.definition: in a way that is clear to everyone. It claims certainty, while apparently often leaves room for doubt.
entries.definitionCN: 以人人都清楚的方式。它宣称确定，而 apparently 常给怀疑留有余地。

entries.definition: as the evidence shows. It is close to the 'clearly' sense of apparently but sounds more formal and more confident.
entries.definitionCN: 正如证据所显示的。它接近 apparently 的“显然”义，但更正式、更有把握。

entries.definition: as it seems, often suggesting that the appearance may mislead. It overlaps with apparently's 'to all appearances' sense.
entries.definitionCN: 看来如此，常暗示表象可能误导。它与 apparently 的“就外表看来”义重叠。

normalIntro.en: Normal associations use the real word parts and the real historical layers, not invented rhymes.
normalIntro.cn: 正常联想使用真实的构词成分和真实的历史层次，不用编造的顺口溜。

normal.en: apparently = apparent + -ly. It is built on the adjective, not on the verb appear.
normal.cn: apparently ＝ apparent + -ly。它建在形容词上，而不是建在动词 appear 上。

normal.en: The -ly suffix comes from Old English -lice; it is the ordinary way English turns an adjective into an adverb.
normal.cn: 后缀 -ly 来自古英语 -lice，是英语把形容词变副词的常规方式。

normal.en: The core is Latin apparere 'come in sight' (ad- + parere), the same root as apparition and transparent.
normal.cn: 核心是拉丁语 apparere“进入视野”（ad- + parere），与 apparition、transparent 同根。

normal.en: The three historical layers are: visibly (late 14c.), evidently (1550s), seemingly (1560s).
normal.cn: 三个历史层次依次是：看得见（14 世纪晚期）、显然（16 世纪 50 年代）、表面上看来（16 世纪 60 年代）。

normal.en: Apparently healthy means 'healthy on the surface'; the adverb is limiting the adjective, not the verb.
normal.cn: apparently healthy 意为“表面上健康”；副词限定的是形容词，不是动词。

abstract.en: Picture a very clean pane of glass: you see everything behind it and forget the glass itself. That is appearance hiding behind its own clarity.
abstract.cn: 想象一块擦得极干净的玻璃：你看清后面的一切，却忘了玻璃本身。这就是“表象”藏在自己的透明之后。

abstract.en: Move the same pane from a window to a mask: what is seen is now deliberately arranged, and 'apparently' becomes 'seemingly'.
abstract.cn: 把同一块玻璃从窗户移到面具上：看到的东西现在是被安排过的，apparently 也就变成了“表面上看来”。

abstract.en: The word never leaves the eye; it only changes how much the eye is trusted — fully, partly, or ironically not at all.
abstract.cn: 这个词始终没有离开眼睛；它改变的只是对眼睛的信任程度——全信、半信，或反讽地一概不信。

examples.en: Apparently, the train was cancelled because of the storm.
examples.cn: 据说火车因暴风雨停运了。

examples.en: The rock looks apparently solid until the first hammer blow.
examples.cn: 那块岩石看上去很坚固，直到第一锤落下。

examples.en: She was apparently calm, but her hands were shaking.
examples.cn: 她表面上很平静，双手却在发抖。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「额，怕人推理」——额，怕人一推理就露馅，只好嘴上说“看来如此” → apparently 看来、据说

root: apparent + -ly；apparent 来自古法语 aparant、拉丁语 apparens（apparere“出现、进入视野”的现在分词）＝ad-“向”+ parere“进入视野”；-ly 出自古英语 -lice。核心是“看得见”，再转为“明显”，最后转为“表面上看来”。

sensesIntro.en: Eight senses of apparently all stay close to the eye: something is visible, then evident, then merely apparent, then reported, then doubted. The word changes its trust in appearances rather than its root.
sensesIntro.cn: apparently 的八个义项都贴近眼睛：先看得见，再显然，再只是表面如此，再转为据说，最后转为怀疑。这个词改变的是对表象的信任度，而不是词根。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a surface that can be seen, with the question of whether it shows the truth.
core.cn: 核心意象：一个看得见的表面，以及它是否显示真相的问题。

branches.en: SIGHT AND CERTAINTY: what is visible is first taken as clearly true.
branches.cn: 看见与确定：看得见的东西起初被当作明白为真。

branches.en: SURFACE ONLY: appearance can be a mask, and apparently healthy is health on the surface.
branches.cn: 仅及表面：外表可以是面具，apparently healthy 就是表面上的健康。

branches.en: EVIDENTIAL LIMIT: the word caps a claim at what the evidence allows.
branches.cn: 证据限度：这个词把断言封顶在证据允许的范围。

branches.en: HEARSAY: the appearance is now in talk rather than in sight.
branches.cn: 传闻：表象现在出现在言谈里，而不是视野里。

branches.en: IRONY: the hedge is quoted back with scepticism.
branches.cn: 反讽：把这层限定语带怀疑地引用回去。

intro.en: Apparently is apparent + -ly. The -ly adverb suffix descends from Old English -lice; the adjective apparent is a Latin present participle ending in -ent, which English borrowed through French.
intro.cn: apparently 是 apparent + -ly。副词后缀 -ly 源自中古英语，可追至古英语 -lice；形容词 apparent 则是以 -ent 结尾的拉丁语现在分词，经法语借入英语。

latinIntro.en: The Latin verb is apparere 'come in sight', from ad- 'to' + parere 'come in sight'. The participle apparens supplies apparent-; the same parere also appears in transparent and apparition.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁动词是 apparere“进入视野”，由 ad-“向”+ parere“进入视野”构成。分词 apparens 提供 apparent-；同一个 parere 也出现在 transparent 与 apparition 中。

items.meaning: visibly; evidently; as it seems
items.meaningCN: 看得见地；显然；看来（-ly 构成副词）
items.example: Apparently, no one had checked the locks.
items.exampleCN: 看来没有人检查过门锁。

items.meaning: clearly visible or clearly understood; seeming
items.meaningCN: 明显可见或清楚易懂的；表面上的（-ent 构成分词形容词）
items.example: The cause of the fire was apparent to everyone.
items.exampleCN: 火灾原因人人都看得出来。

items.meaning: the act of appearing, or the way something looks
items.meaningCN: 出现；外观（-ance 构成动作／状态名词）
items.example: The building's appearance has changed little since 1900.
items.exampleCN: 这座建筑的外观自 1900 年以来变化很小。

items.meaning: to come into view; to seem
items.meaningCN: 出现；显得（字面“进入视野”）
items.example: A light appeared at the end of the tunnel.
items.exampleCN: 隧道尽头出现了一点光。

items.meaning: to come into view again
items.meaningCN: 重新出现（re- 表“再次”）
items.example: The heron reappeared above the reeds.
items.exampleCN: 那只苍鹭又在芦苇上方出现了。

items.meaning: a sudden or ghostly appearance
items.meaningCN: 突然显现；幽灵（-ition 构成动作／结果名词）
items.example: The apparition vanished when the lamp was lit.
items.exampleCN: 灯一亮，那个幽灵般的影子就消失了。

items.meaning: clear enough to see through
items.meaningCN: 透明的；可看穿的（trans-“穿过”+ par-“显现”）
items.example: The water was transparent down to the stones.
items.exampleCN: 水清澈得能看见底下的石头。

items.meaning: the quality of being apparent
items.meaningCN: 明显；显而易见（-ness 构成性质名词）
items.example: The apparentness of the error made the delay hard to explain.
items.exampleCN: 错误如此明显，延误就很难解释。

items.meaning: to go out of sight
items.meaningCN: 消失；不见（dis- 表“离开”+ appear“出现”）
items.example: The boat disappeared behind the headland.
items.exampleCN: 那条船消失在岬角后面。

items.meaning: the act or fact of going out of sight
items.meaningCN: 消失；失踪（-ance 构成状态／结果名词）
items.example: The disappearance of the bees worried the farmers.
items.exampleCN: 蜜蜂的消失让农民忧心。

latinEntries.meaning: to come in sight, be visible

definition_zh: 可应用性；适用性；相关性；实用性；适用范围；可迁移性；普遍适用性
definition_en: the quality of being able to be applied, or of being relevant and suitable to a particular case
core_image: 一块贴纸反复换墙：每换一面墙，都要看它能不能贴上、贴得正不正
scene: The engineer tests the applicability of a single repair patch on wood, steel and wet concrete before ordering a thousand.
sceneCN: 这里 applicability 是「可应用性、适用性」（第 1 个义项：能被施用）；句意：工程师先在一块木、一块钢和一块湿混凝土上测试同一种修补贴片是否适用，然后才订购一千片。图中可辨识物件：三种材质的样板、修补贴片、刮刀、记录板、放大镜。

pos.zh: 可应用性；适用性；相关性；实用性

derivatives.zh: 适用的；可应用的；相关的
应用；申请；涂抹；应用程序
应用的；施用的（多用于语法学）

senses.title: Capability of being applied: it can be put on or put to work
senses.titleCN: 可施用性：贴得上去，也用得上
senses.definition: the quality of being capable of being applied, whether physically or in practice
senses.definitionCN: 能够被施用——无论是物理上贴上去，还是实践中用起来——的性质
senses.example: The applicability of the new coating depends on the surface being dry.
senses.exampleCN: 这种新涂料是否适用，取决于表面是否干燥。
senses.why: The word is recorded in the 1650s as 'capability of being used'. It is applicable + -ity, and applicable goes back to Latin applicare 'attach to'. The first question is simply whether the thing can be attached or put to use at all.
senses.whyCN: 这个词在 17 世纪 50 年代记录为“可被使用的性质”。它是 applicable + -ity，而 applicable 追溯到拉丁语 applicare“贴附到”。最初的问题就是：这东西到底能不能贴上去、用起来。

senses.title: Relevance: it bears on this particular case
senses.titleCN: 相关性：与眼下这个案子有关
senses.definition: the quality of being relevant or pertinent to the case or question at hand
senses.definitionCN: 与当前案件或问题相关、切题的性质
senses.example: The court questioned the applicability of a 1920 ruling to a digital contract.
senses.exampleCN: 法院质疑一项 1920 年的判例是否适用于一份数字合同。
senses.why: Once the thing is attachable, the next question is whether it attaches here. The 'fold onto' image of plicare becomes 'fit this case': relevance is applicability narrowed to one object.
senses.whyCN: 一旦某物可以贴附，下一个问题就是能不能贴在这里。plicare 的“折上去”意象变成“贴合这个案子”：相关性就是把适用性收窄到一个具体对象。

senses.title: Suitability: it fits the purpose
senses.titleCN: 适合性：与用途相配
senses.definition: the quality of being suitable or fitting for a particular purpose
senses.definitionCN: 适合某一特定用途或目的的性质
senses.example: No one doubted the applicability of the method to small farms; the doubt was about large ones.
senses.exampleCN: 没人怀疑这套方法适合小农场，存疑的是大农场。
senses.why: Fit is the positive side of applicability: not merely 'can be attached' but 'attaches well'. The Latin stem applic- already implies bringing one thing into contact with another, so suitability is contact that works.
senses.whyCN: “合适”是适用性的正面：不只是“能贴上”，而是“贴得合”。拉丁词干 applic- 本就意味着把一物与另一物接触，因此适合性就是“接触得成功”。

senses.title: Legal applicability: a rule governs these facts
senses.titleCN: 法律适用性：规则能否管辖这些事实
senses.definition: in law, the quality of a statute, rule, or precedent being capable of governing a given set of facts
senses.definitionCN: 在法律上，某成文法、规则或判例能否管辖特定事实的性质
senses.example: The dispute turned on the applicability of the consumer protection act to second-hand sales.
senses.exampleCN: 争议的关键在于消费者保护法是否适用于二手交易。
senses.why: Law is the domain where applicability is argued most sharply: a rule is a template, and the case must be folded onto it. If the facts do not fit the template, the rule does not apply.
senses.whyCN: 法律是“适用性”被争论得最尖锐的领域：规则是一块模板，案件必须被折贴上去。事实若不合模板，规则就不适用。

senses.title: Mathematical applicability: a theorem has a valid domain
senses.titleCN: 数学适用性：定理有它的有效范围
senses.definition: the quality of a theorem, formula, or method being valid within a stated domain
senses.definitionCN: 定理、公式或方法在所述定义域内有效的性质
senses.example: The applicability of the formula stops at the speed of light.
senses.exampleCN: 这个公式的适用范围到光速为止。
senses.why: A formula is applied to a domain the way a stencil is applied to a surface. Applicability names the boundary of that domain; outside it, the application produces nonsense.
senses.whyCN: 公式被施用于一个定义域，就像模板被贴到一个表面。适用性命名的是这个定义域的边界；越界施用，只会得出荒谬结果。

senses.title: Practical usefulness: it works outside the seminar room
senses.titleCN: 实用性：出了研讨室还用得上
senses.definition: the quality of being useful in real situations rather than only in theory
senses.definitionCN: 在真实情境中有用、而非仅停留在理论上的性质
senses.example: The model's applicability was proved in the field, not in the journal.
senses.exampleCN: 这个模型的实用性是在现场、而不是在期刊里得到证明的。
senses.why: Here the 'put to' of applicare is taken literally: a method is put to work. Practical applicability measures whether the fold holds under real pressure, not just on paper.
senses.whyCN: 这里把 applicare 的“施于”按字面理解：方法被放到工作里去。实用性衡量的是这一“折贴”在真实压力下是否还牢，而不只是在纸上。

senses.title: Scope: how far the application reaches
senses.titleCN: 适用范围：能覆盖到多远
senses.definition: the range or extent over which something can be applied
senses.definitionCN: 某事物能够被施用的范围或广度
senses.example: The applicability of the ban is limited to the city centre.
senses.exampleCN: 这项禁令的适用范围仅限于市中心。
senses.why: The noun can shift from the quality to its measure. If applicability is 'can be folded on', its scope is the set of surfaces on which the fold succeeds.
senses.whyCN: 这个名词可以从“性质”转向“度量”。如果适用性是“能折贴上去”，那么适用范围就是所有能折贴成功的表面之集合。

senses.title: Transferability: skills that travel
senses.titleCN: 可迁移性：本事换个地方也能用
senses.definition: the quality of a skill or body of knowledge being usable in a new setting
senses.definitionCN: 技能或知识体系能在新环境中继续使用的性质
senses.example: Employers now ask about the applicability of a degree to jobs outside its field.
senses.exampleCN: 雇主现在会问，一个学位在专业之外的岗位上是否也能用。
senses.why: A skill is applied to a new task as a tool is applied to new material. Transferability is applicability across contexts, with the emphasis on the move rather than on the fit.
senses.whyCN: 技能被施用于新任务，就像工具被施于新材料。可迁移性就是跨情境的适用性，重点在“迁移”而不在“贴合”。

senses.title: General applicability: the rule holds for all
senses.titleCN: 普遍适用性：对所有人都成立
senses.definition: the quality of a principle or rule applying to every relevant case, not merely some
senses.definitionCN: 某项原则或规则适用于所有相关情形、而非仅部分情形的性质
senses.example: The appeal was to the general applicability of the principle, not to local custom.
senses.exampleCN: 所诉诸的是该原则的普遍适用性，而不是地方习俗。
senses.why: If a stencil fits every surface of the same shape, its applicability is general. The suffix -ity turns the adjective into the name of a property that can be measured from one case to all.
senses.whyCN: 如果一块模板能贴合所有同形状的表面，它的适用性就是普遍的。-ity 把这个形容词变成一种可以从个案推广到全体的性质之名。

intro.en: Applicability is a double suffixation: Latin applicare 'attach' gives applicable through -able, and applicable then takes -ity. The obsolete appliableness once competed with it. Dates are approximate.
intro.cn: applicability 是双重后缀化的结果：拉丁语 applicare“贴附”经 -able 得出 applicable，applicable 再加 -ity。已废弃的 appliableness 曾与它竞争。年代为大致估计。

items.en: Applicability is recorded, meaning 'capability of being used'. It is formed from applicable plus -ity, from Latin -itatem, a suffix naming a quality or state.
items.cn: applicability 见于记载，意为“可被使用的性质”。它由 applicable 加 -ity 构成；-ity 出自拉丁语 -itatem，表示性质或状态。

items.en: An earlier noun appliableness is recorded, with the same sense. It is now obsolete; applicability won the place.
items.cn: 更早的名词 appliableness 已有记载，意思相同。它如今已废弃，位置由 applicability 取代。

items.en: Applicable is recorded in the 1650s as 'capable of being applied, suitable'. An earlier appliable dates from the mid-15c., and applicable itself is recorded in the 1560s with the different sense 'pliable, well-disposed'.
items.cn: applicable 于 17 世纪 50 年代记录为“可施用的、合适的”。更早的 appliable 可追溯至 15 世纪中期，而 applicable 本身在 16 世纪 60 年代另有“柔顺的、易于影响的”一义。

items.en: The verb apply is recorded meaning 'join or combine (with); attach, adhere'. The physical sense of pressing one thing to another comes first.
items.cn: 动词 apply 见于记载，意为“与……结合；贴附、黏着”。把一物压到另一物上的物理义最先出现。

items.en: Apply comes from Old French aploiier, from Latin applicare 'attach to, join, connect', built from ad- 'to' + plicare 'fold'.
items.cn: apply 来自古法语 aploiier，源自拉丁语 applicare“贴附、连接、结合”，由 ad-“向”+ plicare“折叠”构成。

items.en: plicare goes back to PIE *plek- 'to plait, weave'. The chain is fold → attach → put to use: something folded onto something else is joined to it, and what is joined can be put into service.
items.cn: plicare 可追溯至原始印欧语 *plek-“编织、折叠”。链条是：折叠 → 贴附 → 投入使用；一物折贴到另一物上便与之结合，而结合之物就能被派上用场。

note.en: The first group separates forms built on the same applic- stem from look-alikes; the second group compares nouns of related meaning.
note.cn: 第一组区分同一 applic- 词干构成的形式与撞形词；第二组比较意思相关的名词。

entries.definition: the adjective from which applicability is formed: 'capable of being applied'. The noun simply adds -ity.
entries.definitionCN: 构成 applicability 的形容词：“可施用的”。名词只是在它后面加 -ity。

entries.definition: the act of applying or a formal request. It shares applicare but uses -ation, an action/result suffix, where applicability uses -ity, a quality suffix.
entries.definitionCN: 施用行为或正式申请。它同出 applicare，但用 -ation（动作／结果后缀），而 applicability 用 -ity（性质后缀）。

entries.definition: a machine for a household task. It comes from the same apply family, but names the thing to which power or a task is applied, not a quality.
entries.definitionCN: 家用器具。它同出 apply 词族，但命名的是“被施加动力或任务的东西”，不是一种性质。

entries.definition: the quality of being connected to the matter at hand. It stresses connection, while applicability stresses whether something can be used or enforced.
entries.definitionCN: 与当前事情相关的性质。它强调关联，而 applicability 强调能否被使用或执行。

entries.definition: the quality of being right for a purpose. It is close to applicability but sounds more about fit and less about formal application.
entries.definitionCN: 适合某用途的性质。它接近 applicability，但更侧重“合身”，较少指正式施用。

entries.definition: the range a rule or activity covers. It names the boundary, while applicability names the capacity to apply within it.
entries.definitionCN: 规则或活动覆盖的范围。它命名边界，而 applicability 命名在边界内施用的能力。

normalIntro.en: Normal associations follow the real suffixes and the real root plicare, not invented rhymes.
normalIntro.cn: 正常联想沿着真实后缀和真实词根 plicare 展开，不用编造的顺口溜。

normal.en: applicability = applicable + -ity. The -ity (Latin -itatem) turns 'able to be applied' into 'the quality of being applicable'.
normal.cn: applicability ＝ applicable + -ity。-ity（拉丁 -itatem）把“能被施用”变成“可施用这一性质”。

normal.en: applicable = applic- (Latin stem of apply) + -able. The -able suffix says 'can be', so the base meaning is 'can be attached or put to'.
normal.cn: applicable ＝ applic-（apply 的拉丁词干）+ -able。-able 表示“能够被……”，所以底层意思是“能被贴附或施用”。

normal.en: plicare means 'fold'. To apply something is to fold it onto something else — a patch onto a wall, a rule onto a case.
normal.cn: plicare 意为“折叠”。把某物 apply 上去，就是把它折贴到另一物上——贴片贴墙，规则贴案情。

normal.en: The obsolete rival was appliableness (1580s); applicability (1650s) displaced it.
normal.cn: 已被淘汰的竞争者是 16 世纪 80 年代的 appliableness；17 世纪 50 年代的 applicability 取代了它。

normal.en: Application and applicant are siblings, not synonyms: -ation names the act or request, -ant names the person.
normal.cn: application 和 applicant 是同胞而非同义词：-ation 命名动作或请求，-ant 命名人。

abstract.en: Picture a single patch tested on three surfaces: the question is not what the patch is, but where it will hold.
abstract.cn: 想象同一块贴片被拿到三种表面上测试：问题不在于贴片是什么，而在于它在哪些地方贴得住。

abstract.en: Every use of the word is a fold: a method folded onto a farm, a rule folded onto a case, a formula folded onto a domain.
abstract.cn: 这个词的每次使用都是一次折叠：方法折到农场、规则折到案情、公式折到定义域。

abstract.en: The suffix -ity freezes the fold into a measurable property: you can have more or less of it, and you can set its boundary.
abstract.cn: 后缀 -ity 把这次折叠冻成一种可度量的性质：它可以有多有少，也可以划定边界。

examples.en: The committee reviewed the applicability of the old rule to online sales.
examples.cn: 委员会审议了旧规则是否适用于线上销售。

examples.en: Doubts about the applicability of the theory grew as new data came in.
examples.cn: 随着新数据出现，人们对这套理论是否适用的怀疑加深了。

examples.en: The grant requires applicants to explain the practical applicability of their research.
examples.cn: 这项资助要求申请人说明其研究的实际应用价值。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「阿普立刻比了比」——阿普立刻拿尺子比了比桌面，看这块板到底能不能用 → applicability 适用性、可应用性

root: applicable + -ity；applicable 由 apply 的拉丁词干 applic- 加 -able 构成，applicare＝ad-“向”+ plicare“折叠”（PIE *plek-“编织”）。核心链条是“折上去 → 贴附 → 投入使用”，-ity 再把此能力名词化为“适用性”。

sensesIntro.en: Nine senses of applicability all ask one question: will this fold hold here? The surface changes from a wall to a case, a formula's domain, a farm, a new job, or the whole world.
sensesIntro.cn: applicability 的九个义项都在问同一个问题：这次“折贴”在这里贴得住吗？表面则从墙面换到案情、公式定义域、农场、新岗位，乃至全世界。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a patch is folded onto a surface and must hold there.
core.cn: 核心意象：一块贴片被折贴到某个表面上，并且必须在那里贴住。

branches.en: CAN IT BE USED: the basic capability and the positive fit of a method to a purpose.
branches.cn: 能不能用：最基本的能力，以及方法与用途的正面契合。

branches.en: DOES IT BEAR ON THIS CASE: relevance in argument and applicability in law.
branches.cn: 是否切合本案：论证中的相关性，以及法律中的可适用性。

branches.en: DOES IT HOLD IN THIS DOMAIN: a formula or theorem has a valid range.
branches.cn: 在此定义域是否成立：公式或定理有其有效范围。

branches.en: DOES IT WORK OUTSIDE THE PAGE: practical use and skills that transfer.
branches.cn: 出了纸面是否管用：实际用途，以及能迁移的技能。

branches.en: HOW FAR DOES IT REACH: the scope of a ban and the generality of a principle.
branches.cn: 能伸到多远：禁令的适用范围与原则的普遍性。

intro.en: Applicability carries two suffixes: -able (Latin -abilis, 'capable of being') makes the adjective applicable, and -ity (Latin -itatem, 'quality or state') makes the noun. The base is the Latin stem applic- of applicare.
intro.cn: applicability 带两个后缀：-able（拉丁 -abilis，“能够被……”）先构成形容词 applicable，-ity（拉丁 -itatem，“性质或状态”）再构成名词。词基是 applicare 的拉丁词干 applic-。

latinIntro.en: Latin applicare 'attach to' joins ad- 'to' and plicare 'fold'. The same plicare supplies apply, application, applicant, appliance, explicit, complicate and multiply, all through the image of folding or plaiting.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语 applicare“贴附到”由 ad-“向”和 plicare“折叠”构成。同一个 plicare 还提供 apply、application、applicant、appliance、explicit、complicate、multiply，全部经由“折叠／编织”的意象。

items.meaning: the quality of being capable of being applied
items.meaningCN: 可应用性；适用性（-able 表“能被”，-ity 表性质）
items.example: The applicability of the rule is still debated.
items.exampleCN: 这条规则是否适用仍有争议。

items.meaning: capable of being applied; relevant
items.meaningCN: 可应用的；适用的（-able 构成形容词）
items.example: The discount is applicable only to members.
items.exampleCN: 折扣仅适用于会员。

items.meaning: to put one thing onto another; to put to use; to make a request
items.meaningCN: 贴附；应用；申请（字面“折向”）
items.example: Apply the cream twice a day.
items.exampleCN: 每天涂两次药膏。

items.meaning: the act of applying, or a formal request
items.meaningCN: 应用；申请（-ation 构成动作／结果名词）
items.example: The application of heat softened the metal.
items.exampleCN: 加热使金属变软。

items.meaning: a person who applies for something
items.meaningCN: 申请人（-ant 表示正在做该动作的人）
items.example: Only three applicants met the deadline.
items.exampleCN: 只有三名申请人在截止前提交。

items.meaning: relating to application; in grammar, a construction that promotes an oblique object
items.meaningCN: 应用的；施用的；（语法） applicative 结构的
items.example: The applicative suffix adds a beneficiary to the verb.
items.exampleCN: applicative 后缀给动词增加一个受益者论元。

items.meaning: a device used for a particular household task
items.meaningCN: 器具；家用电器（-ance 构成事物／状态名词）
items.example: The kitchen appliance broke after one year.
items.exampleCN: 那台厨房电器用了一年就坏了。

items.meaning: to fold things together, hence to make difficult
items.meaningCN: 使复杂（字面“折叠在一起”）
items.example: A second contract complicated the deal.
items.exampleCN: 第二份合同让交易变复杂了。

items.meaning: unfolded, hence fully stated and clear
items.meaningCN: 明确的（字面“折展开来”）
items.example: The instructions were explicit about the order of steps.
items.exampleCN: 说明对步骤顺序写得很明确。

items.meaning: to increase many times over
items.meaningCN: 乘；成倍增加（字面“折成许多层”）
items.example: Bacteria multiply rapidly in warm water.
items.exampleCN: 细菌在温水中迅速繁殖。

latinEntries.meaning: a joining to; the act of applying

definition_zh: 可应用的；适用的；相关的；合适的；法律上适用的；（公式等）在定义域内成立的；可抵用的；（古义）顺从的、易于影响的
definition_en: capable of being applied, put to use, or brought to bear on a particular case; also, in older use, pliable
core_image: 一张标签正对着一只瓶口：尺寸刚好，贴上去不歪
scene: The label is applicable to both the small and the large jar, but not to the square tin.
sceneCN: 这里 applicable 是「可贴用的、适用的」（第 1 个义项：能被贴上使用）；句意：这种标签适用于小罐和大罐，却不适用于方形铁盒。图中可辨识物件：两种圆形罐子、方形铁盒、标签纸、尺子、贴好的样签。

pos.zh: 可应用的；适用的；相关的；（古义）柔顺的

collocations.zh: 在适用的情况下；如适用

forms.label: 比较级（更多用 more 构成）
最高级（更多用 most 构成）

senses.title: Capable of being put on: the patch fits the surface
senses.titleCN: 贴得上：贴片与表面相合
senses.definition: capable of being physically applied, as a coating, patch, or label
senses.definitionCN: 能够在物理上被涂上、贴上，如涂料、贴片或标签
senses.example: The sealant is applicable to metal roofs but not to rubber ones.
senses.exampleCN: 这种密封胶适用于金属屋顶，不适用于橡胶屋顶。
senses.why: Applicable is recorded in the 1650s as 'capable of being applied, suitable'. It is the Latin stem applic- plus -able, and applicare means 'attach to'. The first image is literal contact: one thing laid on another.
senses.whyCN: applicable 于 17 世纪 50 年代记录为“可施用的、合适的”。它是拉丁词干 applic- 加 -able，而 applicare 意为“贴附到”。最初的意象就是字面接触：一物铺在另一物上。

senses.title: Capable of being used: the method can be put to work
senses.titleCN: 用得上：方法能被投入使用
senses.definition: capable of being put into practice or used for a purpose
senses.definitionCN: 能够被付诸实践、或用于某一目的
senses.example: The same sampling method is applicable to soil, water and air.
senses.exampleCN: 同一套采样方法可用于土壤、水和空气。
senses.why: The physical 'laid on' extends to 'put to': a tool or method is applied to a task just as a patch is applied to a wall. The suffix -able marks the possibility, not the act.
senses.whyCN: 物理上的“铺上去”延伸到“施于”：工具或方法被用到任务上，就像贴片被贴到墙上。-able 标记的是可能性，而不是动作本身。

senses.title: Relevant: the remark bears on the case
senses.titleCN: 切题：这句话与本案有关
senses.definition: relevant or pertinent to the matter under discussion
senses.definitionCN: 与所讨论的事情相关或切题
senses.example: His objection is applicable to the second proposal, not the first.
senses.exampleCN: 他的反对意见适用于第二个方案，而不是第一个。
senses.why: A rule or remark is 'laid onto' a case as a stencil is laid onto paper. If the outline matches, it is applicable; if not, the remark is beside the point.
senses.whyCN: 规则或评论被“铺到”案件上，就像模板铺到纸上。轮廓对得上，就是 applicable；对不上，这句话就文不对题。

senses.title: Legally applicable: the statute governs these facts
senses.titleCN: 法律上适用：制定法管辖这些事实
senses.definition: of a law, rule, or precedent: capable of governing a given case
senses.definitionCN: 指法律、规则或判例能够管辖某一具体案件
senses.example: The 1998 statute is applicable only to contracts signed after that date.
senses.exampleCN: 1998 年的制定法只适用于该日期之后签订的合同。
senses.why: In law the stencil metaphor becomes strict: a statute is applicable if the facts fall within its terms. The question is not whether the rule is good, but whether it covers this case.
senses.whyCN: 在法律中，模板隐喻变得严格：事实落入法条范围，制定法才算 applicable。问题不是规则好不好，而是它是否覆盖本案。

senses.title: Valid in a domain: the formula holds here
senses.titleCN: 定义域内成立：公式在这里有效
senses.definition: of a formula, theorem, or method: valid within a stated range or set of conditions
senses.definitionCN: 指公式、定理或方法在所述范围或条件内有效
senses.example: Newton's law is applicable at everyday speeds but not near the speed of light.
senses.exampleCN: 牛顿定律适用于日常速度，不适用于接近光速的情形。
senses.why: A formula is applied to a domain as a template is applied to a surface. Applicable here means the application yields valid results inside that boundary.
senses.whyCN: 公式被施用于一个定义域，正如模板被贴到一个表面。这里的 applicable 意味着：在该边界内，施用能得出有效结果。

senses.title: Suitable: it is the right tool for the job
senses.titleCN: 合适：正是这件活儿该用的
senses.definition: suitable or fitting for a particular purpose or person
senses.definitionCN: 适合某一特定目的或人选
senses.example: A calm, factual tone proved applicable to the sensitive announcement.
senses.exampleCN: 平静而就事的语气证明适合这则敏感通告。
senses.why: The sense of 'suitable' was already present in the 1650s definition. If a thing can be applied and the result works well, it is not merely possible but fitting.
senses.whyCN: “合适”义已包含在 17 世纪 50 年代的释义里。若某物能被施用且效果良好，它就不只是“可以”，而是“合宜”。

senses.title: Applicable to a person or group: the rule reaches them
senses.titleCN: 适用于某人或某群体：规则覆盖到他们
senses.definition: of a rule, condition, or price: binding on or available to a particular person or group
senses.definitionCN: 指规则、条件或价格对特定人或群体有约束力或可供其使用
senses.example: The student discount is applicable to anyone with a valid card.
senses.exampleCN: 学生折扣适用于任何持有效证件的人。
senses.why: Here the surface being covered is a person or group. The rule is laid over a set of people; whoever falls under the outline is covered.
senses.whyCN: 这里被覆盖的表面是一人或一群人。规则被铺在一组人之上；落入轮廓之内的人就被覆盖。

senses.title: Archaic pliable: easily bent or influenced
senses.titleCN: 古义“柔顺”：容易弯曲或受影响
senses.definition: in 16c. use, pliable or well-disposed; now archaic
senses.definitionCN: 16 世纪用法，指柔顺的、易于影响的；今已古旧
senses.example: In the 1560s an applicable mind meant one ready to be shaped by advice.
senses.exampleCN: 在 16 世纪 60 年代，an applicable mind 指容易接受建议塑造的心智。
senses.why: The 1560s sense 'pliable, well-disposed' treats a person as a surface that can be folded or shaped. It survives as an archaic curiosity, while the modern word keeps the same applicare image but applies it to rules and tools.
senses.whyCN: 16 世纪 60 年代的“柔顺、易于影响”义，把人当作一个可以被折叠、被塑造的表面。它作为古旧用法留存下来；现代词保留同一个 applicare 意象，只是把施用对象换成了规则与工具。

senses.title: Applicable to a balance: credit that can be set against a debt
senses.titleCN: 可抵用：款项能冲抵欠款
senses.definition: of a payment or credit: able to be applied to a debt or account
senses.definitionCN: 指付款或信用额度能够用来冲抵债务或记入账户
senses.example: The deposit is applicable to the final invoice.
senses.exampleCN: 这笔定金可用于冲抵最终发票。
senses.why: In accounting, an amount is 'applied' to an account: it is laid against the balance to reduce it. This is a technical extension of the same 'put onto' image.
senses.whyCN: 在会计中，一笔款项被“施于”某个账户：它被铺到余额上，以冲减余额。这是同一个“铺上去”意象的技术延伸。

intro.en: Applicable is apply's Latin stem applic- plus -able (Latin -abilis, 'capable of being'). An earlier appliable existed, and applicable briefly meant 'pliable'. Dates are approximate.
intro.cn: applicable 是 apply 的拉丁词干 applic- 加 -able（拉丁 -abilis，“能够被……”）。更早存在 appliable，而 applicable 一度表“柔顺的”。年代为大致估计。

items.en: Applicable is recorded in its modern sense 'capable of being applied, suitable'. It is formed from the Latin stem applic- of applicare plus -able.
items.cn: applicable 以现代义“可施用的、合适的”见于记载。它由 applicare 的拉丁词干 applic- 加 -able 构成。

items.en: An earlier use of applicable means 'pliable, well-disposed'. The modern sense of a rule or tool being applicable is later.
items.cn: applicable 更早的用法意为“柔顺的、易于影响的”。规则或工具“可适用”的现代义出现得更晚。

items.en: The form appliable is recorded, built on the English verb apply plus -able. It preceded applicable and is now obsolete.
items.cn: appliable 这一形式见于记载，由英语动词 apply 加 -able 构成。它早于 applicable，如今已废弃。

items.en: The verb apply means 'join or combine (with); attach, adhere'. Physical attachment is the earliest English sense.
items.cn: 动词 apply 意为“与……结合；贴附、黏着”。物理上的贴附是最早的英语义。

items.en: Apply comes from Old French aploiier, from Latin applicare 'attach to, join, connect', from ad- 'to' + plicare 'fold'.
items.cn: apply 来自古法语 aploiier，源自拉丁语 applicare“贴附、连接、结合”，由 ad-“向”+ plicare“折叠”构成。

items.en: plicare goes back to PIE *plek- 'to plait'. The chain fold → attach → put to use explains the modern spread. Note that applicate (1530s) is a rare variant, not a separate modern word to confuse with applicable.
items.cn: plicare 可追溯至原始印欧语 *plek-“编织”。链条“折叠 → 贴附 → 投入使用”解释了现代义的扩展。注意 applicate（16 世纪 30 年代）是罕见异体，不是可与 applicable 混淆的另一个现代词。

note.en: The first group separates members of the same applic- family from a rare variant; the second group compares adjectives of related meaning.
note.cn: 第一组区分同一 applic- 词族的成员与一个罕见异体；第二组比较意思相近的形容词。

entries.definition: a person who applies for something. It shares applicare but uses -ant, a person suffix, not -able.
entries.definitionCN: 申请人。它同出 applicare，但用 -ant（表人后缀），不是 -able。

entries.definition: the act of applying or a formal request. It uses -ation, an action/result suffix, and is not interchangeable with the adjective.
entries.definitionCN: 应用行为或正式申请。它用 -ation（动作／结果后缀），不能与形容词互换。

entries.definition: a 1530s variant meaning 'applied or put to'. It is now rare and should not be treated as a modern synonym of applicable.
entries.definitionCN: 16 世纪 30 年代的异体，意为“被施用或放置的”。今已罕见，不应视为 applicable 的现代同义词。

entries.definition: connected with the matter at hand. It stresses connection, while applicable stresses that something can be used or enforced.
entries.definitionCN: 与当前事情有关。它强调关联，而 applicable 强调能被使用或执行。

entries.definition: right or appropriate for a purpose. It is broader and softer than applicable, which often implies a rule or tool.
entries.definitionCN: 适合某用途的。它比 applicable 更宽、更软，后者常暗含规则或工具。

entries.definition: having legal or logical force. It is close to the legal and mathematical senses of applicable but does not imply physical attachment.
entries.definitionCN: 具有法律或逻辑效力的。它接近 applicable 的法律与数学义，但不含物理贴附之意。

normalIntro.en: Normal associations follow the real suffixes and the real root plicare, not invented rhymes.
normalIntro.cn: 正常联想沿着真实后缀和真实词根 plicare 展开，不用编造的顺口溜。

normal.en: applicable = applic- (Latin stem of apply) + -able ('capable of being'). The suffix asks a yes/no question: can it be applied?
normal.cn: applicable ＝ applic-（apply 的拉丁词干）+ -able（“能够被……”）。后缀问的是一个是非题：能被施用吗？

normal.en: plicare 'fold' is the root: applicable things can be folded onto something else and made to fit.
normal.cn: 词根 plicare“折叠”：可适用的东西能折贴到另一物上并与之相合。

normal.en: The family splits by suffix: -able (applicable), -ation (application), -ant (applicant), -ive (applicative), -or (applicator).
normal.cn: 这个词族按后缀分工：-able（applicable）、-ation（application）、-ant（applicant）、-ive（applicative）、-or（applicator）。

normal.en: appliable was the mid-15c. English-formed rival; applicable came later from the Latin stem.
normal.cn: appliable 是 15 世纪中期由英语自身构成的竞争者；applicable 后来才从拉丁词干造出。

normal.en: Where applicable is the standard legal and technical phrase: it means 'in the cases where it applies'.
normal.cn: where applicable 是法律与技术文本的标准短语，意思是“在适用的情况下”。

abstract.en: Picture a stencil held over a page: the word applicable is the moment you check whether the cut-out matches the shape below.
abstract.cn: 想象一块模板悬在纸面上：applicable 就是你检查镂空是否与下方形状相合的那一刻。

abstract.en: The same check is repeated at every scale: a label on a jar, a method on a farm, a law on a case, a formula on a domain.
abstract.cn: 同一次检查在每个尺度上重演：标签对罐子、方法对农场、法律对案件、公式对定义域。

abstract.en: The suffix -able keeps the word on the edge of possibility: it says 'can be', not 'is being'.
abstract.cn: 后缀 -able 把词停在“可能性”的边缘：它说的是“能被”，不是“正在被”。

examples.en: The discount is applicable only to full-time students.
examples.cn: 这项折扣只适用于全日制学生。

examples.en: Is this rule applicable to cases that began before the law passed?
examples.cn: 这条规则适用于法律通过前就已开始的案件吗？

examples.en: The old map is no longer applicable to the rebuilt city.
examples.cn: 那张旧地图已不再适用于重建后的城市。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「阿普利可宝」——阿普利说这块补丁可宝贝了，哪都能贴 → applicable 适用的、可应用的

root: apply 的拉丁词干 applic- + -able（拉丁 -abilis“能够被……”）；applicare＝ad-“向”+ plicare“折叠”（PIE *plek-“编织”）。核心是“能折贴上去、能投入使用”，并由“贴附”扩展到“切题、有效、合适”。

sensesIntro.en: Nine senses of applicable all test the same fit: can this be laid onto that? The 'that' runs from a jar to a method, a case, a statute, a domain, a person, and finally an account.
sensesIntro.cn: applicable 的九个义项都在检验同一种贴合：这个能不能铺到那个上？那个对象从罐子一路换到方法、案件、法条、定义域、人，最后到账户。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a label is laid onto a surface and must match its shape.
core.cn: 核心意象：一张标签铺到某个表面上，必须与它的形状相合。

branches.en: PHYSICAL AND PRACTICAL: a coating can be laid on, and a method can be put to work.
branches.cn: 物理与实际：涂料能铺上去，方法能投入使用。

branches.en: REACHING THE CASE OR PERSON: a remark fits the argument, a rule covers a group.
branches.cn: 覆盖案情或人：评论切合论证，规则覆盖某群体。

branches.en: FORMAL FORCE: a statute governs facts, a formula holds inside its domain.
branches.cn: 形式效力：法条管辖事实，公式在定义域内成立。

branches.en: FITNESS: the tool is not only possible but right for the job.
branches.cn: 合宜：不只是可行，而是正合这件活儿。

branches.en: OLDER AND TECHNICAL EDGES: the archaic 'pliable' and the accounting 'applicable to a balance'.
branches.cn: 较旧与技术的边缘：古义“柔顺”，以及会计中“可冲抵余额”。

intro.en: Applicable is applic- + -able. The suffix -able comes from Latin -abilis and marks capability; the stem applic- is the Latin stem of applicare 'attach'. English later adds -ity to make applicability.
intro.cn: applicable 是 applic- + -able。后缀 -able 出自拉丁 -abilis，表示“能够被……”；词干 applic- 是 applicare“贴附”的拉丁词干。英语后来再加 -ity 构成 applicability。

latinIntro.en: ad- 'to' plus plicare 'fold' gives applicare 'attach to'. The same plicare underlies explicit, complicate, multiply, and the simplex ply; all carry the image of folding or plaiting.
latinIntro.cn: ad-“向”加 plicare“折叠”得出 applicare“贴附到”。同一个 plicare 还支撑 explicit、complicate、multiply 以及单纯词 ply；它们都带着“折叠／编织”的意象。

items.meaning: capable of being applied or brought to bear
items.meaningCN: 可应用的；适用的（-able 表“能被”）
items.example: The rule is applicable to all new members.
items.exampleCN: 这条规则适用于所有新成员。

items.meaning: to lay one thing on another; to put to use; to request
items.meaningCN: 贴附；应用；申请（字面“折向”）
items.example: She applied the sealant with a brush.
items.exampleCN: 她用刷子涂上密封胶。

items.meaning: the act of applying, or a formal request
items.meaningCN: 应用；申请（-ation 构成动作／结果名词）
items.example: The application of the rule changed the outcome.
items.exampleCN: 规则的适用改变了结果。

items.meaning: one who applies for something
items.meaningCN: 申请人（-ant 表人）
items.example: Each applicant must sign the form.
items.exampleCN: 每位申请人都必须签署表格。

items.meaning: the quality of being applicable
items.meaningCN: 适用性；可应用性（-ity 构成性质名词）
items.example: No one questioned the applicability of the method.
items.exampleCN: 没有人质疑这套方法的适用性。

items.meaning: relating to application
items.meaningCN: 应用的；施用的（-ive 构成形容词）
items.example: The applicative use of the term is rare.
items.exampleCN: 这个词的应用义用法很少见。

items.meaning: a tool for applying something
items.meaningCN: 涂抹器；施用工具（-or 表施动者或工具）
items.example: Use the applicator to spread the glue evenly.
items.exampleCN: 用涂抹器把胶水涂匀。

items.meaning: unfolded, hence clearly stated
items.meaningCN: 明确的（字面“折展开来”）
items.example: The warning was explicit and could not be missed.
items.exampleCN: 警告很明确，不可能被忽略。

items.meaning: to fold together, hence to make difficult
items.meaningCN: 使复杂（字面“折在一起”）
items.example: New rules complicated the application process.
items.exampleCN: 新规则让申请流程变复杂了。

items.meaning: to increase many times over
items.meaningCN: 乘；成倍增加（字面“折成多层”）
items.example: The errors multiplied after the change.
items.exampleCN: 改动之后错误成倍增加。

latinEntries.meaning: a joining to; the act of applying

definition_zh: 申请人；求职者；应征者；报名者；求学者；签证申请人；贷款申请人；资助申请人；（法律）申请方；专利申请人；投保人
definition_en: a person who applies for something: a job, a place, a grant, a visa, a patent, insurance, or a legal remedy
core_image: 一个人把自己递到桌前：双手奉上表格，身子微微前倾，像把自己贴到那件事上
scene: By nine o'clock the applicant had already attached her form to the last page of the file and was waiting outside the interview room.
sceneCN: 这里 applicant 是「申请人、求职者」（第 1 个义项：申请职位的人）；句意：九点不到，这位申请人已把表格附在档案最后一页，在面试室外等候。图中可辨识物件：档案夹、订书机、申请表、面试室门牌、等候椅、胸牌。

pos.zh: 申请人；求职者；应征者；报名者；申请方

collocations.zh: 申请人群体；候选人才库

senses.title: Job applicant: one who applies for work
senses.titleCN: 求职者：向雇主递上申请的人
senses.definition: a person who formally asks an employer for a job
senses.definitionCN: 正式向雇主请求职位的人
senses.example: Each applicant was asked to solve the same problem in twenty minutes.
senses.exampleCN: 每位求职者都被要求在二十分钟内解决同一个问题。
senses.why: Applicant is recorded in the late 15c. as 'one who applies, candidate'. It comes from Latin applicans, the present participle of applicare 'attach to': the applicant is literally the person attaching himself to the post.
senses.whyCN: applicant 在 15 世纪晚期记录为“申请的人、候选人”。它来自拉丁语 applicans——applicare“贴附到”的现在分词：申请人字面上就是“把自己贴到那个职位上的人”。

senses.title: Admission applicant: one who seeks a place at a school
senses.titleCN: 入学申请人：争取一个学位名额的人
senses.definition: a person who applies for admission to a school, college, or university
senses.definitionCN: 申请进入学校、学院或大学的人
senses.example: The committee reads every applicant's essay before making offers.
senses.exampleCN: 委员会在发出录取通知前会读每位申请人的文章。
senses.why: The thing being attached to is now an institution rather than an employer. The grammar is the same: the person attaches himself to a place he hopes to enter.
senses.whyCN: 被贴附的对象现在是机构，而不是雇主。语法关系不变：人把自己贴到他希望进入的地方。

senses.title: Visa or immigration applicant: one who asks to enter a country
senses.titleCN: 签证或移民申请人：请求入境的人
senses.definition: a person who applies to a government for a visa, residence, or citizenship
senses.definitionCN: 向政府申请签证、居留或公民身份的人
senses.example: The visa applicant had to show bank records for the past six months.
senses.exampleCN: 签证申请人必须出示过去六个月的银行记录。
senses.why: Here the applicant attaches himself to a state's permission. The Latin image survives in the paperwork: forms, photographs, fingerprints, all used to fix one person to one file.
senses.whyCN: 这里申请人把自己贴到国家的许可上。拉丁意象在文书里存活：表格、照片、指纹，都是把一个人固定到一份档案上的手段。

senses.title: Loan or credit applicant: one who asks for money
senses.titleCN: 贷款申请人：请求授信的人
senses.definition: a person who applies to a bank or lender for credit
senses.definitionCN: 向银行或放贷机构申请信贷的人
senses.example: The loan applicant's income was too irregular for the standard product.
senses.exampleCN: 这位贷款申请人的收入对标准产品来说太不稳定。
senses.why: The applicant is attached to a sum of money and to the terms that govern it. The word still names the person, while application names the request.
senses.whyCN: 申请人把自己贴到一笔钱及其条款上。这个词仍命名人，而 application 命名请求本身。

senses.title: Grant or funding applicant: one who asks for support
senses.titleCN: 资助申请人：请求经费支持的人
senses.definition: a person or team who applies for a grant, scholarship, or research funding
senses.definitionCN: 申请资助、奖学金或研究经费的个人或团队
senses.example: Only applicants with preliminary data were invited to the second round.
senses.exampleCN: 只有已有初步数据的申请人才被邀请进入第二轮。
senses.why: The thing applied for is support rather than a post. The present participle still fits: the applicant is the one in the act of attaching a proposal to a funder's programme.
senses.whyCN: 所申请的是支持而非职位。现在分词依然贴切：申请人正把一份提案贴到资助方的项目上。

senses.title: Legal applicant: the party who brings the application
senses.titleCN: 法律申请方：提出申请的一方
senses.definition: in law, the party who makes a formal application or petition to a court or tribunal
senses.definitionCN: 在法律上，向法院或法庭提出正式申请或请求的一方
senses.example: The applicant asked for an injunction; the respondent opposed it.
senses.exampleCN: 申请方请求禁令，被申请方表示反对。
senses.why: In legal usage applicant is a role, not a personality: the side that initiates the application. The Latin participle's '-ant' marks the one doing the act at the moment in question.
senses.whyCN: 在法律用法中，applicant 是一个角色，而非某个人：发起申请的一方。拉丁分词后缀 -ant 标记“在相关时刻正在做该动作的人”。

senses.title: Patent applicant: the person or firm seeking a patent
senses.titleCN: 专利申请人：请求授予专利的人或公司
senses.definition: the person or company that files an application for a patent
senses.definitionCN: 提交专利申请的个人或公司
senses.example: The patent applicant was a small firm, not the multinational named in the press.
senses.exampleCN: 专利申请人是一家小公司，并非报道中提到的跨国公司。
senses.why: An invention is attached to a legal claim, and the applicant is the one who makes that attachment. The technical register keeps the original 'attach oneself' force.
senses.whyCN: 发明被贴到一项法律主张上，申请人就是完成这次贴附的人。技术性语域保留了原初“把自己贴上去”的力度。

senses.title: Insurance applicant: the person proposing a policy
senses.titleCN: 投保申请人：提出保单的人
senses.definition: a person who applies to an insurer for a policy, distinct from the insured once the policy is issued
senses.definitionCN: 向保险人申请保单的人；保单签发后与“被保险人”可相区别
senses.example: The insurer may decline an applicant whose risk falls outside its rules.
senses.exampleCN: 保险人可以拒绝风险超出其规则的投保申请人。
senses.why: At the moment of applying, the person is attached to a proposed contract, not yet to a completed one. English keeps applicant for that pre-contract stage, which is why it is not simply 'the insured'.
senses.whyCN: 在申请的那一刻，此人贴到的是一份拟议合同，而非已完成的合同。英语用 applicant 指这个“缔约前”阶段，因此它并不等同于 the insured。

senses.title: General candidate: one who puts himself forward
senses.titleCN: 泛指的应征者：把自己递出去的人
senses.definition: broadly, a candidate or person who offers himself for a position, honour, or selection
senses.definitionCN: 广义上，为职位、荣誉或遴选而自荐或报名的人
senses.example: Every applicant for the prize must submit three works.
senses.exampleCN: 每位奖项申请人都必须提交三件作品。
senses.why: The oldest gloss is simply 'one who applies, candidate'. When the specific institution drops away, what remains is the core picture: a person attaching himself to something he wants.
senses.whyCN: 最古老的释义就是“申请的人、候选人”。当具体机构退场，剩下的就是核心画面：一个人把自己贴到他想要的东西上。

intro.en: Applicant is a direct borrowing of the Latin present participle applicans (applicantem), not an English apply + -ant coinage. The noun application has a different suffix and a different job. Dates are approximate.
intro.cn: applicant 是对拉丁语现在分词 applicans（applicantem）的直接借用，并非英语 apply + -ant 的临时拼装。名词 application 后缀不同、分工也不同。年代为大致估计。

items.en: Applicant is first recorded meaning 'one who applies, candidate'. It enters English as a whole Latin participle, already carrying the '-ant' ending.
items.cn: applicant 最早记录为“申请的人、候选人”。它整块地作为拉丁分词进入英语，已经带着 -ant 词尾。

items.en: The source is applicantem, accusative of applicans, the present participle of applicare. The participle says 'the one attaching (himself)', not 'the one who has attached'.
items.cn: 来源是 applicantem——applicans 的宾格，applicare 的现在分词。分词说的是“正在（把自己）贴上去的人”，而不是“已经贴好的人”。

items.en: The -ant comes from Latin -antem, the ending of present participles used as nouns: it names the person doing the action now.
items.cn: -ant 出自拉丁语 -antem，是现在分词作名词时的词尾：命名“此刻正在做该动作的人”。

items.en: applicare 'attach to' is ad- 'to' + plicare 'fold'. The applicant literally 'folds himself onto' the job, the school, the state or the fund.
items.cn: applicare“贴附到”是 ad-“向”+ plicare“折叠”。申请人字面上是“把自己折贴到”职位、学校、国家或基金上。

items.en: English does not build applicant as apply + -ant; the word was borrowed ready-made. Application, by contrast, uses -ation (Latin -ationem), an action/result suffix, so it names the request, not the person.
items.cn: 英语并不是用 apply + -ant 造出 applicant；这个词是成品借入的。相反，application 用 -ation（拉丁 -ationem）这一动作／结果后缀，因此命名请求，而非人。

items.en: The word spreads across domains — employment, admission, immigration, credit, grants, law, patents, insurance — while keeping one role: the person who initiates an application.
items.cn: 这个词扩展到就业、入学、移民、信贷、资助、法律、专利、保险等领域，却始终保留一个角色：发起申请的人。

note.en: The first group separates the applicant word family from look-alikes; the second group compares words for people in related roles.
note.cn: 第一组把 applicant 词族与撞形词分开；第二组比较指人的相关角色词。

entries.definition: the act of applying or the form submitted. It uses -ation and names the request, while applicant names the person.
entries.definitionCN: 申请行为或提交的表格。它用 -ation，命名请求；applicant 则命名人。

entries.definition: capable of being applied. It is an adjective from the same stem, not a person noun.
entries.definitionCN: 可应用的；适用的。它是同一词干的形容词，不是指人的名词。

entries.definition: a tool for applying a substance. The -or suffix marks an instrument or agent, not a person who files a request.
entries.definitionCN: 涂抹工具。后缀 -or 标记工具或施动者，不是提交申请的人。

entries.definition: a person put forward or putting himself forward for a position or award. It is broader than applicant and can include nominees.
entries.definitionCN: 被提名或自荐争取职位、奖项的人。它比 applicant 更宽，可包括被提名者。

entries.definition: a person who presents a formal petition, especially to a court or authority. It is close to the legal sense of applicant.
entries.definitionCN: 提交正式请愿书的人，尤指向法院或当局。它接近 applicant 的法律义。

entries.definition: a person who claims a right, benefit, or payment. It stresses an entitlement being asserted, not an application being filed.
entries.definitionCN: 主张权利、福利或款项的人。它强调主张某项应得权利，而非提交申请。

normalIntro.en: Normal associations follow the real Latin participle and the real family suffixes, not invented rhymes.
normalIntro.cn: 正常联想沿着真实的拉丁分词和真实词族后缀展开，不用编造的顺口溜。

normal.en: applicant is a borrowed Latin present participle, applicans; it is not apply + -ant assembled in English.
normal.cn: applicant 是借来的拉丁现在分词 applicans；不是英语里用 apply + -ant 拼装的。

normal.en: The -ant (Latin -antem) means 'the one doing it now': the applicant is caught in the act of attaching himself.
normal.cn: -ant（拉丁 -antem）意为“此刻正在做的人”：applicant 正处在“把自己贴上去”的动作中。

normal.en: The family shares one stem but different suffixes: -ant person, -ation request, -able ability, -or instrument.
normal.cn: 词族共享一个词干，后缀各司其职：-ant 指人，-ation 指请求，-able 指能力，-or 指工具。

normal.en: plicare 'fold' explains the paperwork: the applicant folds himself onto the job, the school, or the visa file.
normal.cn: plicare“折叠”解释了文书行为：申请人把自己折贴到职位、学校或签证档案上。

normal.en: In law, applicant and respondent are a pair: the one who brings the application and the one who answers it.
normal.cn: 在法律中，applicant 与 respondent 成对：一个提出申请，一个应诉。

abstract.en: Picture a person at a desk, leaning forward with a form in both hands, pressing himself toward the thing he wants.
abstract.cn: 想象一个人坐在桌前，双手举着表格，身体前倾，朝他想得到的东西压过去。

abstract.en: The form, the photograph and the signature are all ways of pinning one person to one file; that is the 'attach' inside applicant.
abstract.cn: 表格、照片和签名都是把一个人钉到一份档案上的方式；这就是 applicant 内部那个“贴附”。

abstract.en: The word always names the person, never the paper: the paper is the application, the person is the applicant.
abstract.cn: 这个词永远指人，不指纸：纸是 application，人是 applicant。

examples.en: The applicant was invited back for a second interview.
examples.cn: 这位申请人被邀请参加第二轮面试。

examples.en: Applicants must submit their transcripts by the end of March.
examples.cn: 申请人必须在三月底前提交成绩单。

examples.en: The court asked the applicant to file the missing documents within seven days.
examples.cn: 法院要求申请方在七天内补交缺失的文件。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「阿普利肯求」——阿普利肯低声恳求，双手递上表格求一份工作 → applicant 申请人

root: 拉丁语 applicans／applicantem，是 applicare“贴附到”的现在分词；applicare＝ad-“向”+ plicare“折叠”（PIE *plek-“编织”）。字面是“正在把自己贴上去的人”，后缀 -ant（拉丁 -antem）表“正在做该动作的人”。

sensesIntro.en: Nine senses of applicant all name the same role: the person in the act of attaching himself to something he wants. The object changes — a job, a school, a state, credit, a grant, a court, a patent, an insurer, a prize.
sensesIntro.cn: applicant 的九个义项都命名同一个角色：正在把自己贴到想要之物上的人。变化的只是对象——职位、学校、国家、信贷、资助、法院、专利、保险人、奖项。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a person leans forward and attaches himself to the thing he is asking for.
core.cn: 核心意象：一个人身体前倾，把自己贴到他正在争取的东西上。

branches.en: WORK AND STUDY: the two everyday applications, to an employer and to a school.
branches.cn: 工作与求学：两种最常见的申请，向雇主和向学校。

branches.en: MONEY AND MOVEMENT: permission to enter a country, and permission to borrow.
branches.cn: 钱与迁徙：获准入境，以及获准借款。

branches.en: SUPPORT AND OWNERSHIP: funding for a project, and the legal claim in a patent.
branches.cn: 支持与权利：项目经费，以及专利中的法律主张。

branches.en: THE COURTROOM: applicant becomes a formal party to a proceeding.
branches.cn: 法庭：applicant 成为诉讼中的正式一方。

branches.en: CONTRACT AND GENERAL: the pre-policy applicant, and the broad candidate who puts himself forward.
branches.cn: 合同与泛指：保单签发前的申请人，以及广义上自荐的候选人。

intro.en: Applicant carries -ant, not -ation. The suffix comes from Latin -antem, the ending of present participles used as nouns; it names the person performing the action. The base is applic- from applicare.
intro.cn: applicant 带的是 -ant，不是 -ation。该后缀出自拉丁语 -antem，是现在分词作名词的词尾，命名正在执行动作的人。词基是 applicare 的 applic-。

latinIntro.en: Applicare 'attach to' is ad- 'to' + plicare 'fold'. Its present participle applicans supplies applicant-; its action noun applicatio supplies application.
latinIntro.cn: applicare“贴附到”由 ad-“向”+ plicare“折叠”构成。它的现在分词 applicans 提供 applicant-；它的动作名词 applicatio 提供 application。

items.meaning: a person who applies for something
items.meaningCN: 申请人（-ant 表示正在做该动作的人）
items.example: Only one applicant had the required licence.
items.exampleCN: 只有一位申请人持有必需的执照。

items.meaning: to attach oneself or something; to request
items.meaningCN: 贴附；应用；申请（字面“折向”）
items.example: He applied for the post on Monday.
items.exampleCN: 他周一申请了那个职位。

items.meaning: the act of applying; the form or request
items.meaningCN: 申请；申请书；应用（-ation 构成动作／结果名词）
items.example: Her application arrived after the deadline.
items.exampleCN: 她的申请在截止之后才到。

items.meaning: capable of being applied; relevant
items.meaningCN: 可应用的；适用的（-able 构成形容词）
items.example: The condition is applicable to all applicants.
items.exampleCN: 该条件适用于所有申请人。

items.meaning: the quality of being applicable
items.meaningCN: 适用性（-ity 构成性质名词）
items.example: The board debated the applicability of the old policy.
items.exampleCN: 董事会讨论了旧政策的适用性。

items.meaning: relating to application
items.meaningCN: 应用的；施用的（-ive 构成形容词）
items.example: The applicative suffix marks the beneficiary.
items.exampleCN: applicative 后缀标记受益者。

items.meaning: a tool used to apply a substance
items.meaningCN: 涂抹器；施用工具（-or 表工具或施动者）
items.example: The nurse used a sterile applicator.
items.exampleCN: 护士使用了无菌涂抹器。

items.meaning: an older English-formed rival of applicable
items.meaningCN: appliable：由英语 apply 直接加 -able 的旧形式，后被 applicable 取代
items.example: The word appliable was common in the 15c.
items.exampleCN: appliable 一词在 15 世纪很常见。

items.meaning: to apply something wrongly or to the wrong case
items.meaningCN: 误用；错误地施用（mis- 表“错误”）
items.example: The rule was misapplied to a case it never covered.
items.exampleCN: 这条规则被误用到它从未覆盖的案件上。

items.meaning: to apply again, as for a post or a grant
items.meaningCN: 重新申请；再次施用（re- 表“再次”）
items.example: She decided to reapply for the scholarship next year.
items.exampleCN: 她决定明年重新申请这项奖学金。

latinEntries.meaningCN: 正在贴附（自身）的；正在申请的

definition_zh: 应用；运用；用途；涂抹；敷用；申请；申请书；应用程序
definition_en: the act of putting something to use or bringing it to bear on a task; a formal request, especially for a job; a computer program; also the act of spreading a substance onto a surface
core_image: 把一层东西折好、贴到要用的位置上：折→贴→投入使用
scene: At a job fair, a woman slides a completed application form under the glass of the recruitment desk, a pen still in her hand, and the clerk clips it into a folder marked with the job title.
sceneCN: 这里 application 是「申请」（第 5 个义项：正式提出求职请求）；句意：招聘会上，一名女子把填好的申请表从招聘台的玻璃下递进去，工作人员把它夹进标有岗位名称的文件夹。图中可辨识物件：申请表、招聘台玻璃、岗位文件夹、夹子、笔。

pos.zh: 应用；运用；用途；涂抹；申请；申请书；应用程序

senses.title: Bringing something to bear: putting it to work
senses.titleCN: 把某物施加上去：投入使用
senses.definition: the act of bringing a method, tool, or force to bear on something so that it does work
senses.definitionCN: 把方法、工具或力量施加到某物上，使其发挥作用的行为
senses.example: The application of heat turned the solid slowly into a liquid.
senses.exampleCN: 加热使这种固体慢慢变成了液体。
senses.why: Applicare is ad- 'to' plus plicare 'fold': one thing is folded onto another. The earliest English sense, 'the bringing of something to bear on something else', is that folding made active — a force or method laid against a target.
senses.whyCN: applicare 是 ad-“向”加 plicare“折叠”：把一样东西折贴到另一样上。英语最早的义项“把某物施加到另一物上”，就是这一折贴动作开始发力——让力量或方法贴住目标。

senses.title: Force pressed onto a surface
senses.titleCN: 施加在表面上的力
senses.definition: the act of pressing or placing something, such as force or pressure, directly onto a surface or point
senses.definitionCN: 把力、压力等直接施加到某个表面或点上的行为
senses.example: The brake failed because too much application of force cracked the pad.
senses.exampleCN: 刹车失灵，是因为施加的力过大，把刹车片压裂了。
senses.why: The 'fold onto' picture can be physical and literal: a hand or a pad is laid on a surface and pressed. From 'bringing to bear' comes this narrower sense of force or pressure actually touching its target.
senses.whyCN: “折贴上去”的画面可以非常具体：手或垫片被放到表面并压下去。由“施加”就分出了这个更窄的义项——力或压力真正接触目标。

senses.title: A particular use or purpose
senses.titleCN: 特定的用途
senses.definition: a specific way in which something can be used, or the purpose for which it is intended
senses.definitionCN: 某物可以被使用的特定方式，或它被设计要达到的目的
senses.example: The new material has applications in aircraft and medical implants.
senses.exampleCN: 这种新材料在航空和医疗植入物方面有用途。
senses.why: Once a tool or method is folded onto a need, that point of attachment is a use. The sense shifts from the act of applying to the place where the thing can be applied: its application.
senses.whyCN: 当一种工具或方法被折贴到某个需求上，那个贴合点就是一种用途。词义于是从“施加这个动作”转到“可以被施加的地方”——它的用途。

senses.title: A layer spread onto a surface
senses.titleCN: 涂在表面上的一层
senses.definition: the act of spreading a substance such as paint, cream, or medicine onto a surface
senses.definitionCN: 把颜料、乳霜或药物等物质涂敷到某一表面上的行为
senses.example: Apply the ointment in a thin application twice a day.
senses.exampleCN: 每天薄薄涂敷药膏两次。
senses.why: This is the fold image at its most literal: a layer is laid onto a surface and made to adhere. The noun names both the spreading act and, by extension, the layer itself.
senses.whyCN: 这是“折贴”画面最字面的一次：一层东西被铺到表面上并粘住。这个名词既指涂抹动作，也引申指涂上去的那一层。

senses.title: A formal request, especially for a job
senses.titleCN: 正式申请（尤指求职）
senses.definition: a formal request made to a person or organization, especially for a job, a place, or permission
senses.definitionCN: 向个人或机构提出的正式请求，尤指求职、入学名额或许可
senses.example: She sent her application to three firms before graduation.
senses.exampleCN: 毕业前她向三家公司递交了求职申请。
