senses.why: The 1851 sense 'a formal request to be hired' extends 'bringing something to bear': a request is brought formally before someone with power to grant it. The object being applied is now the request itself.
senses.whyCN: 1851 年出现的“正式请求受雇”义扩展了“把某物施加到……”：请求被正式带到有权批准的人面前。此时被贴上去的对象，就是请求本身。

senses.title: The written form that carries the request
senses.titleCN: 承载请求的书面表格
senses.definition: the paper or online form on which such a request is written, rather than the request itself
senses.definitionCN: 写有这种请求的纸质或在线表格，指的是文件而非请求本身
senses.example: Please send your application by email before Friday.
senses.exampleCN: 请在周五前通过电子邮件发送你的申请表。
senses.why: From the request, the noun moves to the physical paper that bears it. The sheet is what is clipped to the employer's file, so it inherits the name of the act it records.
senses.whyCN: 从“请求”本身，这个词又转到承载请求的那张纸。被夹进雇主档案的正是这张表，于是它继承了它所记录的那项行为的名称。

senses.title: A computer program
senses.titleCN: 应用程序
senses.definition: a computer program designed to perform a task for a user, especially one run on a phone or personal computer
senses.definitionCN: 为完成用户任务而设计的计算机程序，尤指手机或个人电脑上运行的软件
senses.example: The map application finds the nearest train station.
senses.exampleCN: 这款地图应用程序能找到最近的火车站。
senses.why: The 20th-century computer sense keeps the core picture: a program is a tool folded onto the user's task. It is not a new root meaning but one more thing that can be 'applied' to a need.
senses.whyCN: 20 世纪的计算机义保留了核心画面：程序是被折贴到用户任务上的工具。它不是新的词根义，而是又一种可以被“施加”到需求上的东西。

senses.title: Close attention or hard effort
senses.titleCN: 专注用力
senses.definition: the act of applying oneself closely and with steady effort to a task or subject
senses.definitionCN: 把自己紧贴在一项任务或学科上，持续用力的状态
senses.example: His application to Latin grammar finally paid off.
senses.exampleCN: 他对拉丁语语法的刻苦钻研终于有了回报。
senses.why: The c.1600 sense 'sincere hard effort' folds the person onto the work: the mind is held against the subject. Here what is applied is not a tool but one's attention.
senses.whyCN: 约 1600 年出现的“真诚的努力”义，把人折贴到工作上：心智紧贴住这门学问。这里被施加的不是工具，而是自己的注意力。

senses.title: Relevance: the rule fits the case
senses.titleCN: 适用性：规则恰好贴合该情形
senses.definition: the quality of being relevant to or valid for a particular case or situation
senses.definitionCN: 与某一具体案例或情境相关、或对其有效的性质
senses.example: The old rule has no application to online sales.
senses.exampleCN: 这条旧规则不适用于线上销售。
senses.why: A rule is folded onto a case; if the two surfaces fit, the rule has application. The noun now names the fit itself, moving from the act of applying to the possibility of being applied.
senses.whyCN: 规则被折贴到一个案例上；如果两个面贴合，这条规则就有适用性。名词此时命名的是这种贴合，从“施加动作”转到“可被施加的可能性”。

intro.en: Application reaches English from Latin through Old French. Its parts are ad- 'to' and plicare 'fold', and the suffix -ation turns the action of folding something on into a noun; the modern senses are successive extensions of that attachment.
intro.cn: application 经由古法语从拉丁语进入英语。构词成分是 ad-“向”和 plicare“折叠”，后缀 -ation 把“把某物折贴上去”这一动作变成名词；现代各义项都是这一贴附意象的连续扩展。

items.en: First recorded in English as 'the bringing of something to bear on something else', a very general sense of putting one thing against another.
items.cn: 最早见于英语，义为“把某物施加到另一物上”，是一个非常宽泛的“把一物作用到另一物”的意思。

items.en: Borrowed through Old French aplicacion (14c.), which carried the Latin noun into English spelling and pronunciation.
items.cn: 经由 14 世纪古法语 aplicacion 借入，这一法语形式把拉丁名词带入了英语的拼写与读音。

items.en: Latin applicationem (applicatio) meant 'a joining to, an attaching oneself to; relation of a client to a patron'. It is the action noun of the past-participle stem of applicare.
items.cn: 拉丁语 applicationem（applicatio）意为“连接、把自己附着上去；门客与庇护人的关系”。它是 applicare 过去分词词干的动作名词。

items.en: Applicare 'attach to, join, connect' = ad- 'to' + plicare 'fold'. PIE *plek- 'to plait' supplies the underlying picture of folding one strand or surface onto another.
items.cn: applicare“附着、连接、结合”= ad-“向”+ plicare“折叠”。原始印欧语 *plek-“编织”提供了底层画面：把一股或一层折到另一层上。

items.en: The sense 'sincere hard effort' is recorded about 1600, and 'a formal request to be hired' in 1851. Both extend the idea of bringing something to bear: effort onto study, a request before an employer.
items.cn: “真诚而努力”义约记录于 1600 年，“正式请求受雇”义记录于 1851 年。两者都扩展了“把某物施加上去”：把努力贴到学业上，把请求带到雇主面前。

items.en: The computer sense of application, a program applied to a user's task, is a 20th-century addition. The suffix -ation throughout marks the action or its result, not a new root.
items.cn: 计算机义“应用程序”（施加于用户任务上的程序）是 20 世纪的增补。贯穿其中的后缀 -ation 标记动作或其结果，并非新的词根。

note.en: The first group shares the applic- stem and the -ation/-ance/-able shapes; the second shares the idea of using or asking. Form and meaning are kept apart on purpose.
note.cn: 第一组共享 applic- 词干以及 -ation／-ance／-able 的词形；第二组共享“使用”或“请求”的意思。两组刻意把词形与词义分开。

entries.definition: a person who formally asks for something, especially a job. It is applic- plus -ant, a person noun from the same apply family.
entries.definitionCN: 正式提出请求的人，尤指求职者。它是 applic- 加 -ant 构成的人名词，与 apply 同属一个词族。

entries.definition: able to be applied or relevant to a case. It is applic- plus -able, and describes fitness rather than a request or a program.
entries.definitionCN: 可应用的；适用于某情形的。它是 applic- 加 -able，描述“是否贴合”，而不是请求或程序。

entries.definition: a device, usually electrical, used in the home. It is apply plus -ance, so it names a thing that is applied to a household task, not a formal request.
entries.definitionCN: 家用电器。它是 apply 加 -ance，指被用于家务任务的器具，而不是正式申请。

entries.definition: the act of employing something for a purpose. It is the broad everyday word; application often sounds more technical or deliberate.
entries.definitionCN: 为某目的使用某物。它是最宽泛的日常词；application 往往更技术化，或更强调有意识地施加。

entries.definition: the act of putting a plan, rule, or system into effect. It stresses execution, while application stresses the point where a method meets a case.
entries.definitionCN: 把计划、规则或制度付诸实施。它强调执行，而 application 强调方法与案例相贴合的落点。

entries.definition: the act of politely or formally asking for something. It covers the asking itself, while an application is the formal, often written request.
entries.definitionCN: 礼貌或正式地请求某事的行为。它泛指“请求”，而 application 是正式的、常为书面的申请。

normalIntro.en: These links are real: the Latin parts ad- and plicare, the noun suffix -ation, and the documented phrases application form and application software.
normalIntro.cn: 这些联想都是真实的：拉丁语成分 ad- 与 plicare、名词后缀 -ation，以及有据可查的 application form、application software 等短语。

normal.en: Ad- means 'to' and plicare means 'fold': think of folding a patch onto cloth, and the patch is applied to the cloth.
normal.cn: ad- 意为“向”，plicare 意为“折叠”：想象把一块补丁折贴到布上，这块补丁就被 apply 到布上了。

normal.en: A job application is a request folded onto an employer's file: the employer receives it and can act on it.
normal.cn: 求职申请就是把请求折贴到雇主档案里：雇主收到它，才能据此行动。

normal.en: Application form and application software are fixed phrases: one carries a request, the other runs a user's task.
normal.cn: application form 与 application software 是固定短语：前者承载请求，后者运行用户的任务。

normal.en: The family is visible: apply the verb, applicant the person, applicable the fit, appliance the household device.
normal.cn: 同族关系一眼可见：apply 是动词，applicant 是人，applicable 是“贴合”，appliance 是家用器具。

normal.en: The older sense survives in 'application to study': here the mind is what is applied to the subject.
normal.cn: 较古老的义项仍活在 application to study 中：这里被施加到学科上的是心智。

abstract.en: A sheet is folded over the edge of a file: first it is loose, then it is aligned, then it is pressed flat. Application is that final contact.
abstract.cn: 一张纸沿文件边缘折过去：先松散，再对齐，最后压平。application 就是最后贴合的那一下。

abstract.en: The same patch can be a tool laid on a task, a rule laid on a case, a request laid before an authority, or a program laid on a need.
abstract.cn: 同一块“补丁”可以是放到任务上的工具、放到案例上的规则、递到权力机构前的请求，或放到需求上的程序。

abstract.en: The word always needs two surfaces: something that is applied, and something it is applied to. Remove either and the image collapses.
abstract.cn: 这个词永远需要两个面：被施加的东西，以及它施加到的对象。拿掉任一面，画面就塌了。

examples.en: The application of fertilizer doubled the yield in one season.
examples.cn: 施肥使一季的产量翻了一番。

examples.en: Her job application was rejected because the form arrived after the deadline.
examples.cn: 她的求职申请被拒，因为申请表在截止日期之后才到。

examples.en: This app has a simple application that lets you scan a page into text.
examples.cn: 这款应用有一个简单功能，能让你把书页扫描成文字。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「阿普利凯申」——阿普（Ap）利落地把申请表递进窗口，凯申（Kai Shen）接过就盖章 → application 申请、应用

root: 源自拉丁语 applicare“attach to, join, connect”（ad-“向”+ plicare“折叠”），由“把某物折贴到另一物上”引申为应用、用途、涂抹、正式申请与应用程序。

sensesIntro.en: Nine senses of application all come from one fold: something is laid onto something else and made to act there. From a force brought to bear, the word branches into uses, layers, requests, forms, software, effort and relevance.
sensesIntro.cn: application 的九个义项都来自同一个“折”：把某物铺到另一物上并在那里起作用。从“施加的力”出发，这个词分出用途、涂层、请求、表格、软件、专注与适用性等分支。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a layer or sheet folded onto a surface and pressed into use.
core.cn: 核心意象：一层东西或一张纸被折贴到表面上，并压入使用。

branches.en: FORCE AND METHOD: a tool or pressure laid on a target is the first English sense.
branches.cn: 力量与方法：工具或压力被放到目标上，这是最早的英语义项。

branches.en: USES AND LAYERS: the point where something is applied becomes a use, and a substance spread on a surface becomes a layer.
branches.cn: 用途与涂层：某物被施加的落点变成用途，涂在表面上的物质变成一层。

branches.en: REQUEST AND FORM: the formal request, and then the sheet that carries it to the employer.
branches.cn: 申请与表格：正式的请求，以及把请求带到雇主面前的纸张。

branches.en: SOFTWARE: a program is one more tool folded onto a user's task.
branches.cn: 软件：程序是又一种被折贴到用户任务上的工具。

branches.en: EFFORT AND RELEVANCE: the mind applied to study, and a rule that fits the case.
branches.cn: 用力与适用：心智贴到学业上，以及恰好贴合案例的规则。

intro.en: Application is applic- plus -ation. The -ation, from Latin -ationem, turns an action into a noun or names its result; English then builds applicant, applicable, applicability, appliance and misapplication around the same stem.
intro.cn: application 是 applic- 加 -ation。-ation 来自拉丁语 -ationem，把动作变成名词或命名其结果；英语随后围绕同一词干构造出 applicant、applicable、applicability、appliance 与 misapplication。

latinIntro.en: Latin applicare 'attach to' is ad- plus plicare 'fold, plait'. Its action noun applicatio gives application, and the same plicare family includes implicare 'enfold, entangle'.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语 applicare“附着”是 ad- 加 plicare“折叠、编织”。其动作名词 applicatio 给出 application，同一 plicare 词族还包括 implicare“包住、缠绕”。

items.meaning: the act of applying, or a formal request / program
items.meaningCN: 应用；申请；应用程序（-ation 构成动作或结果名词）
items.example: The application of the new rule starts in May.
items.exampleCN: 新规则的施行从五月开始。

items.meaning: to put something to use, spread it on, or make a request
items.meaningCN: 应用；涂抹；申请（ap- 是 ad- 的拼写变体，ply 来自 plicare“折叠”）
items.example: Apply the paint in thin layers.
items.exampleCN: 把颜料薄薄地涂上几层。

items.meaning: a person who makes a formal request
items.meaningCN: 申请人（-ant 表示做该动作的人）
items.example: Each applicant must bring two photographs.
items.exampleCN: 每位申请人必须带两张照片。

items.meaning: relevant to, or able to be applied to, a case
items.meaningCN: 适用的；可应用的（-able 表示能够被……的）
items.example: The discount is applicable to full-price tickets only.
items.exampleCN: 折扣只适用于全价票。

items.meaning: the quality of being relevant or usable in a case
items.meaningCN: 适用性（-ity 构成状态名词）
items.example: The court questioned the applicability of the old law.
items.exampleCN: 法院质疑这条旧法律的适用性。

items.meaning: a device used for a household task
items.meaningCN: 家用器具；电器（-ance 构成事物或状态名词）
items.example: The kitchen appliance heats water in seconds.
items.exampleCN: 这台厨房电器几秒钟就能把水加热。

items.meaning: put to practical use, as in applied science
items.meaningCN: 应用的；实用的（-ed 构成形容词）
items.example: Applied research aims at a usable product.
items.exampleCN: 应用研究以可用的产品为目标。

items.meaning: the wrong use of a rule, word, or resource
items.meaningCN: 误用；滥用（mis- 表示错误地）
items.example: The report criticized the misapplication of the funds.
items.exampleCN: 报告批评了这些资金的误用。

latinEntries.meaning: to attach, join, connect; to apply
a joining to, an attaching oneself to

definition_zh: 估价；评估；赏识；感激；增值；货币升值；鉴赏
definition_en: the act of estimating the quality or worth of something; recognition of value; gratitude; an increase in value; also a written or spoken expression of approval
core_image: 把一件东西放上估价的天平：先称出它值多少，再承认它值钱，最后为这份价值心生感激
scene: At a gallery, a curator holds a small bronze bird under a lamp, turns it slowly with a magnifying glass, and writes a figure on a valuation slip beside a stack of auction records. Its appreciation took three experts two days.
sceneCN: 这里 appreciation 是「估价、评估价值」（第 1 个义项：判断某物的品质与价值）；句意：那件小铜鸟的估价花了三位专家两天时间。图中可辨识物件：青铜鸟、台灯、估价单、拍卖记录、放大镜。

pos.zh: 估价；评估；赏识；感激；增值；鉴赏

collocations.zh: 深切的感激；深刻的理解

derivatives.zh: 未受赏识的；未被感激的

senses.title: Estimating worth: putting a value on something
senses.titleCN: 估定价值：给某物定个价
senses.definition: the act of estimating the quality, condition, or monetary worth of something
senses.definitionCN: 判断某物的品质、状况或金钱价值的行为
senses.example: The appreciation of the painting took three experts two days.
senses.exampleCN: 鉴定这幅画的价值花了三位专家两天时间。
senses.why: Late Latin appretiare is ad- 'to' plus pretium 'price': to set a price on a thing. The first English sense, recorded c.1600, is exactly this act of estimating quality and worth.
senses.whyCN: 晚期拉丁语 appretiare 是 ad-“向”加 pretium“价格”：给某物定个价。英语最早记录于约 1600 年的义项，正是这种判断品质与价值的行为。

senses.title: Recognition of value: esteeming what is good
senses.titleCN: 认出价值：赏识好东西
senses.definition: a favorable estimate of someone or something; the recognition that something is valuable or excellent
senses.definitionCN: 对某人或某物的高评价；承认某物有价值或很出色的认识
senses.example: Her appreciation of the old craftsman's skill grew with every visit.
senses.exampleCN: 每去一次，她对这位老匠人技艺的赏识就多一分。
senses.why: If the estimated worth is high, the estimate becomes esteem. After c.1650 appreciation commonly carried this 'high estimate' sense: the scale tips upward and the word names recognition rather than mere measurement.
senses.whyCN: 如果估出的价值很高，估价就变成器重。约 1650 年之后，appreciation 通常带有“高估”之义：天平向上倾斜，词义也从单纯的测量转为“认出价值”。

senses.title: Gratitude: valuing what someone has done
senses.titleCN: 感激：珍视别人所做之事
senses.definition: the feeling of being thankful for a kindness or benefit, and of recognizing its worth
senses.definitionCN: 因受到善意或帮助而心存感谢，并承认这份好处的价值
senses.example: He wrote a short note of appreciation to the nurse who stayed late.
senses.exampleCN: 他给那位守到很晚的护士写了一张简短的感谢便条。
senses.why: The thing now valued is another person's act. To appreciate a kindness is to put a high worth on it, and that estimate surfaces as gratitude — the emotional form of 'it was worth a lot to me'.
senses.whyCN: 此时被估价的是他人的行为。appreciate 一份善意，就是给它很高的价值，而这份估价浮上来就成感激——也就是“这对我很值”的情感形式。

senses.title: Rise in value: the asset gains worth
senses.titleCN: 增值：资产变得值钱
senses.definition: an increase in the value of property, shares, or other assets over time
senses.definitionCN: 房产、股票或其他资产随时间而增加的价值
senses.example: The house's appreciation paid for their daughter's tuition.
senses.exampleCN: 这栋房子的增值支付了他们女儿的学费。
senses.why: The noun shifts from the act of valuing to the value itself moving upward. The 1784 sense 'a rise in value' is the price side of pretium growing, not a new estimate being made.
senses.whyCN: 名词从“估价的动作”转到“价值本身向上走”。1784 年出现的“价值上升”义，是 pretium 的“价格”一面在增长，而不是又做了一次估价。

senses.title: A formal valuation: the official figure
senses.titleCN: 正式估价：官方核定的数字
senses.definition: a formal assessment of value, as for tax, insurance, or sale, often recorded as a figure
senses.definitionCN: 为税务、保险或出售而做的正式价值评估，通常落成一个数字
senses.example: The insurance appreciation came in well below the rebuild cost.
senses.exampleCN: 保险估价远低于重建成本。
senses.why: The 1799 sense 'act of setting a value on' narrows the first sense into an official act. Here the estimate is written down and binding, so appreciation becomes a valuation document rather than a private judgment.
senses.whyCN: 1799 年出现的“给某物定价的行为”把最早义项收窄为一种官方行为。此时估价被写下来并具有约束力，appreciation 也就从私人判断变成一份估价文件。

senses.title: An expression of approval: the words of praise
senses.titleCN: 赞赏之辞：说出来的好评
senses.definition: a spoken or written statement that recognizes the good qualities of someone or something
senses.definitionCN: 口头或书面承认某人某物优点的表述
senses.example: The review was a warm appreciation of the young pianist.
senses.exampleCN: 那篇评论是对这位年轻钢琴家的热情赞赏。
senses.why: The 1858 sense 'expression of favorable estimation' externalizes the inner estimate. What was a judgment in the mind becomes words; the noun now names the tribute rather than the appraisal.
senses.whyCN: 1858 年出现的“表达有利评价”把内心的估价外化。原本在心里的判断变成了话语；名词此时命名的是称许，而不是评估过程。

senses.title: Understanding the significance: seeing why it matters
senses.titleCN: 体认意义：明白它为何重要
senses.definition: a clear understanding of the importance, difficulty, or meaning of something
senses.definitionCN: 对某事的重要性、难度或意义的清楚理解
senses.example: Living through the drought gave them a new appreciation of water.
senses.exampleCN: 经历过那场干旱，他们对水有了新的体会。
senses.why: To value something fully you must see what it costs or what it does. This branch moves from worth to understanding: the estimate is now a grasp of significance, as in an appreciation of the difficulty.
senses.whyCN: 要真正看重某物，必须看见它的代价或作用。这条分支从“价值”转到“理解”：估价在这里变成对意义的把握，如 appreciation of the difficulty（对困难的认识）。

senses.title: Currency appreciation: the money grows stronger
senses.titleCN: 货币升值：钱变得更值钱
senses.definition: an increase in the exchange value of a currency relative to other currencies
senses.definitionCN: 一种货币相对于其他货币的汇兑价值上升
senses.example: A sharp appreciation of the yen made imports cheaper.
senses.exampleCN: 日元的急剧升值让进口商品变便宜了。
senses.why: This is the asset sense applied to a whole currency: its price in other currencies rises. The word still measures worth, but the worth being measured is the money itself.
senses.whyCN: 这是资产义应用到整种货币上：它以其他货币计的价格上升。这个词仍在衡量价值，只是被衡量的对象变成了钱本身。

senses.title: Aesthetic appreciation: taste trained on art
senses.titleCN: 审美鉴赏：被艺术训练过的眼光
senses.definition: the trained enjoyment and evaluation of art, music, or beauty, based on discernment rather than mere liking
senses.definitionCN: 对艺术、音乐或美的有训练的欣赏与评价，基于鉴别力而非单纯喜欢
senses.example: The course teaches the appreciation of Renaissance painting.
senses.exampleCN: 这门课教授文艺复兴绘画的鉴赏。
senses.why: The recognition sense is applied to beauty: the viewer estimates quality, feels its worth, and is pleased. Aesthetic appreciation is thus valuation and gratitude-like delight fused into taste.
senses.whyCN: “认出价值”的义项被用到美上：观者判断品质，感到它可贵，并因此愉悦。审美鉴赏于是是估价与类似感激的喜悦融合成趣味。

intro.en: Appreciation entered English c.1600 from French appréciation, the action noun of apprécier, and behind both stands Late Latin appretiare 'estimate the quality of' — ad- 'to' plus pretium 'price'. The suffix -ion turns the act into a noun. Its family is the price family, not the proper family of appropriate and not the near family of approximate.
intro.cn: appreciation 约于 1600 年从法语 appréciation 进入英语，它是 apprécier 的动作名词；两者背后是晚期拉丁语 appretiare“评估品质”——ad-“向”加 pretium“价格”。后缀 -ion 把这个动作变成名词。它属于“价格”词族，既不是 appropriate 的“自己的”词族，也不是 approximate 的“最近”词族。

items.en: First recorded as 'act of estimating the quality and worth of something'. The earliest sense is valuation, not gratitude.
items.cn: 最早记录为“判断某物品质与价值的行为”。最早的义项是估价，而不是感激。

items.en: From French appréciation, the action noun of apprécier (14c.). French passed on both the noun and the verb pattern, with -tion marking an action or its result.
items.cn: 来自法语 appréciation，即 apprécier（14 世纪）的动作名词。法语把名词和动词模式一并传下，-tion 标记动作或其结果。

items.en: Appretiare 'estimate the quality of' = ad- 'to' + pretium 'price'. The verb literally sets a price on a thing, so worth and price are one idea at the root.
items.cn: appretiare“评估品质”= ad-“向”+ pretium“价格”。这个动词字面上就是给某物定价，因此在词根处，价值与价格是同一个概念。

items.en: After c.1650 the noun generally includes a 'high estimate'; 1784 adds 'a rise in value', and 1799 'act of setting a value on'. Esteem, market gain and official valuation split off from the first sense.
items.cn: 约 1650 年之后，这个词通常含有“高估”；1784 年增加“价值上升”义，1799 年增加“给某物定值的行为”义。器重、市场增值与官方估价从最早义项中分了出来。

items.en: Appreciate is recorded only in the 1650s, later than appreciation. The 1858 sense 'expression of favorable estimation' adds spoken or written praise.
items.cn: appreciate 直到 17 世纪 50 年代才有记录，晚于 appreciation。1858 年出现的“表达有利评价”义，增加了口头或书面的称许。

items.en: All senses still run through pretium 'price': estimate a price, value it highly, feel its worth, watch it rise. Appropriate (proprius 'one's own') and approximate (proximus 'nearest') are different roots that only look alike.
items.cn: 所有义项仍贯穿 pretium“价格”：估一个价、把价估高、感到它可贵、看着它上涨。appropriate（proprius“自己的”）与 approximate（proximus“最近的”）只是形近，词根完全不同。

note.en: The first group separates appreciation from two famous look-alikes that belong to different roots; the second group separates it from words of gratitude and valuation that share only part of its meaning.
note.cn: 第一组把 appreciation 与两个著名的形近词分开，它们属于不同词根；第二组把它与只共享部分含义的“感激”和“估价”词分开。

entries.definition: to value, understand, be grateful for, or rise in value. It shares the pretium root, but it is recorded in the 1650s, later than appreciation c.1600.
entries.definitionCN: 重视；理解；感激；增值。它与 appreciation 共享 pretium 词根，但直到 17 世纪 50 年代才有记录，晚于约 1600 年的 appreciation。

entries.definition: suitable or proper for a purpose. It comes from proprius 'one's own', not from pretium 'price', so it is not a relative of appreciation.
entries.definitionCN: 合适的；恰当的。它来自 proprius“自己的”，而不是 pretium“价格”，因此不是 appreciation 的同族词。

entries.definition: close to the correct value but not exact. It comes from proximus 'nearest', a third root that merely looks similar.
entries.definitionCN: 接近正确值但不精确的。它来自 proximus“最近的”，是第三个只是看起来相似的词根。

entries.definition: the feeling of being thankful. It covers only the emotional branch, while appreciation also means valuation and increase in value.
entries.definitionCN: 感激之情。它只覆盖情感分支，而 appreciation 还表示估价与增值。

entries.definition: the act of publicly acknowledging someone's merit or existence. It stresses acknowledgment, while appreciation stresses the high value placed on the thing.
entries.definitionCN: 公开承认某人的功绩或存在。它强调“承认”，而 appreciation 强调给某物很高的评价。

entries.definition: an expert or official estimate of monetary value. It is the technical valuation branch, while appreciation can also mean esteem or gratitude.
entries.definitionCN: 专家或官方对金钱价值的估算。它是技术性的估价分支，而 appreciation 还可以指器重或感激。

normalIntro.en: These links are real: pretium 'price', the documented dates c.1600 / 1650s / 1784 / 1799 / 1858, and the fixed phrases express appreciation and capital appreciation.
normalIntro.cn: 这些联想都是真实的：pretium“价格”，有据可查的年代 1600／17 世纪 50 年代／1784／1799／1858，以及 express appreciation、capital appreciation 等固定搭配。

normal.en: Pretium is 'price'. Appreciation begins as putting a price on a thing, which is why the word can mean valuation before it means gratitude.
normal.cn: pretium 是“价格”。appreciation 的起点是给某物定价，所以它会先表示估价，之后才表示感激。

normal.en: Appreciation is recorded c.1600 but appreciate only in the 1650s: the noun came first, and the verb followed.
normal.cn: appreciation 约记录于 1600 年，而 appreciate 到 17 世纪 50 年代才出现：名词先来，动词后到。

normal.en: Capital appreciation is the rise of an asset's price; currency appreciation is the rise of a currency against others.
normal.cn: capital appreciation 是资产价格上涨；currency appreciation 是一种货币对其他货币的升值。

normal.en: Express appreciation is the standard phrase for saying thank you in a formal setting.
normal.cn: express appreciation 是在正式场合表达感谢的标准说法。

normal.en: An appreciation of art is trained taste: the same word that prices a bronze bird also judges a painting.
normal.cn: an appreciation of art 是受过训练的趣味：给铜鸟估价的同一个词，也用来品评一幅画。

abstract.en: A balance with a small object on one pan and weights on the other: the needle settles, and the object now has a worth.
abstract.cn: 一架天平，一盘放小物件，一盘放砝码：指针停住，这件东西便有了价值。

abstract.en: The needle can move up two ways: someone raises the estimate, or the object itself becomes more valuable. Appreciation covers both.
abstract.cn: 指针可以向上走两种方式：有人提高估价，或物件本身变得更值钱。appreciation 两者都覆盖。

abstract.en: Once worth is felt as a personal gift, the scale turns into a thank-you note: valuation and gratitude are the same estimate seen from inside.
abstract.cn: 当价值被感受为一份私人馈赠，天平就变成一张感谢便条：估价与感激是同一个判断的内外两面。

examples.en: The audience showed its appreciation with a long round of applause.
examples.cn: 观众以长久的掌声表达赞赏。

examples.en: Land in the district has seen steady appreciation over ten years.
examples.cn: 这个区的土地十年来稳步增值。

examples.en: Travel gave her a deeper appreciation of how differently people live.
examples.cn: 旅行让她更深刻地体会到人们的生活方式有多么不同。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「阿普瑞希爱申」——阿普（Ap）把画举到灯下估价，瑞希（Rui Xi）看得连连点头，爱申（Ai Shen）写下“很值钱” → appreciation 欣赏、感激、增值

root: 源自晚期拉丁语 appretiare“estimate the quality of”（ad-“向”+ pretium“价格”），核心是给事物定价、估出价值，再由“估得高”引申为赏识、感激与增值。

sensesIntro.en: Nine senses of appreciation all start from a pair of scales: something is priced, the price is judged high, the high worth is felt as gratitude, and the value itself may rise. Art, formal documents and currencies are later fields for the same estimate.
sensesIntro.cn: appreciation 的九个义项都从一架天平开始：给某物定价，判断价格很高，把这份高价值感受为感激，而价值本身还可能上涨。艺术、正式文件与货币只是这同一估价行为后来进入的领域。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: an object placed on a scale and given a worth.
core.cn: 核心意象：把一件东西放上天平，给它一个价值。

branches.en: ESTIMATE AND VALUATION: the original act of judging worth, and its official, written form.
branches.cn: 估价与核价：判断价值的最初行为，以及它官方化、书面化的形式。

branches.en: RECOGNITION AND TASTE: esteeming what is excellent, including the trained appreciation of art.
branches.cn: 赏识与趣味：器重出色之物，包括受过训练的艺术鉴赏。

branches.en: GRATITUDE: the high estimate of a kindness, felt as thankfulness.
branches.cn: 感激：把一份善意估得很高，并在心里感受为感谢。

branches.en: ASSETS AND CURRENCY: worth that rises, whether in property or in money itself.
branches.cn: 资产与货币：价值向上走，无论对象是房产还是货币本身。

branches.en: PRAISE AND UNDERSTANDING: the estimate spoken aloud, and the grasp of why something matters.
branches.cn: 称许与理解：说出口的评价，以及对某物为何重要的把握。

intro.en: Appreciation is appreciat- plus -ion, from Latin -ionem, which names an action or its result. English builds appreciate, appreciative, appreciatively, appreciable, appreciably and unappreciated on the same stem, and de- gives the opposite depreciate.
intro.cn: appreciation 是 appreciat- 加 -ion，后者来自拉丁语 -ionem，命名动作或其结果。英语在同一词干上构造出 appreciate、appreciative、appreciatively、appreciable、appreciably 与 unappreciated，而 de- 给出反方向的 depreciate。

latinIntro.en: The direct source is Late Latin appretiare, ad- plus pretium 'price'. Latin pretium also gives pretiare 'to price' and depretiare 'to lower the value of'; none of these belongs to proprius or proximus.
latinIntro.cn: 直接来源是晚期拉丁语 appretiare，即 ad- 加 pretium“价格”。拉丁语 pretium 还给出 pretiare“定价”与 depretiare“降低价值”；这些都不属于 proprius 或 proximus。

items.structure: appreciat- (set a value) + -ion (action or result noun)
items.meaning: valuation, esteem, gratitude, or increase in value
items.meaningCN: 估价；赏识；感激；增值（-ion 构成动作或结果名词）
items.example: She showed her appreciation with a handwritten card.
items.exampleCN: 她用一张手写卡片表达感谢。

items.meaning: to value, understand, thank, or increase in worth
items.meaningCN: 重视；理解；感激；增值（-ate 构成动词）
items.example: I appreciate your help more than I can say.
items.exampleCN: 我对你的帮助感激不尽。

items.meaning: showing gratitude or sensitive to value
items.meaningCN: 感激的；有鉴赏力的（-ive 构成形容词）
items.example: The audience was appreciative of the small ensemble.
items.exampleCN: 观众对这个小乐团很是欣赏。

items.meaning: in a grateful or admiring way
items.meaningCN: 感激地；赞赏地（-ly 构成副词）
items.example: She smiled appreciatively at the gift.
items.exampleCN: 她对这份礼物感激地笑了。

items.meaning: large enough to be noticed or measured
items.meaningCN: 可察觉的；相当可观的（-able 构成形容词）
items.example: There was an appreciable drop in temperature.
items.exampleCN: 气温有了明显的下降。

items.meaning: to a noticeable degree
items.meaningCN: 明显地；可观地（-ly 构成副词）
items.example: The room grew appreciably quieter.
items.exampleCN: 房间明显安静了下来。

items.meaning: not recognized or thanked for one's value
items.meaningCN: 未受赏识的；未被感激的（un- 表示否定）
items.example: The night staff felt unappreciated.
items.exampleCN: 夜班员工觉得自己未受重视。

items.meaning: to fall in value, or to belittle
items.meaningCN: 贬值；贬低（de-“向下”+ preci-“价格”+ -ate）
items.example: The car depreciates as soon as it is driven away.
items.exampleCN: 这辆车一开走就贬值。

latinEntries.meaning: to estimate the quality or value of
to lower the value of, disparage

definition_zh: 合适地；恰当地；得体地；适度地；合乎规定地
definition_en: in a way that is suitable for a particular purpose, person, or occasion; in a proper or fitting manner
core_image: 把一把钥匙对准它自己的锁孔：只属于这里，也只适合这里
scene: A guest in a dark suit waits until the bride's father finishes his speech, then raises a glass at exactly the right moment and says a few short words; a clock on the wall shows the hour. He acts appropriately, raising his glass only when the speech ends.
sceneCN: 这里 appropriately 是「得体地、恰合时宜地」（第 2 个义项：在社交场合举止合乎礼数）；句意：他举止得体，等演讲结束才举杯。图中可辨识物件：深色西装、酒杯、婚礼长桌、正在讲话的父亲、时钟。

pos.zh: 合适地；恰当地；得体地；适度地

collocations.zh: 说来也巧；果然恰如其分

senses.title: Suitable for the purpose: the right tool for the task
senses.titleCN: 合乎目的：用对了工具
senses.definition: in a way that suits the purpose or function of something
senses.definitionCN: 以适合某物目的或功能的方式
senses.example: The shelves were appropriately sized for the narrow alcove.
senses.exampleCN: 这些搁板做得正好适合那个窄壁龛。
senses.why: Appropriare is ad- 'to' plus proprius 'one's own': to make a thing one's own, then to set it apart for a use. What is set apart for a use fits that use, so the adverb says the action matches its purpose.
senses.whyCN: appropriare 是 ad-“向”加 proprius“自己的”：使某物成为自己的，再把它拨出来专供某用。被拨给某用途的东西就与那用途相称，因此副词表示“做某事合乎其目的”。

senses.title: Socially proper: behaving as the occasion expects
senses.titleCN: 合乎礼数：举止符合场合期待
senses.definition: in a polite or socially correct way, as the situation requires
senses.definitionCN: 以礼貌或符合社会规范的方式，符合情境要求
senses.example: The children were appropriately quiet during the ceremony.
senses.exampleCN: 仪式期间，孩子们安静得很得体。
senses.why: The 'making one's own' root turns outward: a person takes on the manners that belong to the occasion. What is proper to the room becomes proper in the person, and the adverb names that fit.
senses.whyCN: “使成为自己的”这一词根转向外部：一个人把属于这个场合的举止接纳为自己的。属于这个房间的礼数，变成这个人身上的得体，副词命名的正是这种贴合。

senses.title: Fitting the context: the response matches the situation
senses.titleCN: 贴合情境：回应与局面相称
senses.definition: in a way that matches the particular circumstances, facts, or mood of a situation
senses.definitionCN: 以符合某一情境的具体情况、事实或情绪的方式
senses.example: When the plan changed, she appropriately revised the whole schedule.
senses.exampleCN: 计划一变，她就相应地改了整个日程。
senses.why: The fit is now between an action and a changing situation. Since the appropriate response belongs to that situation, acting appropriately is acting as the case itself demands.
senses.whyCN: 这里的贴合发生在“行动”与“变化的情境”之间。恰当的回应属于那个情境，因此 appropriately 行动，就是按事情本身的要求行动。

senses.title: In due proportion: neither too much nor too little
senses.titleCN: 适度：不多也不少
senses.definition: to a proper or moderate degree, in proportion to what is needed
senses.definitionCN: 达到恰当或适中的程度，与所需成比例
senses.example: The sauce was appropriately seasoned, not oversalted.
senses.exampleCN: 酱汁调味适度，没有过咸。
senses.why: Proprius also carries the idea of what belongs to a thing's own measure. A proper share is the share that belongs to the case, so the adverb can regulate degree: enough, and not more than enough.
senses.whyCN: proprius 还带有“属于某物自身尺度”的意思。恰当的份额，就是属于这个情形的份额，因此副词也能调节程度：足够，但不超过。

senses.title: Assigned to its proper use: allocated rightly
senses.titleCN: 拨归正用：分配得当
senses.definition: of funds, time, or resources, in a way that assigns them to the use they are meant for
senses.definitionCN: 指资金、时间或资源，以把它们分配给既定用途的方式
senses.example: The grant was appropriately divided between research and training.
senses.exampleCN: 这笔拨款在研究和培训之间分配得当。
senses.why: This is the oldest mechanical sense of appropriare: to set a thing apart for a specific owner or use. Done appropriately, the allocation puts each part where it belongs.
senses.whyCN: 这是 appropriare 最古老的“操作”义：把某物拨出来专供某个所有者或用途。分配得 appropriately，就是把每一部分放到它该在的地方。

senses.title: Suited to a role: the part fits the person
senses.titleCN: 称职：角色与人相配
senses.definition: in a way that suits a person's role, rank, or responsibilities
senses.definitionCN: 以适合一个人的角色、身份或职责的方式
senses.example: The new captain appropriately took charge of the evacuation.
senses.exampleCN: 新船长恰如其分地接管了撤离工作。
senses.why: A role is something a person takes as his own. When the person's action belongs to the office he holds, he acts appropriately: the role and the conduct are one fit.
senses.whyCN: 角色是一个人认作自己的东西。当一个人的行为属于他所担任的职位，他就是 appropriately 行动：角色与举止合成一个贴合。

senses.title: Legally or officially proper: within the rules
senses.titleCN: 合乎规定：在规则之内
senses.definition: in accordance with the law, rules, or official procedure
senses.definitionCN: 依照法律、规则或正式程序
senses.example: The documents were appropriately filed with the court.
senses.exampleCN: 这些文件已按规定提交法院备案。
senses.why: What is proper to an institution is what its rules assign to each step. Acting appropriately here means following the procedure that belongs to the case, not merely being polite.
senses.whyCN: 属于一个机构的东西，就是它的规则分配给每个步骤的东西。这里的 appropriately 指遵循属于该案件的程序，而不只是礼貌。

senses.title: Right for the register: words that fit the audience
senses.titleCN: 措辞得体：语言贴合听众
senses.definition: of language, in a style or level of formality that suits the audience and setting
senses.definitionCN: 指语言，以适合听众与场合的风格或正式程度
senses.example: He appropriately avoided slang in the formal report.
senses.exampleCN: 他在正式报告里恰当地避开了俚语。
senses.why: A register is the language that belongs to a setting. Choosing appropriately is choosing the words that are proper to that room, so the social fit becomes a lexical one.
senses.whyCN: 语域是属于某个场合的语言。appropriately 选择，就是选择属于那个房间的词，于是社交上的贴合变成了用词上的贴合。

senses.title: At the right moment: sensible timing and judgment
senses.titleCN: 时机得当：明智的判断
senses.definition: at a fitting moment or in a sensible way, showing good judgment about when and how to act
senses.definitionCN: 在合适的时刻或以明智的方式，表现出对何时行动、如何行动的良好判断
senses.example: She appropriately waited until the meeting ended before raising the objection.
senses.exampleCN: 她恰当地等到会议结束后才提出异议。
senses.why: Timing is part of what belongs to an occasion: the right act at the wrong moment is not appropriate. The adverb therefore also judges when, fusing suitability with good sense.
senses.whyCN: 时机也是属于一个场合的东西：正确的行为放在错误的时刻就不恰当。因此这个副词也判断“何时”，把合适与明智融在一起。

intro.en: Appropriately is appropriate plus the adverb suffix -ly. The adjective comes from Latin appropriatus, the past participle of appropriare 'make one's own' — ad- 'to' plus proprius 'one's own'. The path runs from taking something as one's own, to setting it apart for a use, to being suitable for that use. Its root is proprius, not pretium (appreciate) and not proximus (approximate).
intro.cn: appropriately 是 appropriate 加副词后缀 -ly。appropriate 来自拉丁语 appropriatus，即 appropriare“使成为自己的”的过去分词——ad-“向”加 proprius“自己的”。路径是：把某物认作自己的 → 把它拨出来专供某用 → 与那用途相称。它的词根是 proprius，不是 appreciate 的 pretium，也不是 approximate 的 proximus。

items.en: The adjective appropriate is first recorded in English meaning 'specially suitable, proper', already carrying the fit-to-purpose sense.
items.cn: 形容词 appropriate 最早记录于英语，义为“特别合适的、恰当的”，已经带有“合乎目的”的意思。

items.en: Appropriate comes from Latin appropriatus, the past participle of appropriare 'make one's own'. The participle frames the word as 'having been made one's own'.
items.cn: appropriate 来自拉丁语 appropriatus，即 appropriare“使成为自己的”的过去分词。分词形式把这个词框定为“已经被认作自己的”。

items.en: Appropriare = ad- 'to' + proprius 'one's own' (the source of proper). To appropriate something is first to take it as your own, then to set it aside for a particular owner or use.
items.cn: appropriare = ad-“向”+ proprius“自己的”（也是 proper 的来源）。appropriate 某物，先是把它认作自己的，再把它拨给某个所有者或用途。

items.en: From 'make one's own' the sense moves to 'assign to a special use', and from there to 'fitting that use'. What belongs to a purpose is what suits it, so ownership turns into suitability.
items.cn: 从“使成为自己的”，词义转到“拨归专门用途”，再转到“与那用途相称”。属于某个目的的东西，就是适合它的东西，于是“所有权”变成了“合适”。

items.en: The English suffix -ly is added to the adjective to form an adverb of manner: suitable becomes 'in a suitable manner'. The suffix adds no new root meaning; it turns the fit into the way an action is done.
items.cn: 英语后缀 -ly 加在形容词后构成方式副词：suitable 变成“以合适的方式”。这个后缀不增加新的词根含义，只是把“相称”变成“行动的方式”。

items.en: Modern English uses appropriately for purpose, manners, context, degree, allocation, roles, rules, register and timing. The base appropriare never meant 'price' or 'nearest'; those belong to appreciate and approximate.
items.cn: 现代英语用 appropriately 表示合乎目的、礼数、情境、适度、分配、角色、规定、语域与时机。词源 appropriare 从来不表示“价格”或“最近”；那些属于 appreciate 与 approximate。

note.en: The first group puts the two false friends (pretium and proximus) beside a true relative; the second group separates appropriately from adverbs that cover only part of its range.
note.cn: 第一组把两个“假朋友”（pretium 与 proximus）放在一个真正的同族词旁边；第二组把 appropriately 与只覆盖其部分范围的副词分开。

entries.definition: to value, be grateful for, or rise in value. It comes from pretium 'price', a root entirely separate from proprius 'one's own'.
entries.definitionCN: 重视；感激；增值。它来自 pretium“价格”，与 proprius“自己的”是完全不同的一套词根。

entries.definition: close to the correct value but not exact. It comes from proximus 'nearest', the third look-alike root that must not be folded into this family.
entries.definitionCN: 接近正确值但不精确的。它来自 proximus“最近的”，是第三个形近词根，绝不能并进这个词族。

entries.definition: the act of setting money or property aside for a use, or of taking it as one's own. It is the noun from appropriate (v.), not the adverb.
entries.definitionCN: 拨款；拨用；挪用；据为己有。它是动词 appropriate 的名词形式，不是副词。

entries.definition: in a way that is right for a purpose or occasion. It is the broadest of the group; appropriately often adds social or moral propriety.
entries.definitionCN: 以适合某目的或场合的方式。它是这一组里最宽泛的；appropriately 往往还加上社交或道德上的得体。

entries.definition: in the correct, accepted, or polite way. It stresses rules and decorum, while appropriately stresses the fit between action and situation.
entries.definitionCN: 以正确、被接受或礼貌的方式。它强调规则与礼仪，而 appropriately 强调行为与情境之间的贴合。

entries.definition: in a way that is apt or becoming, often used of ceremonies and tributes. It is more formal and narrower than appropriately.
entries.definitionCN: 以恰当或相称的方式，常用于仪式与致意。它比 appropriately 更正式，范围也更窄。

normalIntro.en: These links are real: proprius 'one's own', the appropriare family, the adverb suffix -ly, and the fixed phrases appropriately dressed and appropriately named.
normalIntro.cn: 这些联想都是真实的：proprius“自己的”、appropriare 词族、副词后缀 -ly，以及 appropriately dressed、appropriately named 等固定搭配。

normal.en: Proprius means 'one's own'. Something appropriate has been made to belong to its purpose, so it fits.
normal.cn: proprius 意为“自己的”。appropriate 的东西已经被认作属于它的目的，因此是合适的。

normal.en: Appropriate is the adjective, -ly makes the adverb: 'suitable' becomes 'in a suitable manner'.
normal.cn: appropriate 是形容词，-ly 把它变成副词：“合适的”变成“以合适的方式”。

normal.en: Appropriately dressed and appropriately named are everyday frames: the clothes or the name matches the person or occasion.
normal.cn: appropriately dressed 与 appropriately named 是日常搭配：衣服或名字与人或场合相配。

normal.en: Appropriation is the noun for money set aside or property taken; it is not the adverb appropriately.
normal.cn: appropriation 是“拨出的款项”或“被占取的财产”的名词，不是副词 appropriately。

normal.en: Appropriately enough is a fixed sentence adverb meaning 'as was fitting', often used for something wryly predictable.
normal.cn: appropriately enough 是固定的句子副词，意为“果然恰如其分”，常用于略带讽刺的“不出所料”。

abstract.en: A key turns only in the lock made for it: the key is not merely good, it belongs to that lock. Appropriately is that one-lock fit.
abstract.cn: 一把钥匙只在为它打造的锁里转动：钥匙不只是好，它属于那把锁。appropriately 就是这种“一把锁的贴合”。

abstract.en: A suit cut for one body hangs badly on another: the same garment can be right here and wrong there.
abstract.cn: 为一个人的身材裁的西装，穿在另一个人身上就别扭：同一件衣服在此处合适，在别处就不合适。

abstract.en: The word judges three things at once: the act, the moment, and the company. Change any one and the fit may fail.
abstract.cn: 这个词同时判断三样东西：行为、时机与在场的人。改动任何一项，贴合都可能失效。

examples.en: She appropriately apologized before the argument could grow.
examples.cn: 在争吵升级之前，她适时地道了歉。

examples.en: The museum appropriately labels each object with its date and origin.
examples.cn: 博物馆恰当地为每件物品标上年代与来源。

examples.en: He was appropriately dressed for the cold chapel, in a heavy coat and gloves.
examples.cn: 他穿着厚外套、戴着手套，正适合那座寒冷的礼拜堂。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「阿普若普瑞特利」——阿普若（Ap-pro）挑了一件合身的礼服，普瑞（Pu Rui）帮他把领结扶正，特利（Te Li）说：这样出场才得体 → appropriately 合适地、得体地

root: 由 appropriate（源自拉丁语 appropriare“make one's own”，ad- + proprius“自己的”）加副词后缀 -ly 构成，核心是“使成为自己的→拨归专用→与目的相称”，故为合适地、恰当地。

sensesIntro.en: Nine senses of appropriately all measure one fit: an action and the purpose, occasion, role, rule, register or moment it belongs to. The adverb does not describe the action alone; it describes how well the action sits in its place.
sensesIntro.cn: appropriately 的九个义项都在衡量同一种贴合：一个行为与它所属的目的、场合、角色、规则、语域或时刻是否相配。这个副词不只描述行为本身，更描述行为在它的位置上坐得有多正。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a key that turns only in the lock made for it.
core.cn: 核心意象：一把只在为它打造的锁里转动的钥匙。

branches.en: PURPOSE AND CONTEXT: the action suits its task, then suits the changing situation.
branches.cn: 目的与情境：行为先合乎其任务，再合乎变化中的局面。

branches.en: SOCIAL AND LINGUISTIC MANNER: behavior proper to the room, and words proper to the audience.
branches.cn: 社交与语言方式：举止合乎这个房间，用词合乎这批听众。

branches.en: DEGREE AND ALLOCATION: the right share, and resources sent to their proper use.
branches.cn: 程度与分配：恰当的份额，以及资源被送到它该去的用途。

branches.en: ROLE AND RULE: conduct that fits an office, and procedure that fits the law.
branches.cn: 角色与规则：与职位相配的举止，以及与法律相配的程序。

branches.en: TIMING AND JUDGMENT: the right act at the right moment, which is part of the fit.
branches.cn: 时机与判断：正确的行为落在正确的时刻，这也是贴合的一部分。

intro.en: Appropriately is appropriate + -ly, an adverb-of-manner suffix with no root meaning of its own. Appropriate comes from appropriare; English then builds appropriateness, inappropriate, inappropriately, appropriation, misappropriate and misappropriation around the same proprius stem.
intro.cn: appropriately 是 appropriate 加 -ly，后者是构成方式副词的后缀，本身不带来词根含义。appropriate 来自 appropriare；英语随后围绕同一 proprius 词干构造出 appropriateness、inappropriate、inappropriately、appropriation、misappropriate 与 misappropriation。

latinIntro.en: Latin proprius 'one's own, proper' is the direct root. Appropriare 'make one's own' adds ad-, and its participle appropriatus gives the English adjective; proprietas gives the related noun of ownership.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语 proprius“自己的、专属的”是直接词根。appropriare“使成为自己的”加了 ad-，其分词 appropriatus 给出英语形容词；proprietas 给出表示所有权的相关名词。

items.meaning: in a fitting or proper way
items.meaningCN: 合适地；恰当地（-ly 构成方式副词）
items.example: The room was appropriately lit for the reading.
items.exampleCN: 这个房间为朗读会打上了恰当的光。

items.meaning: suitable or proper for a purpose
items.meaningCN: 合适的；恰当的（-ate 构成形容词）
items.example: Jeans are not appropriate for the ceremony.
items.exampleCN: 牛仔裤不适合这个仪式。

items.meaning: to set aside for a use, or take as one's own
items.meaningCN: 拨用；挪用；据为己有（同形动词）
items.example: The council appropriated funds for the new library.
items.exampleCN: 议会为新图书馆拨了款。

items.meaning: the quality of being suitable
items.meaningCN: 恰当；得体（-ness 构成状态名词）
items.example: They questioned the appropriateness of the joke.
items.exampleCN: 他们质疑这个笑话是否得体。

items.meaning: not suitable for the purpose or occasion
items.meaningCN: 不合适的；不得体的（in- 表示否定）
items.example: The comment was inappropriate for a public meeting.
items.exampleCN: 那句评论在公开会议上不合适。

items.meaning: in an unsuitable or improper way
items.meaningCN: 不恰当地；不得体地（-ly 构成副词）
items.example: He laughed inappropriately at the bad news.
items.exampleCN: 听到坏消息时，他不合时宜地笑了。

items.meaning: money set aside, or the taking of something as one's own
items.meaningCN: 拨款；拨用；挪用（-ion 构成动作名词）
items.example: The appropriation for road repairs was approved.
items.exampleCN: 道路维修的拨款获批了。

items.meaning: to take money or property dishonestly for one's own use
items.meaningCN: 挪用；侵吞（mis- 表示错误地、不正当地）
items.example: The treasurer misappropriated the club's funds.
items.exampleCN: 司库挪用了俱乐部的资金。

items.meaning: the dishonest taking of funds for one's own use
items.meaningCN: 挪用；侵吞（-ion 构成动作名词）
items.example: The audit revealed misappropriation of the grant.
items.exampleCN: 审计发现了这笔拨款的挪用。

items.meaning: a person who sets something aside or takes it as his own
items.meaningCN: 拨用者；占取者（-or 表示做该动作的人）
items.example: The appropriator of the land was later sued.
items.exampleCN: 占用这块土地的人后来被起诉了。

latinEntries.meaning: one's own, proper, peculiar to a person
latinEntries.meaningCN: 自己的；专属的；某人特有的

latinEntries.meaning: to make one's own, take as one's own
latinEntries.meaningCN: 使成为自己的；据为己有

latinEntries.meaning: made one's own, taken for a use
latinEntries.meaningCN: 已被认作自己的；已被拨用的

definition_zh: 近似；接近；近似值；粗略估算；逼近；近似物
definition_en: the act of coming close to something; a value, estimate, or model that is close to the true one but not exact; also a thing that resembles another
core_image: 一支箭落在靶心旁边：没有正中，但已经足够靠近
scene: An archer releases an arrow that lands a finger's width from the centre of the target, the coach marks the distance with a small ruler, and a scoreboard waits beside them. The coach calls the distance an approximation, not an exact measure.
sceneCN: 这里 approximation 是「近似、接近」（第 1 个义项：靠近某物或某个值的行为）；句意：教练说这段距离只是近似值，不是精确测量。图中可辨识物件：弓、箭、靶心、小尺、记分板。

pos.zh: 近似；接近；近似值；粗略估算；逼近

derivatives.zh: 近似的；大约的；接近；近似

senses.title: Coming near: the act of approaching
senses.titleCN: 靠近：接近某物的动作
senses.definition: the act of coming near or close to a place, thing, or value
senses.definitionCN: 靠近某个地点、事物或数值的行为
senses.example: The approximation of the storm forced the boats back to harbour.
senses.exampleCN: 风暴的逼近迫使船只返回港口。
senses.why: Latin approximare is ad- 'to' plus proximare 'come near', from proximus 'nearest'. The earliest English sense, recorded in the early 15th c., is simply the act of coming close.
senses.whyCN: 拉丁语 approximare 是 ad-“向”加 proximare“靠近”，后者出自 proximus“最近的”。英语最早的义项记录于 15 世纪早期，就是“靠近”这个动作。

senses.title: A value close to the truth: the near figure
senses.titleCN: 接近真值的数：近似值
senses.definition: a number, measurement, or result that is close to the true value but not exact
senses.definitionCN: 接近真实值但不精确的数字、测量或结果
senses.example: Pi to two decimals is the approximation 3.14.
senses.exampleCN: 圆周率保留两位小数，近似值是 3.14。
senses.why: From the act of coming near, the noun shifts to the result of that approach: a figure that has come close to the true value. The 1650s sense 'result of approximating' is exactly this landing point.
senses.whyCN: 名词从“靠近的动作”转到“靠近的结果”：一个已经接近真值的数字。17 世纪 50 年代出现的“近似的结果”义，正是这个落点。

senses.title: A rough estimate: close enough for the purpose
senses.titleCN: 粗略估算：够用就好
senses.definition: a rough calculation or estimate that is accepted because it is close enough for a practical purpose
senses.definitionCN: 为实际目的而接受的粗略计算或估计，因为已经足够接近
senses.example: A quick approximation put the crowd at three thousand.
senses.exampleCN: 快速估算一下，人群大约有三千人。
senses.why: The approach is deliberately not exact: you stop when you are near enough. Approximation here names the stopping point, not a failure to reach the target.
senses.whyCN: 这种靠近是刻意不精确的：够近就停下。这里的 approximation 命名的是这个停下的位置，而不是“没打中靶心”的失败。

senses.title: A near copy: something resembling another
senses.titleCN: 近似仿本：像，但不是原物
senses.definition: a thing that resembles another thing in appearance or character without being the same
senses.definitionCN: 在外观或性质上像另一物、但并不相同的东西
senses.example: The model is only an approximation of the real bridge.
senses.exampleCN: 这个模型只是真实桥梁的一个近似物。
senses.why: Two objects can come near each other in shape. The copy approaches the original without touching it, so approximation becomes resemblance rather than measurement.
senses.whyCN: 两个物件可以在形状上彼此靠近。仿本接近原作却没有重合，因此 approximation 从测量变成“相似之物”。

senses.title: Mathematical approximation: a curve that comes close
senses.titleCN: 数学逼近：曲线靠上目标
senses.definition: a mathematical expression or method that comes close to a value, curve, or function without equalling it
senses.definitionCN: 接近某个值、曲线或函数但不与之相等的数学表达式或方法
senses.example: The students used a straight line as an approximation to the curve.
senses.exampleCN: 学生们用一条直线作为这条曲线的近似。
senses.why: Here the approach is formalised: a simpler object is chosen because it comes near the true one. Approximation becomes a tool for replacing the hard exact object with a near one.
senses.whyCN: 这里的靠近被形式化了：选择一个更简单的对象，因为它接近真实对象。approximation 于是成为“用近似的对象替换难处理的精确对象”的工具。

senses.title: Numerical or statistical approximation: close by method
senses.titleCN: 数值或统计近似：用方法靠近
senses.definition: a result obtained by a numerical or statistical method that converges on, or estimates, a true value
senses.definitionCN: 通过数值或统计方法得到的、收敛到或估计出真值的结果
senses.example: The simulation's approximation improved with every extra round of sampling.
senses.exampleCN: 每增加一轮抽样，模拟的近似就更精确。
senses.why: The approach is now repeated by a procedure: each step brings the result nearer. Approximation names both the method's output and the closeness it achieves.
senses.whyCN: 这里的靠近由一套程序反复执行：每一步都把结果带得更近。approximation 既命名方法的输出，也命名它达到的接近程度。

senses.title: Approximation to a standard: nearing the target
senses.titleCN: 接近标准：朝指标靠拢
senses.definition: a state of coming close to a standard, norm, or desired level without fully reaching it
senses.definitionCN: 接近某个标准、规范或理想水平但尚未完全达到的状态
senses.example: The new engine's efficiency is a close approximation to the design target.
senses.exampleCN: 新发动机的效率已很接近设计目标。
senses.why: What is approached is now an abstract target. The word measures the gap that remains, so it can describe progress toward a norm rather than a number.
senses.whyCN: 此时被靠近的是一个抽象目标。这个词衡量仍然存在的差距，因此可以描述朝某个规范取得的进展，而不只是一个数字。

senses.title: A model close to reality: useful but not exact
senses.titleCN: 接近现实的模型：有用但不精确
senses.definition: a simplified model or description that is close enough to reality to be useful, while knowingly not exact
senses.definitionCN: 一种简化模型或描述，接近现实到足以有用，同时明知并不精确
senses.example: The economic model is an approximation that ignores migration.
senses.exampleCN: 这个经济模型是一个忽略了人口迁移的近似。
senses.why: A model approaches the world but never becomes the world. Approximation here names the accepted distance between a simplified account and the reality it describes.
senses.whyCN: 模型靠近世界，却永远不会变成世界。这里的 approximation 命名的是简化描述与被描述现实之间被接受的距离。

senses.title: The quality of being near but not identical
senses.titleCN: 近似性：接近但不相同
senses.definition: the quality or state of being close to something in value, form, or meaning without being identical to it
senses.definitionCN: 在数值、形式或意义上接近某物、但不完全相同的性质或状态
senses.example: The translation's approximation to the original is its greatest strength and its limit.
senses.exampleCN: 这份译文与原作的近似，既是它最大的优点，也是它的局限。
senses.why: The noun moves from countable results to an abstract quality: the degree of nearness itself. This is the latest and most general branch, where approximation means 'closeness without identity'.
senses.whyCN: 名词从可数的结果转到抽象性质：接近的程度本身。这是最晚、也最一般化的分支，approximation 在此意为“接近但不重合”。

intro.en: Approximation is an action noun in -ion, from Latin -ionem, naming an act or its result. It comes from Latin approximare 'come near to' — ad- 'to' plus proximare 'come near' — or from the English verb approximate. The root proximus is the superlative of prope 'near', so the whole word is built from nearness, not from price or ownership.
intro.cn: approximation 是带 -ion 的动作名词，-ion 来自拉丁语 -ionem，命名动作或其结果。它来自拉丁语 approximare“接近”——ad-“向”加 proximare“靠近”——或来自英语动词 approximate。词根 proximus 是 prope“近”的最高级，因此整个词建立在“近”上，而不是“价格”或“所有权”。

items.en: First recorded as approximacioun, 'act of coming near or close'. The earliest sense is physical or spatial approach, not numerical accuracy.
items.cn: 最早记录为 approximacioun，意为“靠近、接近的动作”。最早的义项是物理或空间上的接近，不是数值精度。

items.en: The noun is the action noun of approximate (v.), or is taken directly from Latin approximare. The suffix -ion marks the action or its result: the coming near, then the thing that has come near.
items.cn: 这个名词是动词 approximate 的动作名词，或直接取自拉丁语 approximare。后缀 -ion 标记动作或其结果：先是“靠近”，再是“已经靠近的东西”。

items.en: Approximare 'come near to' = ad- 'to' + proximare 'come near'. The prefix points the movement toward a target, so the verb means approach rather than mere proximity.
items.cn: approximare“接近”= ad-“向”+ proximare“靠近”。前缀把运动指向一个目标，因此这个动词是“朝……靠近”，而不只是“在旁边”。

items.en: Proximare comes from proximus 'nearest', the superlative of prope 'near'. The root is a ranking of nearness, which is why an approximation is the closest available figure rather than an exact one.
items.cn: proximare 来自 proximus“最近的”，即 prope“近”的最高级。这个词根是对“近”的排序，因此 approximation 是“可得到的最接近的数字”，而不是精确值。

items.en: The adjective approximate is recorded in the 1640s meaning 'near in position, close to', and the noun's sense 'result of approximating' in the 1650s.
items.cn: 形容词 approximate 记录于 17 世纪 40 年代，义为“位置上靠近的”；名词“近似的结果”义记录于 17 世纪 50 年代。

items.en: The sense 'near in accuracy or correctness' appears in 1816. This is the branch behind approximations to a true value, a standard, or a model of reality.
items.cn: “在准确度或正确性上接近”的义项出现于 1816 年。这就是“接近真值、标准或现实模型”的分支。

note.en: The first group puts approximation beside its own base and the two look-alike roots that must not be confused with it; the second group separates it from estimate, estimation and resemblance.
note.cn: 第一组把 approximation 放在它自己的基础词，以及两个绝不能与它混淆的形近词根旁边；第二组把它与 estimate、estimation、resemblance 分开。

entries.definition: close to the true value or position but not exact. It is the adjective and verb behind approximation, built on the same proximus root.
entries.definitionCN: 接近真实值或位置但不精确的。它是 approximation 背后的形容词与动词，建立在同一 proximus 词根上。

entries.definition: suitable or proper for a purpose. It comes from proprius 'one's own', not from proximus 'nearest', despite the similar opening.
entries.definitionCN: 适合某目的的；恰当的。它来自 proprius“自己的”，而不是 proximus“最近的”，尽管开头很像。

entries.definition: to value, be grateful for, or rise in value. It comes from pretium 'price', a third root that merely looks like the other two.
entries.definitionCN: 重视；感激；增值。它来自 pretium“价格”，是第三个只是看起来相似的词根。

entries.definition: a judgment of size, value, or amount based on evidence. An estimate need not be close to a known true value, while an approximation always suggests closeness.
entries.definitionCN: 依据证据对大小、价值或数量作出的判断。estimate 不一定接近已知真值，而 approximation 总含有“已经靠近”的意思。

entries.definition: the act of estimating, or a considered opinion of worth. It stresses judgment, while approximation stresses nearness to an exact value.
entries.definitionCN: 估算的行为，或经过考虑的价值判断。它强调判断，而 approximation 强调与精确值的接近。

entries.definition: the state of looking like someone or something else. It covers the 'near copy' branch, while approximation can also be numerical.
entries.definitionCN: 看起来像某人某物的状态。它覆盖“近似仿本”这一分支，而 approximation 还可以是数值上的。

normalIntro.en: These links are real: proximus 'nearest' and prope 'near', the ad- prefix, the -ion action noun, and the fixed phrases rough approximation and successive approximation.
normalIntro.cn: 这些联想都是真实的：proximus“最近的”与 prope“近”、ad- 前缀、-ion 动作名词，以及 rough approximation、successive approximation 等固定搭配。

normal.en: Prope is 'near' and proximus is 'nearest': approximation is the figure that has come nearest to the true one.
normal.cn: prope 是“近”，proximus 是“最近的”：approximation 就是已经最靠近真值的那个数字。

normal.en: Ad- means 'to': approximare is to move toward a target, so every approximation contains a direction of approach.
normal.cn: ad- 意为“向”：approximare 就是朝目标移动，因此每个 approximation 里都含有一个靠近的方向。

normal.en: Approximate is the adjective and verb; approximately is the adverb; approximation is the noun of the act or result.
normal.cn: approximate 是形容词和动词，approximately 是副词，approximation 是动作或结果的名词。

normal.en: A rough approximation and a first approximation are standard phrases: close enough to start, not close enough to finish.
normal.cn: a rough approximation 与 a first approximation 是标准说法：近到可以开始，但还没近到可以结束。

normal.en: Successive approximation is a real method: each attempt comes closer than the one before.
normal.cn: successive approximation 是一种真实的方法：每一次尝试都比上一次更靠近。

abstract.en: An arrow lands beside the bullseye: the score depends on how near, and the nearness is the whole point.
abstract.cn: 一支箭落在靶心旁边：得分取决于有多近，而“近”正是全部意义。

abstract.en: A staircase tries to follow a smooth curve: each step is flat and exact, yet the staircase only approximates the curve.
abstract.cn: 一段楼梯试图跟随一条光滑曲线：每级台阶都是平直而精确的，但整段楼梯只是曲线的近似。

abstract.en: A pencil sketch of a face: fewer lines than a photograph, yet near enough for you to recognise who it is.
abstract.cn: 一张人脸的铅笔速写：线条比照片少得多，却已经近到让你认得出那是谁。

examples.en: The figure is an approximation; the exact cost will be known after the survey.
examples.cn: 这个数字只是近似值；确切成本要等勘测之后才知道。

examples.en: Her description was a fair approximation of what we saw.
examples.cn: 她的描述相当接近我们所看到的情形。

examples.en: The method uses successive approximation to solve the equation.
examples.cn: 这种方法用逐次逼近来解方程。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「阿普若克西美申」——阿普若（Ap-pro）射出一箭，克西（Ke Xi）喊“差一点”，美申（Mei Shen）把箭拔下来又朝靶心靠近一步 → approximation 近似、接近

root: 源自拉丁语 approximare“接近”（ad-“向”+ proximare“靠近”，proximus“最近的”是 prope“近”的最高级），核心是“靠近”，再由空间接近引申为数值与判断上的近似。

sensesIntro.en: Nine senses of approximation all follow one movement: something comes near a target without landing on it. From physical approach and a near figure, the word extends to rough estimates, near copies, mathematical and numerical methods, standards, models, and finally the abstract quality of closeness.
sensesIntro.cn: approximation 的九个义项都遵循同一个动作：某物朝目标靠近，却没有落在目标上。从物理接近与一个接近的数字，它扩展到粗略估算、近似仿本、数学与数值方法、标准、模型，最后到抽象的“接近性”。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: an arrow landing beside the bullseye, close but not exact.
core.cn: 核心意象：一支箭落在靶心旁边，很近，但不正中。

branches.en: APPROACH AND RESULT: the act of coming near, and the near figure that results.
branches.cn: 靠近与结果：接近的动作，以及由此得到的接近数字。

branches.en: ROUGH ESTIMATE: closeness accepted because it is enough for the purpose.
branches.cn: 粗略估算：因为够用而被接受的接近。

branches.en: NEAR COPY: resemblance, where one object comes near another in form.
branches.cn: 近似仿本：相似，一个物件在形态上靠近另一个。

branches.en: FORMAL METHODS: curves, functions and procedures that converge on a true value.
branches.cn: 形式方法：曲线、函数与程序朝真值收敛。

branches.en: STANDARDS, MODELS AND QUALITY: nearing a target, modelling reality, and closeness as such.
branches.cn: 标准、模型与性质：靠近目标、模拟现实，以及“接近”本身。

intro.en: Approximation is approximat- plus -ion, from Latin -ionem, an action-or-result noun. The same stem gives approximate, approximately, approximative, approximator and approximated; the bare proxim- root lives on in proximity and proximate.
intro.cn: approximation 是 approximat- 加 -ion，后者来自拉丁语 -ionem，构成动作或结果名词。同一词干给出 approximate、approximately、approximative、approximator 与 approximated；光秃的 proxim- 词根仍活在 proximity 与 proximate 中。

latinIntro.en: The direct source is Latin approximare, ad- plus proximare 'come near'. Proximare comes from proximus 'nearest', the superlative of prope 'near'; English proximity keeps the same proximus stem.
latinIntro.cn: 直接来源是拉丁语 approximare，即 ad- 加 proximare“靠近”。proximare 来自 proximus“最近的”，即 prope“近”的最高级；英语 proximity 保留同一 proximus 词干。

items.meaning: the act of coming near, or a near value or model
items.meaningCN: 近似；接近；近似值（-ion 构成动作或结果名词）
items.example: The map is only an approximation of the coast.
items.exampleCN: 这幅地图只是海岸线的一个近似。

items.meaning: to come near, or close to the true value
items.meaningCN: 接近；近似的（-ate 构成动词或形容词）
items.example: The repair will approximate two hundred dollars.
items.exampleCN: 维修费大约要两百美元。

items.meaning: about; near a stated figure
items.meaningCN: 大约；近似地（-ly 构成副词）
items.example: The trip takes approximately three hours.
items.exampleCN: 这段行程大约需要三小时。

items.meaning: of the nature of an approximation; not exact
items.meaningCN: 近似的；接近的（-ive 构成形容词）
items.example: The study offers only an approximative answer.
items.exampleCN: 这项研究只给出一个近似的答案。

items.meaning: a person or device that produces approximations
items.meaningCN: 近似者；近似计算装置（-or 表示做该动作的人或物）
items.example: The software acts as a curve approximator.
items.exampleCN: 这个软件起到曲线逼近器的作用。

items.meaning: estimated or brought close to a value
items.meaningCN: 被近似的；估算出的（-ed 构成形容词）
items.example: The approximated cost was still too high.
items.exampleCN: 估算出的成本仍然太高。

items.meaning: nearness in space or time
items.meaningCN: 接近；邻近（-ity 构成状态名词）
items.example: The house's proximity to the river worried the owners.
items.exampleCN: 这房子离河太近，让房主担心。

items.meaning: nearest in space, time, or cause
items.meaningCN: 最近的；直接的（-ate 构成形容词）
items.example: The proximate cause of the fire was a faulty wire.
items.exampleCN: 火灾的直接原因是一根故障电线。

items.meaning: able to be approximated or estimated closely
items.meaningCN: 可逼近的；可近似估算的（-able 表示能够被……的）
items.example: The function is approximable by a short series.
items.exampleCN: 这个函数可以用一个短级数逼近。
