senses.title: Relating to the study of ancient material remains
senses.titleCN: 与古代实物遗存研究有关
senses.definition: relating to the scientific study of past human societies through the objects, structures, and traces they left behind
senses.definitionCN: 与通过古人留下的器物、建筑与痕迹来科学研究过去人类社会有关
senses.example: The valley is protected as an archaeological zone.
senses.exampleCN: 这个山谷被划为考古保护区。
senses.why: Greek arkhaiologia joins archaeo- 'ancient' and -logy 'study'. The adjective adds -ical, so it names whatever belongs to that study: its methods, its sites, its evidence.
senses.whyCN: 希腊语 arkhaiologia 由 archaeo-“古老的”与 -logy“研究”组成。形容词再加 -ical，因此它命名一切属于这门研究的东西：方法、遗址、证据。

senses.title: Pertaining to the remains themselves
senses.titleCN: 指遗存本身：地下的器物与痕迹
senses.definition: of or concerning the physical remains of past human activity, rather than the written account of it
senses.definitionCN: 指或关于过去人类活动的实物遗存，而非关于它的书面记述
senses.example: Archaeological evidence shows that the village burned twice.
senses.exampleCN: 考古证据表明这个村庄曾两次被烧毁。
senses.why: The study and its objects are named as one: what archaeologists deal with becomes 'archaeological material'. The adjective shifts from the discipline to the things that feed it.
senses.whyCN: 研究与研究对象被用同一个名字：考古学家处理的东西成了“考古材料”。形容词从学科转到喂养这门学科实物。

senses.title: Belonging to ancient history as a subject
senses.titleCN: 属于作为学科对象的古代史
senses.definition: in the older sense, relating to the written or literary study of ancient history, before archaeology became a field science
senses.definitionCN: 较早的义项：与古代史的书写或文献研究有关，那时考古学尚未成为田野科学
senses.example: In 1700, an archaeological lecture was a lecture on ancient history, not on a dig.
senses.exampleCN: 在 1700 年，一场“考古学”讲座其实是古代史讲座，而不是关于发掘的讲座。
senses.why: Archaeology entered English c.1600 meaning 'ancient history'. The adjective could therefore describe bookish ancient history, long before the 1825 sense of a scientific study of peoples and civilizations.
senses.whyCN: archaeology 约 1600 年进入英语时意为“古代史”。因此这个形容词可以描述书斋式的古代史研究，远早于 1825 年才出现的“对民族与文明进行科学研究”的义项。

senses.title: Relating to field excavation
senses.titleCN: 与田野发掘有关
senses.definition: relating to the practical work of excavating, recording, and interpreting a site layer by layer
senses.definitionCN: 与逐层发掘、记录和解读遗址的实地工作有关
senses.example: The archaeological dig was closed during the rainy season.
senses.exampleCN: 考古发掘在雨季暂停了。
senses.why: A study of ancient things must go to the ground to find them. The adjective attaches to the trowel, the trench and the layer, so 'archaeological' becomes fieldwork rather than library work.
senses.whyCN: 对古老事物的研究必须下到地里去找它们。形容词于是附着在铲子、探方与地层上，archaeological 也从书斋工作变成田野工作。

senses.title: Belonging to the academic discipline
senses.titleCN: 属于这门学科：系、课程与专业
senses.definition: relating to archaeology as an academic department, degree, or profession
senses.definitionCN: 与作为大学院系、学位或职业的考古学有关
senses.example: She is writing an archaeological thesis on coastal trade.
senses.exampleCN: 她正在写一篇关于沿海贸易的考古学论文。
senses.why: Once the study is organised into departments and degrees, its adjective marks membership: an archaeological thesis, an archaeological society. The root is the same; the referent is now the institution.
senses.whyCN: 当这门研究被组织成院系与学位，它的形容词就标记归属：考古学论文、考古学会。词根未变，所指变成了机构。

senses.title: Relating to a period or region: classical archaeology
senses.titleCN: 属于某一时期或地区：古典考古学
senses.definition: relating to a branch of the discipline defined by a period, region, or culture, such as classical or prehistoric archaeology
senses.definitionCN: 与按时期、地区或文化划分的学科分支有关，如古典考古学或史前考古学
senses.example: Classical archaeological methods differ from those used on prehistoric camps.
senses.exampleCN: 古典考古的方法与用于史前营地的方法不同。
senses.why: The modifier narrows 'ancient' to one stretch of the ancient past. The adjective still says 'of the study', but the study is now bounded by a period or a map.
senses.whyCN: 修饰语把“古老”收窄到古代中的某一段。形容词仍表示“属于这门研究”，只是这门研究被时期或地图圈定了。

senses.title: Relating to industrial remains
senses.titleCN: 与工业遗存有关：工业考古
senses.definition: relating to the study of factories, machines, and infrastructure from the industrial age, often standing or still in use
senses.definitionCN: 与对工业时代的工厂、机器与基础设施的研究有关，这些遗存常仍矗立或仍在使用
senses.example: An archaeological survey of the mill recorded every gear and chimney.
senses.exampleCN: 对这座工厂的考古调查记录了每一个齿轮和烟囱。
senses.why: The method of reading objects, not the age of the objects, defines the adjective. Industrial remains can be studied with the same layer-by-layer discipline, so 'archaeological' extends to the recent past.
senses.whyCN: 定义这个形容词的是“读实物”的方法，而不是实物的年代。工业遗存也能用同样的逐层方法研究，因此 archaeological 延伸到了近现代。

senses.title: Relating to submerged sites: underwater archaeology
senses.titleCN: 与沉没遗址有关：水下考古
senses.definition: relating to the study of shipwrecks, drowned settlements, and other remains lying under water
senses.definitionCN: 与对沉船、被淹没的聚落及其他水下遗存的研究有关
senses.example: Underwater archaeological work mapped the wreck before anything was lifted.
senses.exampleCN: 水下考古工作在打捞任何东西之前先测绘了沉船。
senses.why: The ancient thing is now under water, but the same 'study of ancient things' applies. The adjective travels with the method into a new environment.
senses.whyCN: 古老的东西现在在水下，但“对古老事物的研究”仍然适用。形容词随方法进入了新的环境。

senses.title: Metaphorical: digging through layers of thought
senses.titleCN: 隐喻用法：挖掘思想的层层堆积
senses.definition: used figuratively of an inquiry that uncovers the hidden layers and assumptions beneath a system of ideas
senses.definitionCN: 比喻性地指一种探究，揭开某个观念体系下面隐藏的层次与前提
senses.example: The book offers an archaeological reading of modern medicine.
senses.exampleCN: 这本书对现代医学做了一种考古学式的解读。
senses.why: The discipline's signature move is removing layer after layer to expose what lies beneath. Applied to ideas, archaeology becomes a metaphor for tracing how a system was built up, as in an archaeology of knowledge.
senses.whyCN: 这门学科的标志动作是一层层去掉覆盖物，露出下面的东西。把它用到观念上，archaeology 就成为追溯一个体系如何层层堆积起来的隐喻，如“知识考古学”。

intro.en: Archaeological is archaeology plus -ical. Archaeology is Greek arkhaiologia 'the study of ancient things': archaeo-, from arkhaios 'ancient', plus -logy, from -logia 'study'. Arkhaios itself comes from arkhē 'beginning'. The -ical ending is -ic plus -al, a compound adjective suffix. The archaeo- element means 'ancient' and has nothing to do with archi- 'chief' in architectural.
intro.cn: archaeological 是 archaeology 加 -ical。archaeology 来自希腊语 arkhaiologia“对古老事物的研究”：archaeo- 出自 arkhaios“古老的”，-logy 出自 -logia“研究”。arkhaios 本身出自 arkhē“开端”。-ical 结尾是 -ic 加 -al 的复合形容词后缀。archaeo- 成分意为“古老”，与 architectural 中 archi-“首席”毫无关系。

items.en: Greek arkhaiologia meant 'the study of ancient things'. It joined archaeo-, from arkhaios 'ancient', with -logia 'study, discourse'.
items.cn: 希腊语 arkhaiologia 意为“对古老事物的研究”。它把出自 arkhaios“古老的”的 archaeo- 与 -logia“研究、论述”结合起来。

items.en: Arkhaios 'ancient' derives from arkhē 'beginning': the ancient is what belongs to the beginning. The second element is -logy, the study of a subject.
items.cn: arkhaios“古老的”出自 arkhē“开端”：古老之物就是属于开端的东西。第二个成分是 -logy，即对某主题的研究。

items.en: English archaeology first meant 'ancient history', borrowed from French archéologie (16c.) or directly from Greek. It was a bookish term, not yet a field science.
items.cn: 英语 archaeology 最初意为“古代史”，借自 16 世纪法语 archéologie，或直接借自希腊语。它是个书斋词，还不是田野科学。

items.en: Only in 1825 does archaeology come to mean the scientific study of ancient peoples and civilizations through their remains.
items.cn: 直到 1825 年，archaeology 才指通过遗存对古代民族与文明进行的科学研究。

items.en: Archaeologic is recorded in 1731 and archaeological in 1766, both built on archaeology. The ending -ical is -ic plus -al: -ic makes the relational adjective, -al completes and stabilises it.
items.cn: archaeologic 记录于 1731 年，archaeological 记录于 1766 年，二者都建立在 archaeology 上。结尾 -ical 是 -ic 加 -al：-ic 构成关系形容词，-al 补足并稳定它。

items.en: Modern branches such as classical, industrial and underwater archaeology all keep the same elements. Only the modifier changes; archaeo- still means 'ancient', while archi- in architectural is Greek arkhi- 'chief'.
items.cn: 古典考古、工业考古、水下考古等现代分支都保留同样的成分。变的只是修饰语；archaeo- 仍指“古老”，而 architectural 里的 archi- 是希腊语 arkhi-“首席”。

note.en: The first group contains one true root-alike and two traps: architectural has archi- 'chief', while archaic shares the ancient root but not the discipline. The second group separates archaeology from neighbouring studies.
note.cn: 第一组包含一个真正同根的词和两个陷阱：architectural 里的 archi- 是“首席”，archaic 虽共享“古老”词根却不指这门学科。第二组把考古学与邻近学科分开。

entries.definition: relating to architecture or building design. Its archi- comes from Greek arkhi- 'chief', not from archaeo- 'ancient'.
entries.definitionCN: 与建筑或建筑设计有关的。它的 archi- 来自希腊语 arkhi-“首席”，不是 archaeo-“古老”。

entries.definition: very old or old-fashioned, often deliberately so. It shares arkhaios 'ancient' but describes age or style, not the study of remains.
entries.definitionCN: 古老的；过时的，常指刻意仿古。它共享 arkhaios“古老的”，但描述年代或风格，而不是对遗存的研究。

entries.definition: a person who studies ancient remains. It is archaeology plus -ist, so it names the practitioner rather than the adjective.
entries.definitionCN: 研究古代遗存的人。它是 archaeology 加 -ist，命名从业者，而不是形容词。

entries.definition: the study of human societies and cultures, including living peoples. Archaeology is one branch of it when remains are the main evidence.
entries.definitionCN: 对人类社群与文化的研究，也包括在世的人群。当主要证据是遗存时，考古学是它的一个分支。

entries.definition: the study of ancient life through fossils. It deals with organisms, while archaeology deals with human material remains.
entries.definitionCN: 通过化石研究古代生命。它处理生物，而考古学处理人类的实物遗存。

entries.definition: the study of the past based mainly on written documents. Archaeology works from objects and traces, especially where no texts survive.
entries.definitionCN: 主要依据书面文献对过去的研究。考古学从器物与痕迹入手，尤其在无文字留存的地方。

normalIntro.en: These links are real: Greek archaeo- 'ancient' and -logy 'study', the 1731/1766 -ic then -ical formation, and the fixed phrases archaeological site and archaeological evidence.
normalIntro.cn: 这些联想都是真实的：希腊语 archaeo-“古老”与 -logy“研究”、1731／1766 年先 -ic 后 -ical 的构词，以及 archaeological site、archaeological evidence 等固定搭配。

normal.en: Archaeo- is 'ancient', -logy is 'study': archaeology is the study of ancient things, and archaeological is everything belonging to it.
normal.cn: archaeo- 是“古老”，-logy 是“研究”：archaeology 是对古老事物的研究，archaeological 则属于这门研究的一切。

normal.en: Arkhaios comes from arkhē 'beginning', so the ancient is literally what belongs to the beginning.
normal.cn: arkhaios 出自 arkhē“开端”，所以“古老的”字面上就是“属于开端的”。

normal.en: Archaeologic came first in 1731, archaeological in 1766: -ical is simply -ic plus -al.
normal.cn: archaeologic 先在 1731 年出现，archaeological 在 1766 年出现：-ical 不过是 -ic 加 -al。

normal.en: Archaeological site and archaeological evidence are the standard frames: a place to dig and the objects that speak.
normal.cn: archaeological site 与 archaeological evidence 是标准搭配：一个可供发掘的地方，以及会说话的器物。

normal.en: Architectural has archi- 'chief', not archaeo- 'ancient': an architect is a chief builder, not a student of ruins.
normal.cn: architectural 里的 archi- 是“首席”，不是 archaeo-“古老”：建筑师是首席建造者，不是废墟研究者。

abstract.en: A trowel removes one thin layer at a time: the past is read from the top down, and each layer is younger than the one below.
abstract.cn: 一把铲子每次刮掉薄薄一层：过去要从上往下读，每一层都比下面那层年轻。

abstract.en: A grid of strings divides the ground into squares: the same ancient thing can be located precisely by its square and depth.
abstract.cn: 用绳子把地面分成方格：同一件古物可以靠它的方号与深度被精确定位。

abstract.en: Broken pots are fitted back together: archaeology rebuilds a whole society from fragments that were never meant to be a message.
abstract.cn: 破碎的陶罐被拼回原形：考古学用从未打算传递信息的碎片，重建整个社会。

examples.en: The archaeological team found a wall under the car park.
examples.cn: 考古队在停车场下面发现了一道墙。

examples.en: Archaeological evidence suggests the harbour silted up slowly.
examples.cn: 考古证据表明这个港口是慢慢淤塞的。

examples.en: She joined an archaeological survey of the old iron works.
examples.cn: 她加入了对那座旧铁厂的考古调查。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「阿凯奥勒吉扣」——阿凯（Ar-chae）在奥勒（O-le）的土层里一层层挖，吉扣（Ji Kou）把碎片拼成一只古碗 → archaeological 考古的

root: 源自希腊语 arkhaiologia“对古老事物的研究”：archaeo-（arkhaios“古老的”，出自 arkhē“开端”）+ -logy（-logia“研究”）；archaeological 是 archaeology + -ical。

sensesIntro.en: Nine senses of archaeological all hang on one act: removing layers to expose what ancient people left. From the discipline and its remains, the word extends to ancient history, field excavation, academic departments, period branches, industrial and underwater work, and finally to the metaphor of digging through ideas.
sensesIntro.cn: archaeological 的九个义项都挂在同一个动作上：揭开层层覆盖，让古人留下的东西露出来。从学科与遗存，它扩展到古代史、田野发掘、大学院系、分期分支、工业与水下工作，最后到“挖掘观念”的隐喻。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a trowel lifting one thin layer of soil from a marked square.
core.cn: 核心意象：一把小铲从划好的方格中刮起薄薄一层土。

branches.en: DISCIPLINE AND INSTITUTION: the study itself, and its departments, degrees and professions.
branches.cn: 学科与机构：研究本身，以及它的院系、学位与职业。

branches.en: REMAINS AND FIELDWORK: the objects that are studied, and the digging that finds them.
branches.cn: 遗存与田野：被研究的器物，以及找到它们的发掘工作。

branches.en: ANCIENT HISTORY: the earliest bookish sense, before archaeology became a field science.
branches.cn: 古代史：最早的、书斋式的义项，在考古学成为田野科学之前。

branches.en: PERIOD AND WATER: branches narrowed by a period or a region, including submerged sites.
branches.cn: 分期与水下：被时期或地区收窄的分支，包括沉没遗址。

branches.en: INDUSTRY AND METAPHOR: recent remains read like ancient ones, and ideas read like layers of soil.
branches.cn: 工业与隐喻：近现代遗存像古代遗存一样被阅读，观念则像土层一样被阅读。

intro.en: Archaeological is archaeology + -ical, where -ical is the compound of -ic and -al that makes a relational adjective. Archaeology joins archaeo- 'ancient' and -logy 'study'. The same archaeo- stem gives archaeologist, archaeometry, bioarchaeology, archaeobotany, archaic and archaism.
intro.cn: archaeological 是 archaeology 加 -ical，其中 -ical 是 -ic 与 -al 复合而成的关系形容词后缀。archaeology 由 archaeo-“古老”与 -logy“研究”组合。同一 archaeo- 词干给出 archaeologist、archaeometry、bioarchaeology、archaeobotany、archaic 与 archaism。

latinIntro.en: The word is Greek in origin, but New Latin coined archaeologia from the Greek compound, and Latin archaismus gave English archaism. Latin architectura is listed only to show the contrast: its archi- is 'chief', not 'ancient'.
latinIntro.cn: 这个词源于希腊语，但新拉丁语用希腊复合词造出 archaeologia，拉丁语 archaismus 则给出英语 archaism。列入拉丁语 architectura 只为显示对照：它的 archi- 是“首席”，不是“古老”。

items.meaning: relating to the study of ancient material remains
items.meaningCN: 考古学的；考古的（-ical 构成关系形容词）
items.example: The archaeological record is thin in that valley.
items.exampleCN: 那个山谷的考古记录很单薄。

items.meaning: the study of ancient peoples through their remains
items.meaningCN: 考古学（archaeo-“古老”+ -logy“研究”）
items.example: Archaeology depends on careful recording.
items.exampleCN: 考古学依赖细致的记录。

items.meaning: a person who studies ancient remains
items.meaningCN: 考古学家（-ist 表示从事该学科的人）
items.example: The archaeologist brushed the soil away by hand.
items.exampleCN: 考古学家用手刷去泥土。

items.meaning: from an archaeological point of view
items.meaningCN: 从考古学角度；在考古方面（-ly 构成副词）
items.example: The area is archaeologically unexplored.
items.exampleCN: 这个地区在考古上尚未被勘探。

items.meaning: the scientific measurement and analysis of archaeological materials
items.meaningCN: 考古测量学；科技考古（-metry 表示测量）
items.example: Archaeometry dated the pottery to 1200 BCE.
items.exampleCN: 科技考古把这批陶器定年在公元前 1200 年。

items.meaning: the study of human and animal remains from archaeological sites
items.meaningCN: 生物考古学（bio-“生命”+ archaeology）
items.example: Bioarchaeology can reveal diet and disease.
items.exampleCN: 生物考古学能揭示饮食与疾病。

items.meaning: the study of plant remains from archaeological sites
items.meaningCN: 植物考古学（archaeo-“古老”+ botany“植物学”）
items.example: Archaeobotany found seeds of an early wheat.
items.exampleCN: 植物考古学发现了早期小麦的种子。

items.meaning: very old or old-fashioned
items.meaningCN: 古老的；过时的（-ic 构成形容词）
items.example: The poem uses archaic spellings.
items.exampleCN: 这首诗使用了古旧的拼写。

items.meaning: an old word or style kept deliberately
items.meaningCN: 古语词；仿古风格（-ism 表示做法或体系）
items.example: The legal text is full of archaisms.
items.exampleCN: 这份法律文本满是古语词。

items.meaning: the art of designing buildings
items.meaningCN: 建筑学；建筑（archi- 是“首席”，与 archaeo-“古老”不同）
items.example: The architecture of the museum is stark and white.
items.exampleCN: 这座博物馆的建筑风格素净而洁白。

latinEntries.meaning: the study of ancient things, ancient history
latinEntries.meaningCN: 对古老事物的研究；古代史

latinEntries.meaning: the art of building; listed to show the different archi- root
latinEntries.meaningCN: 建筑术；列出以显示不同的 archi- 词根

definition_zh: 考古学家；通过发掘和解读古代遗存来研究古代社会的人
definition_en: a person who studies ancient societies and cultures by excavating and interpreting their material remains
core_image: 探方底部，一个人跪着用毛刷拂去陶片上的沙土
scene: An archaeologist kneels at the bottom of a desert trench, brushing sand from a broken pot while a tape measure, a record sheet and labelled sample bags wait beside her.
sceneCN: 这里 archaeologist 是「在遗址现场清理并记录古代遗存的人」（第 1 个义项：田野考古工作者）；句意：一位考古学家跪在沙漠探方底部，用毛刷拂去碎陶罐上的沙土，身旁放着卷尺、记录表和贴好标签的样品袋。图中可辨识物件：探方、毛刷、碎陶罐、卷尺、标签袋、记录表。

collocations.phrase: the archaeologist in charge of the dig
collocations.zh: 发掘工作的负责考古学家

derivatives.zh: 从考古学角度；以考古方法
古物研究者（1820 年前后的旧称）
古物研究者（1839 年自法语传入的旧称）

senses.title: The digger at a site: field archaeologist
senses.titleCN: 遗址现场的发掘者：田野考古学家
senses.definition: a person who excavates a site, recording the position and context of every find
senses.definitionCN: 在遗址进行发掘、记录每件出土物位置与层位关系的人
senses.example: The archaeologist stopped the digger when a row of post holes appeared in the trench.
senses.exampleCN: 探方里出现一排柱洞时，考古学家叫停了挖掘机。
senses.why: The -ist marks the person and the base archaeology marks ancient things. The most concrete place where those things are read is a trench, so the bare noun first calls up the digger at the site.
senses.whyCN: -ist 标记“人”，词基 archaeology 标记“古代之物”。阅读这些古物最具体的场所就是探方，因此这个名词最先让人想到遗址上的发掘者。

senses.title: The university scholar: academic archaeologist
senses.titleCN: 学院里的研究者：学术考古学家
senses.definition: a researcher or professor who interprets material remains in a laboratory and teaches the discipline
senses.definitionCN: 在实验室解读遗存、并教授这门学科的研究者或教授
senses.example: The archaeologist published a reanalysis of the pottery from the 1930s excavation.
senses.exampleCN: 这位考古学家重新分析了 20 世纪 30 年代那次发掘出土的陶器。
senses.why: Away from the trench the same skill becomes a university post: the person still reads material remains, but now through microscopes, catalogues and seminars rather than a trowel.
senses.whyCN: 离开探方后，同一种本领变成大学里的职位：这个人仍在解读遗存，只是改用显微镜、目录和研讨课，而不是手铲。

senses.title: The antiquary: the older collector-scholar
senses.titleCN: 古物研究者：更早的收藏型学者
senses.definition: historically, a scholar or collector devoted to old objects and antiquities rather than to systematic excavation
senses.definitionCN: 历史上指热衷于古物与古董的学者或收藏者，而非系统发掘者
senses.example: In 1800 the word for such a man was antiquary, not archaeologist.
senses.exampleCN: 在 1800 年，这类人的称呼是 antiquary，而不是 archaeologist。
senses.why: Greek arkhaiologos meant 'antiquary', one who talks about ancient things. The modern -ist inherited that scholarly curiosity before excavation became its defining act.
senses.whyCN: 希腊语 arkhaiologos 意为“古物研究者”，即谈论古代之物的人。现代 -ist 继承了这份好古的学术兴趣，后来发掘才成为其标志性动作。

senses.title: The diver: underwater archaeologist
senses.titleCN: 潜水者：水下考古学家
senses.definition: a specialist who excavates and records shipwrecks and submerged settlements
senses.definitionCN: 发掘并记录沉船与水下聚落的专家
senses.example: The archaeologist mapped the amphora pile before lifting a single jar.
senses.exampleCN: 考古学家先把双耳罐堆绘制成图，才起吊其中一只罐子。
senses.why: Water is only another matrix that hides remains. The -ist still reads ancient things, but the trench is now the seabed and the tools include sonar and diving gear.
senses.whyCN: 水只是另一种掩埋遗存的介质。-ist 仍在阅读古代之物，只是探方变成了海床，工具里多了声呐和潜水装备。

senses.title: The grave reader: forensic archaeologist
senses.titleCN: 读墓者：法医考古学家
senses.definition: a specialist who applies excavation and stratigraphic methods to crime scenes and buried human remains
senses.definitionCN: 把发掘与地层方法用于犯罪现场和埋葬遗骸的专家
senses.example: A forensic archaeologist recovered the buried evidence layer by layer.
senses.exampleCN: 一位法医考古学家一层一层地提取了埋藏的物证。
senses.why: A buried body is treated exactly as material remains: position, depth and surrounding objects all matter. The archaeologist's layer-by-layer recovery is therefore borrowed by law enforcement.
senses.whyCN: 埋藏的人体被完全当作遗存处理：位置、深度和周围物件都有意义。于是考古学家逐层提取的本领被执法部门借用。

senses.title: The rescuer: salvage and contract archaeologist
senses.titleCN: 抢救者：抢救性与商业考古学家
senses.definition: a professional hired to record remains before construction or erosion destroys the site
senses.definitionCN: 在施工或侵蚀毁掉遗址之前受雇记录遗存的专业人员
senses.example: The archaeologist had six weeks to record the site before the road was built.
senses.exampleCN: 修路之前，这位考古学家只有六周时间记录遗址。
senses.why: Construction cuts through layers that took centuries to form. The same reader of remains is called in before they go, so curiosity turns into salvage under a deadline.
senses.whyCN: 施工会切穿数百年才形成的地层。同一位遗存阅读者被抢在遗存消失前请来，于是好古之心变成了有期限的抢救工作。

senses.title: The regional specialist: archaeologist of Egypt or Rome
senses.titleCN: 区域专家：埃及或罗马考古学家
senses.definition: a scholar whose work is confined to one region, period or civilisation
senses.definitionCN: 研究范围限定在某一地区、时期或文明的学者
senses.example: She is an archaeologist of the Roman frontier rather than of the whole empire.
senses.exampleCN: 她研究的是罗马边疆，而不是整个帝国。
senses.why: The base noun can be narrowed by a region or period. The person is still an archaeologist; only the slice of ancient material that counts as 'the ancient things' is fixed.
senses.whyCN: 词基可以被地区或时期收窄。这个人仍是 archaeologist，只是被当作“古代之物”的那一片材料被固定下来了。

senses.title: The satellite reader: space archaeologist
senses.titleCN: 看卫星图的人：太空考古学家
senses.definition: a researcher who uses satellite and aerial imagery to detect buried sites without excavating them
senses.definitionCN: 利用卫星与航空影像发现地下遗址、而不必实地发掘的研究者
senses.example: The space archaeologist found a lost canal from a single satellite image.
senses.exampleCN: 这位太空考古学家从一张卫星图里发现了一条消失的运河。
senses.why: Satellite images become the surface layer. The archaeologist reads traces of ancient settlement from above, so the trench is replaced by pixels but the reading of remains stays the same.
senses.whyCN: 卫星图像成了新的“地表层”。考古学家从高空读取古代聚落的痕迹，探方被像素取代，但“读遗存”这件事没有变。

senses.title: The figurative digger: digital or software archaeologist
senses.titleCN: 比喻的挖掘者：数字或软件考古学家
senses.definition: a person who reconstructs obsolete systems, old code or forgotten data by patiently working through their surviving layers
senses.definitionCN: 耐心梳理残存层次、重建过时系统、旧代码或被遗忘数据的人
senses.example: A software archaeologist rebuilt the program from fragments on old disks.
senses.exampleCN: 一位软件考古学家用旧磁盘上的碎片重建了这个程序。
senses.why: Old code and dead formats are layers too: each version sits on top of the last. The word is used figuratively for anyone who excavates the stored remains of technology.
senses.whyCN: 旧代码和消亡的格式也是地层：每个版本都压在上一版之上。这个词被比喻性地用于任何挖掘技术遗存的人。

senses.title: The public teller: museum and community archaeologist
senses.titleCN: 面向公众的讲述者：博物馆与社区考古学家
senses.definition: a professional who presents finds to the public, curates displays, or works with local communities to interpret a site
senses.definitionCN: 向公众展示出土物、策划陈列，或与当地社区合作解读遗址的专业人员
senses.example: The archaeologist turned the excavation into a weekend walking tour.
senses.exampleCN: 这位考古学家把发掘现场变成了周末步行导览。
senses.why: The same reader of remains now translates them for people who will never enter a trench. The -ist still marks the person, but the work moves from recovery to explanation.
senses.whyCN: 同一位遗存阅读者，如今为永远不会进入探方的人做翻译。-ist 仍标记“人”，但工作从提取转向解释。

intro.en: Archaeologist is a 19c coinage, not an ancient Greek job title. It was built inside English from archaeology plus the agent suffix -ist, and excavation only later became its defining activity.
intro.cn: archaeologist 是 19 世纪新造的职业名词，不是古希腊既有的头衔。它是在英语内部由 archaeology 加施事后缀 -ist 构成的，发掘后来才成为这一职业的标志性活动。

items.en: First recorded in 1824, formed from archaeology + -ist. This is the settled modern term for the person.
items.cn: 最早记录于 1824 年，由 archaeology + -ist 构成。这是最终定型的现代人称名词。

items.en: Earlier variants competed: archaeologian is recorded in 1820, and archaeologue in 1839, the latter from French archéologue.
items.cn: 更早的异形曾相互竞争：archaeologian 记录于 1820 年，archaeologue 记录于 1839 年，后者来自法语 archéologue。

items.en: Greek arkhaiologos meant 'antiquary', a person who studied or collected ancient things, from arkhaios 'ancient' + logos 'word, reason'. It was not a field scientist.
items.cn: 希腊语 arkhaiologos 意为“古物研究者”，即研究或收集古代之物的人，由 arkhaios“古老的”+ logos“言说、理性”构成；它并不是田野科学家。

items.en: The -ist in archaeologist goes back to Greek -istēs 'one who does', through Latin -ista and French -iste. It attaches to the name of the activity, here archaeology.
items.cn: archaeologist 中的 -ist 可追到希腊语 -istēs“从事某事的人”，经拉丁语 -ista 与法语 -iste 传入。它附着在活动名称之后，这里接的是 archaeology。

items.en: As archaeology became a scientific discipline in the 19c, the -ist form fixed on the person who digs, records and interprets, and the older antiquary sense faded.
items.cn: 19 世纪考古学成为一门科学学科，-ist 形式固定指“发掘、记录并解读遗存的人”，较早的古物研究者含义随之淡化。

items.en: Underwater, forensic, contract, space and software archaeology all extend the same person-noun without changing its structure.
items.cn: 水下、法医、抢救性、太空与软件考古都只是延伸同一个人称名词，并未改变其结构。

note.en: The first group collects spellings and neighbours that sound or look close; the second collects people whose work is often confused with the archaeologist's.
note.cn: 第一组是读音或拼写相近的词；第二组是工作常与考古学家混淆的人。

entries.definition: The American simplified spelling of the same word. It drops the ae of archaeology but names exactly the same profession.
entries.definitionCN: 同一个词的美国简化拼写：省去 archaeology 中的 ae，但指的完全是同一职业。

entries.definition: The discipline itself. The -ist form is the person; the -logy form is the field.
entries.definitionCN: 学科本身。-ist 形式指人，-logy 形式指领域。

entries.definition: A keeper of archives. It looks like archaeologist but is built on archives, not on archaeology.
entries.definitionCN: 档案保管员。它看起来像 archaeologist，但词基是 archives，而不是 archaeology。

entries.definition: A student of human societies in general, including living ones. Archaeology is one of its subfields, not a synonym.
entries.definitionCN: 泛指研究人类社会（包括现存社会）的人。考古学只是它的一个分支，不是同义词。

entries.definition: A collector or scholar of old objects. It matches the older sense of archaeologist, before excavation defined the job.
entries.definitionCN: 古物收藏者或研究者。它对应 archaeologist 较早的含义，那时发掘尚未定义这一职业。

entries.definition: A scholar who works mainly from written documents. The archaeologist works mainly from physical remains.
entries.definitionCN: 主要依据文字文献的学者。考古学家主要依据实物遗存。

normalIntro.en: These links are real: the -ist agent suffix, the archaeology base, the Greek antiquary sense, and the documented early variants.
normalIntro.cn: 这些联想都是真实的：-ist 施事后缀、archaeology 词基、希腊语“古物研究者”义，以及有据可查的早期异形。

normal.en: Split it as archaeology + -ist: the field plus the person. Any -logy word can take -logist the same way.
normal.cn: 拆成 archaeology + -ist：学科加人。任何以 -logy 结尾的词都能同样加 -logist 表示从业者。

normal.en: The three common jobs are the trench digger, the laboratory scholar and the underwater diver.
normal.cn: 三种常见身份是探方发掘者、实验室学者和水下潜水者。

normal.en: Before 1824 the same idea was carried by arkhaiologos 'antiquary', and by the English tries archaeologian and archaeologue.
normal.cn: 1824 年以前，同一概念由 arkhaiologos“古物研究者”承载，英语也试过 archaeologian 与 archaeologue。

normal.en: An archaeologist reads what other people walked over: a post hole is a house, a seed is a meal, a slag heap is a workshop.
normal.cn: 考古学家能读别人踩过的东西：一个柱洞是一间房，一粒种子是一顿饭，一堆矿渣是一间作坊。

normal.en: Contract archaeology is the everyday job: recording a site before a road or pipeline destroys it.
normal.cn: 商业考古是日常工作中最常见的一种：在道路或管线毁掉遗址前把它记录下来。

abstract.en: Think of a reader kneeling at the bottom of a square hole, turning sand into sentences.
abstract.cn: 想象一位读者跪在方形土坑底部，把沙土读成句子。

abstract.en: The trowel removes a layer, the brush removes a grain: the method is patience directed at what others threw away.
abstract.cn: 手铲去掉一层，毛刷去掉一粒：这套方法就是把耐心对准别人丢弃的东西。

abstract.en: The archaeologist is the person who arrives after everyone has left and asks what their hands were doing.
abstract.cn: 考古学家是在所有人都离开之后才到场，却追问“他们的手当时在做什么”的人。

examples.en: The archaeologist spent the morning photographing the trench before anyone moved a bucket.
examples.cn: 考古学家花了一上午给探方拍照，然后才让人移动任何一只土桶。

examples.en: A forensic archaeologist can read a shallow grave the way others read a map.
examples.cn: 法医考古学家读一座浅墓，就像别人读一张地图。

examples.en: The museum hired an archaeologist to identify the pottery shards donated by a local farmer.
examples.cn: 博物馆聘请了一位考古学家来鉴定当地农民捐赠的陶片。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「阿凯奥勒吉」——阿凯蹲在探方里，一层一层奥勒吉地刷土，终于刷出一块陶片 → archaeologist 考古学家

root: 由 archaeology + -ist 构成，1824 年首次记录；archaeo- 出自希腊 arkhaios“古老的”，-ist 出自希腊 -istēs“从事者”。

sensesIntro.en: Ten senses of archaeologist all keep one role: a person who reads ancient material remains. The setting changes from trench to laboratory, seabed, grave, road project, satellite image, obsolete software and finally the public gallery.
sensesIntro.cn: archaeologist 的十个义项都保留同一个角色：阅读古代实物遗存的人。场景从探方换到实验室、海床、墓葬、筑路工地、卫星图像、过时软件，最后换到面向公众的展厅。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a person kneeling in a square trench, reading ancient remains layer by layer.
core.cn: 核心意象：一个人跪在方形探方里，一层一层地阅读古代遗存。

branches.en: THE CORE JOB: the field digger and the academic interpreter share one skill in two settings.
branches.cn: 核心职业：田野发掘者与学院解读者，是同一本领的两种场景。

branches.en: THE OLDER ROLE: the antiquary, who collected and discussed old things before excavation defined the job.
branches.cn: 较早的角色：古物研究者，在发掘定义职业之前收集并谈论古物的人。

branches.en: THE MEDIUM CHANGES: seabed and satellite image replace the trench, but the reading of remains continues.
branches.cn: 介质改变：海床与卫星图像取代探方，但读遗存的工作继续。

branches.en: THE URGENT CASES: graves and road projects, where evidence must be recovered before it is lost.
branches.cn: 紧迫情形：墓葬与筑路工程，证据必须在消失前被提取。

branches.en: THE NARROWED AND THE FIGURATIVE: one region or period, or one obsolete system, becomes the site.
branches.cn: 收窄与比喻：一个地区或时期，或一个过时系统，成为新的“遗址”。

intro.en: Archaeologist is transparently built: archaeo- 'ancient' + -logy 'study' + -ist 'person who does'. English merely stacks a Greek-rooted noun and a Greek agent suffix, then adds further suffixes for adjectives and adverbs.
intro.cn: archaeologist 的构造很透明：archaeo-“古老”+ -logy“研究”+ -ist“从事者”。英语只是把一个希腊词根名词和一个希腊施事后缀叠加，再加别的后缀构成形容词和副词。

latinIntro.en: The parts reached English through Latin and French: Greek arkhaios and logos became Latin archaeologia and French archéologie before -ist was added in English. The agent suffix itself arrived as Latin -ista from Greek -istēs.
latinIntro.cn: 这些成分经由拉丁语和法语进入英语：希腊语 arkhaios 与 logos 先变成拉丁语 archaeologia 和法语 archéologie，然后英语才加上 -ist。施事后缀本身则由希腊语 -istēs 经拉丁语 -ista 传入。

items.meaning: the study of ancient societies through material remains
items.meaningCN: 考古学：通过实物遗存研究古代社会（-logy 构成学科名词）
items.example: Archaeology reconstructs daily life from refuse and foundations.
items.exampleCN: 考古学从垃圾与地基重建日常生活。

items.meaning: relating to archaeology or its methods
items.meaningCN: 考古学的；考古方法的（-ical 构成形容词）
items.example: The site has no archaeological value without its layers.
items.exampleCN: 没有地层，这个遗址就没有考古价值。

items.meaning: by archaeological methods or from an archaeological point of view
items.meaningCN: 以考古方法；从考古学角度（-ly 构成副词）
items.example: The valley is archaeologically almost unknown.
items.exampleCN: 这个山谷在考古学上几乎无人了解。

items.meaning: an older word for a student of antiquities
items.meaningCN: 古物研究者的旧称（-ian 构成人称名词）
items.example: The 1820 writer called himself an archaeologian.
items.exampleCN: 那位 1820 年的作者自称 archaeologian。

items.meaning: a student of antiquities, especially in 19c French usage
items.meaningCN: 古物研究者，尤其见于 19 世纪法语用法（-logue 表示言说者或研究者）
items.example: The French archaeologue catalogued the collection.
items.exampleCN: 那位法国古物研究者给藏品编了目。

items.meaning: the application of scientific dating and measurement to archaeological material
items.meaningCN: 考古测年学；科技考古（-metry 表示测量）
items.example: Archaeometry dated the charcoal to 1200 BCE.
items.exampleCN: 科技考古把木炭年代定在公元前 1200 年。

items.meaning: the study of human and animal remains within archaeological contexts
items.meaningCN: 生物考古学：研究考古情境中的人与动物遗骸
items.example: Bioarchaeology can read diet from bones.
items.exampleCN: 生物考古学能从骨骼读出饮食。

items.meaning: the archaeological study of animal remains
items.meaningCN: 动物考古学：对动物遗存的考古研究
items.example: Zooarchaeology identified the fish as a river species.
items.exampleCN: 动物考古学鉴定出那种鱼是河鱼。

latinEntries.meaning: ancient, old, belonging to the beginning
latinEntries.meaningCN: 希腊语形容词：古老的、旧的、属于开端的

latinEntries.meaning: beginning, origin, first place; also rule or office
latinEntries.meaningCN: 希腊语名词：开端、起源、首位；也指统治或官职
希腊语名词：言词、言说、理性、说明

latinEntries.meaning: one who does or practices something
latinEntries.meaningCN: 希腊语施事后缀：从事或实践某事的人

definition_zh: 考古学；对古代社会实物遗存的系统研究；也指某地或某问题的遗存整体
definition_en: the systematic study of ancient societies through their material remains; also the body of remains and the field of study relating to a particular place or question
core_image: 一面剖开的土壁，层层色带里嵌着陶片、炭屑和墙基
scene: A student draws a section of a trench wall where three coloured layers, a row of stones and a charcoal band are pinned with small labels. The archaeology of the trench wall shows three phases of rebuilding.
sceneCN: 这里 archaeology 是「以地层与遗存为证据的研究」（第 5 个义项：地层的解读）；句意：对探方壁的考古解读显示出三个重建阶段。图中可辨识物件：探方壁、地层色带、陶片、炭屑、石块、标签、绘图板。

collocations.zh: 该遗址的考古遗存与研究

senses.title: The discipline: studying ancient societies from things
senses.titleCN: 学科：用实物研究古代社会
senses.definition: the academic discipline that reconstructs ancient societies from their material remains, recorded in this sense from 1825
senses.definitionCN: 从实物遗存重建古代社会的学科，此义记录于 1825 年
senses.example: Archaeology can describe a diet even when no recipe survives.
senses.exampleCN: 即使没有食谱流传下来，考古学也能描述一种饮食。
senses.why: The Greek compound already means 'account of ancient things'. In 1825 that account became a scientific discipline with excavation, stratigraphy and classification, so the word settled on the modern field.
senses.whyCN: 这个希腊语复合词本就意为“关于古代之物的论述”。1825 年，这种论述结合发掘、地层学与分类成为科学学科，词义于是固定为现代学科。

senses.title: Ancient history: the earliest English sense
senses.titleCN: 古代史：最早的英语义项
senses.definition: the study of ancient history as a branch of learning, the sense recorded about 1600
senses.definitionCN: 作为一门学问的古代史研究，此义约记录于 1600 年
senses.example: In 1600 archaeology meant ancient history read from books, not from trenches.
senses.exampleCN: 在 1600 年，archaeology 指的是从书本而非探方中读出的古代史。
senses.why: Before fieldwork existed, the word named the written account of ancient times. It was a library subject: arkhaios 'ancient' plus logos 'account'. Excavation was not yet part of the picture.
senses.whyCN: 在田野工作出现之前，这个词指对古代的文字记述，是一门书房里的学问：arkhaios“古老”+ logos“论述”。发掘尚未进入这幅画。

senses.title: The material record itself: what a place has left
senses.titleCN: 遗存整体：一个地方留下的实物记录
senses.definition: the collective body of physical remains at a place, treated as the object of study
senses.definitionCN: 某一地点实物遗存的总和，被当作研究对象
senses.example: The archaeology of the valley consists of field walls, wells and pottery scatters.
senses.exampleCN: 这个山谷的考古遗存包括田埂、水井和散落的陶片。
senses.why: Metonymy turns the study into the thing studied: the discipline named by -logy comes to stand for the whole set of remains that the discipline reads.
senses.whyCN: 转喻让“研究”变成了“被研究对象”：由 -logy 命名的学科，转而指这门学科所阅读的全部遗存。

senses.title: The field project: a site's excavation programme
senses.titleCN: 田野项目：一个遗址的发掘计划
senses.definition: an organised excavation or survey at a particular site, often named by its purpose or funder
senses.definitionCN: 在特定遗址组织的发掘或调查，常以目的或出资方命名
senses.example: The rescue archaeology began before the new bypass was cut through the field.
senses.exampleCN: 在新绕城公路穿过田野之前，抢救性考古就开始了。
senses.why: Once the discipline is organised into projects, its name transfers to the work on the ground. Rescue archaeology makes the transfer explicit: the study becomes the urgent digging.
senses.whyCN: 当学科被组织成项目，它的名称就转移到地面上的工作。rescue archaeology 把这个转移说得最明白：研究变成了紧急发掘。

senses.title: The reading of layers: stratigraphic evidence
senses.titleCN: 地层的解读：层位证据
senses.definition: the interpretation of superimposed deposits and their relationships as a record of time
senses.definitionCN: 把叠压的堆积及其相互关系解读为时间记录
senses.example: The archaeology of the trench wall showed three phases of rebuilding.
senses.exampleCN: 对探方壁的考古解读显示出三个重建阶段。
senses.why: The core image is a cut through layered soil. Each layer is a page and each object has a position on that page, so archaeology comes to mean reading time from vertical order.
senses.whyCN: 核心意象是切开的分层土壤。每一层都是一页，每件器物在这页上都有位置，因此 archaeology 也指从垂直顺序中读出时间。

senses.title: The archaeology of knowledge: digging through ideas
senses.titleCN: 知识考古学：挖掘观念的地层
senses.definition: a figurative use, especially after Foucault, for tracing the hidden layers and rules behind a body of knowledge
senses.definitionCN: 一种比喻用法，尤其自福柯之后，指追溯一套知识背后的隐藏层次与规则
senses.example: The book offers an archaeology of the idea of madness rather than a history of hospitals.
senses.exampleCN: 这本书提供的是一种“疯狂”观念的考古学，而不是医院史。
senses.why: If ideas accumulate in layers like soil, then the discipline's method can be applied to thought itself. The trench becomes an archive of discourse, and the archaeologist becomes the theorist.
senses.whyCN: 如果观念像土壤一样层层堆积，那么这门学科的方法就能用于思想本身。探方变成话语的档案库，考古学家变成理论家。

senses.title: Digital archaeology: recovering old systems
senses.titleCN: 数字考古：打捞旧系统
senses.definition: the recovery and study of obsolete software, hardware and digital data
senses.definitionCN: 对过时软件、硬件与数字数据的抢救与研究
senses.example: Digital archaeology rescued the files from a 1980s word processor.
senses.exampleCN: 数字考古从一台 1980 年代的文字处理机里救回了文件。
senses.why: Old formats stack up like strata: each operating system buries the last. The word extends because the task is the same, namely recovering meaning from abandoned material.
senses.whyCN: 旧格式像地层一样堆叠：每个操作系统都埋掉上一个。这个词因此扩展，因为任务相同，都是从被废弃的材料中打捞意义。

senses.title: Space archaeology: reading sites from orbit
senses.titleCN: 太空考古：从轨道读取遗址
senses.definition: the use of satellite and aerial imagery to find and map buried or invisible sites
senses.definitionCN: 利用卫星与航空影像发现并测绘埋藏或不可见遗址
senses.example: Space archaeology revealed a road grid beneath the sand.
senses.exampleCN: 太空考古揭示了沙层之下的一张道路网格。
senses.why: A satellite sees the surface as one vast layer. The same reading of traces is done from above, so the discipline's name follows its method into orbit.
senses.whyCN: 卫星把地表看成一整层巨大的地层。同样的读痕工作改从高空进行，学科名称便随方法进入轨道。

senses.title: Industrial archaeology: the remains of machines
senses.titleCN: 工业考古：机器的遗存
senses.definition: the study of industrial buildings, machinery and landscapes from the recent past
senses.definitionCN: 对近代工业建筑、机械与景观的研究
senses.example: Industrial archaeology recorded the mill before it was converted into flats.
senses.exampleCN: 工厂改建成公寓之前，工业考古对它做了记录。
senses.why: The method does not care how old the layer is. Factories, canals and railway sheds are recent deposits, yet they are still read from standing structures and refuse, so the discipline extends to industrial remains.
senses.whyCN: 这套方法并不在意地层有多古老。工厂、运河和铁路棚是较晚的堆积，却仍可从 standing structures 与废弃物中读取，因此学科延伸到工业遗存。

senses.title: Experimental archaeology: rebuilding in order to understand
senses.titleCN: 实验考古：通过重建来理解
senses.definition: the branch of archaeology that tests interpretations by recreating tools, buildings or processes
senses.definitionCN: 通过重建工具、建筑或工艺来检验解释的考古分支
senses.example: Experimental archaeology rebuilt the kiln and fired a batch of pots in it.
senses.exampleCN: 实验考古重建了那座窑，并在里面烧制了一批陶罐。
senses.why: A claim about how something was made can be tested by making it again. The discipline's name extends to reconstruction because remains are read by reproducing them, not only by digging them.
senses.whyCN: 关于“某物如何被制作”的判断，可以通过再做一次来检验。学科名称因此延伸到重建，因为遗存不只靠挖出来读，也靠复制出来读。

intro.en: Archaeology is a Greek compound, not a Latin one: archaeo- comes from arkhaios 'ancient', and -logy from -logia 'study'. It must not be confused with archi- 'chief' in architect. English first used it for ancient history about 1600 and only in 1825 for the scientific study of ancient peoples.
intro.cn: archaeology 是希腊语复合词，不是拉丁语复合词：archaeo- 来自 arkhaios“古老的”，-logy 来自 -logia“研究”。切不可与 architect 中表示“首席”的 archi- 相混。英语约在 1600 年先用它指古代史，直到 1825 年才指对古代民族的科学研究。

items.en: First recorded about 1600 in the sense 'ancient history', a subject of study rather than a field method.
items.cn: 约 1600 年首次记录，义为“古代史”，是一门研习科目，而不是田野方法。

items.en: From French archéologie (16c.) or directly from Greek arkhaiologia 'the study of ancient things'. The French and Greek forms supplied the same compound.
items.cn: 来自法语 archéologie（16 世纪），或直接来自希腊语 arkhaiologia“对古代之物的研究”。法语与希腊语提供的是同一个复合词。

items.en: arkhaios 'ancient' derives from arkhē 'beginning', and -logia 'study' derives from logos 'word, reason'. So the literal frame is 'account of the ancient'.
items.cn: arkhaios“古老的”出自 arkhē“开端”，-logia“研究”出自 logos“言词、理性”。因此字面框架是“关于古代之物的论述”。

items.en: The archaeo- of archaeology is not the archi- of architecture. Arkhi- means 'chief, first in rank'; arkhaios means 'old, of the beginning'. The two Greek stems look alike in English but belong to different compounds.
items.cn: archaeology 的 archaeo- 不是 architecture 的 archi-。arkhi- 意为“首席、位次第一”；arkhaios 意为“古老的、属于开端的”。两个希腊词干在英语里形似，却属于不同的复合词。

items.en: The modern sense 'scientific study of ancient peoples and civilisations' is recorded in 1825, alongside the rise of excavation and stratigraphy.
items.cn: “对古代民族与文明的科学研究”这一现代义记录于 1825 年，与发掘和地层学的兴起同步。

items.en: The 20c and later added underwater, industrial, space, digital and media archaeology, all using the same 'read the remains' frame.
items.cn: 20 世纪及以后又出现水下、工业、太空、数字与媒介考古，全部沿用同一个“阅读遗存”的框架。

note.en: The first group separates spelling variants and the dangerous archi- neighbour from the word itself; the second separates disciplines that also study the human past.
note.cn: 第一组区分拼写变体、以及危险的 archi- 邻词；第二组区分同样研究人类过去的学科。

entries.definition: The simplified American spelling. It is the same word and the same discipline, with ae reduced to e.
entries.definitionCN: 美国简化拼写：同一个词、同一门学科，只是把 ae 缩写成 e。

entries.definition: The art of building. Its archi- means 'chief', not 'ancient'; it comes from arkhi- + tekton 'builder', not from arkhaios.
entries.definitionCN: 建筑艺术。它的 archi- 意为“首席”，不是“古老”；来自 arkhi- + tekton“建造者”，并非来自 arkhaios。

entries.definition: The person who practices archaeology. The -ist form changes the discipline into its practitioner.
entries.definitionCN: 从事考古学的人。-ist 形式把学科变成从业者。

entries.definition: The study of human societies, including living ones. Archaeology is one of its four classic branches.
entries.definitionCN: 研究人类社会（包括现存社会）的学科。考古学是其四大经典分支之一。

entries.definition: The study of the past based mainly on written documents. Archaeology works mainly from physical remains.
entries.definitionCN: 主要依据文字文献研究过去。考古学主要依据实物遗存。

entries.definition: The study of fossil animals and plants. It shares the -logy and the digging, but its subject is ancient life, not human society.
entries.definitionCN: 研究动植物化石的学科。它与考古学共享 -logy 和挖掘，但对象是古代生物，不是人类社会。

normalIntro.en: The links are structural: archaeo- 'ancient', -logy 'study', and the deliberate contrast with archi- 'chief' in architecture.
normalIntro.cn: 这些联想是结构性的：archaeo-“古老”、-logy“研究”，以及与 architecture 中 archi-“首席”的刻意对照。

normal.en: archaeo- = ancient, -logy = study. The word literally offers 'the study of ancient things'.
normal.cn: archaeo- = 古老，-logy = 研究。这个词字面上就是“对古代之物的研究”。

normal.en: Keep architecture apart: archi- means chief, tekton means builder. An architect is a chief builder, not an old builder.
normal.cn: 把 architecture 分开记：archi- 意为首席，tekton 意为建造者。architect 是“首席建造者”，不是“古老的建造者”。

normal.en: The 1600 sense was ancient history; the 1825 sense was excavation-based science. The date marks the shift.
normal.cn: 1600 年的义项是古代史；1825 年的义项是以发掘为基础的科学。年代标记了这次转变。

normal.en: Read a trench wall as a page: layer, object, position. That is archaeology in one image.
normal.cn: 把探方壁当一页书读：层、物、位置。这就是 archaeology 的一幅图。

normal.en: Every new subfield keeps the verb 'read': underwater, industrial, space, digital and media archaeology all read remains.
normal.cn: 每个新分支都保留“读”这个动作：水下、工业、太空、数字与媒介考古都在读遗存。

abstract.en: Time drawn as a stack of coloured bands: the past is not behind us but under us, in order.
abstract.cn: 把时间画成一摞彩色条带：过去不在我们身后，而在我们脚下，并且有顺序。

abstract.en: A broken cup is not rubbish but a sentence: the archaeologist supplies the grammar of layer and association.
abstract.cn: 一只破杯子不是垃圾，而是一个句子：考古学家提供“层位与共存关系”这套语法。

abstract.en: The same reading can be turned on ideas, code or factories: anywhere traces accumulate in layers, archaeology can follow.
abstract.cn: 同一套读法可以转向观念、代码或工厂：凡是痕迹层层堆积之处，考古学都能跟进。

examples.en: Archaeology depends on context: a pot on a shelf tells far less than a pot in a floor.
examples.cn: 考古学依赖情境：架子上的罐子远不如地板中的罐子说明问题。

examples.en: She switched from history to archaeology because she wanted to handle the evidence herself.
examples.cn: 她从历史学转向考古学，因为她想亲手处理证据。

examples.en: The archaeology of this valley is being destroyed by illegal digging.
examples.cn: 这个山谷的考古遗存正被非法盗掘破坏。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「阿基奥乐记」——阿基在土壁前奥乐记地一层层记下颜色和陶片 → archaeology 考古学

root: 希腊语复合词：archaeo- 出自 arkhaios“古老的”（源于 arkhē“开端”），-logy 出自 -logia“研究”（源于 logos“言词、理性”）；约 1600 年指古代史，1825 年定为科学研究。

sensesIntro.en: Ten senses of archaeology grow from one act: reading time from layered remains. The discipline, its early 'ancient history' sense, the remains themselves, a field project, a trench section, and then figurative, technical or experimental extensions all keep that act.
sensesIntro.cn: archaeology 的十个义项都从一个动作生长出来：从分层遗存中读出时间。学科、早期的“古代史”义、遗存本身、田野项目、探方剖面，以及后来的比喻、技术与实验延伸，都保留这个动作。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a cut through layered soil, each band holding objects that date it.
core.cn: 核心意象：切开的分层土壤，每条色带里都藏着能定年的器物。

branches.en: FROM SUBJECT TO SCIENCE: ancient history as a library subject became a field discipline in 1825.
branches.cn: 从科目到科学：作为书房科目的古代史，在 1825 年变成田野学科。

branches.en: THE THING AND THE WORK: the remains themselves, and the organised project that recovers them.
branches.cn: 物与工作：遗存本身，以及把它发掘出来的有组织项目。

branches.en: THE METHODS: stratigraphy reads vertical order, and experimental reconstruction tests a reading by remaking the object.
branches.cn: 方法：地层学读取垂直顺序，实验性重建则通过重做器物来检验解读。

branches.en: FIGURATIVE DIGGING: ideas and obsolete software are read as if they were layers.
branches.cn: 比喻性挖掘：观念与过时软件被当作地层来读。

branches.en: NEW SURFACES: orbit and the industrial landscape become the site.
branches.cn: 新的表面：轨道与工业景观成为遗址。

intro.en: Archaeology is archaeo- 'ancient' + -logy 'study'. Both parts are Greek and both are still productive: bioarchaeology and zooarchaeology add a prefix, while archaeometry swaps -logy for -metry. The archi- of architecture is a different stem and must be kept apart.
intro.cn: archaeology 是 archaeo-“古老”+ -logy“研究”。两部分都来自希腊语，且仍有构词力：bioarchaeology 与 zooarchaeology 加前缀，archaeometry 则把 -logy 换成 -metry。architecture 的 archi- 是另一词干，必须分开。

latinIntro.en: The route was Greek arkhaiologia to French archéologie and then English archaeology. Greek arkhaios and logos reached English through Latin and French forms, which is why the spelling has ae where Greek had ai.
latinIntro.cn: 路径是希腊语 arkhaiologia → 法语 archéologie → 英语 archaeology。希腊语 arkhaios 与 logos 经由拉丁语和法语形式进入英语，因此拼写里用 ae 对应希腊语的 ai。

items.meaning: a person who studies ancient remains
items.meaningCN: 考古学家（-ist 表示从业者）
items.example: The archaeologist recorded every find in a notebook.
items.exampleCN: 考古学家把每件出土物都记在本子上。

items.meaning: relating to archaeology
items.meaningCN: 考古学的（-ical 构成形容词）
items.example: The area was declared an archaeological reserve.
items.exampleCN: 该地区被宣布为考古保护区。

items.meaning: by archaeological means or from an archaeological view
items.meaningCN: 以考古方法；从考古角度（-ly 构成副词）
items.example: The cave is archaeologically sterile.
items.exampleCN: 这个洞穴在考古上没有发现。

items.meaning: an older term for a scholar of antiquities
items.meaningCN: 古物研究者的旧称（-ian 构成人称名词）
items.example: The society still called its curator an archaeologian.
items.exampleCN: 该学会仍把馆藏主管叫作 archaeologian。

items.meaning: a student of antiquities, from French archéologue
items.meaningCN: 古物研究者，来自法语 archéologue（-logue 表示言说或研究者）
items.example: The archaeologue compared the two coin hoards.
items.exampleCN: 这位古物研究者比较了两批钱币窖藏。

items.meaning: scientific measurement and dating of archaeological material
items.meaningCN: 考古测年学；科技考古（-metry 表示测量）
items.example: Archaeometry placed the eruption in the 17th century BCE.
items.exampleCN: 科技考古把这次喷发定在公元前 17 世纪。

items.meaning: archaeological study of biological remains
items.meaningCN: 生物考古学：对生物遗存的考古研究
items.example: Bioarchaeology read arthritis from the joint surfaces.
items.exampleCN: 生物考古学从关节面读出了关节炎。

items.meaning: archaeological study of animal remains
items.meaningCN: 动物考古学：对动物遗存的考古研究
items.example: Zooarchaeology showed that the herd was kept for milk.
items.exampleCN: 动物考古学表明这群牲畜是用于产奶的。

items.meaning: the study of old media technologies and their survival
items.meaningCN: 媒介考古学：研究旧媒介技术及其留存
items.example: Media archaeology examines the gramophone as a dead format.
items.exampleCN: 媒介考古学把留声机当作一种消亡的格式来考察。

definition_en: relating to architecture, to the design of buildings, or to the structure of a building or system

scene: An architect's desk holds a blueprint weighted by a wooden ruler; pencil lines trace an arch, a column and a roof beam. The blueprint on the desk is an architectural drawing.

senses.title: Relating to building design: the professional core
senses.titleCN: 与建筑设计有关：职业核心义
senses.definition: relating to the art and practice of designing buildings, recorded from 1759
senses.definitionCN: 与设计建筑的艺术和实践有关，此义记录于 1759 年
senses.example: The competition rewarded architectural design rather than engineering cost.
senses.exampleCN: 竞赛看重的是建筑设计，而不是工程造价。
senses.why: Architectural is architecture + -al, and architecture is the art of building. The suffix turns the discipline into an adjective, so the first sense names whatever belongs to the designer's art.
senses.whyCN: architectural 是 architecture + -al，而 architecture 是建筑的艺术。后缀把学科变成形容词，因此第一义指属于设计者技艺的一切。

senses.title: Of a building: built according to design principles
senses.titleCN: 建筑物的：按建筑原理建造的
senses.definition: of a structure, built or judged according to the principles of architecture, a sense recorded from the 1610s for architecture itself
senses.definitionCN: 指建筑物按建筑原理建造或评价，该义在 1610s 已见于 architecture
senses.example: The shed is useful but has no architectural quality at all.
senses.exampleCN: 这间棚屋很实用，却毫无建筑品质。
senses.why: The adjective transfers from the art to its product. A building is architectural when it can be judged by the art's rules, not merely when it stands up.
senses.whyCN: 形容词从“艺术”转移到“产物”。一座建筑之所以是 architectural，是因为能用建筑学的规则来评判它，而不只是因为它立得住。

senses.title: Of a style or period: Gothic, Baroque, modern
senses.titleCN: 风格或时期的：哥特式、巴洛克式、现代式
senses.definition: characteristic of a particular period, movement or regional building tradition
senses.definitionCN: 具有某一时期、流派或地区建筑传统特征的
senses.example: The church is Victorian Gothic, a purely architectural label.
senses.exampleCN: 这座教堂是维多利亚哥特式，这是一个纯建筑学的标签。
senses.why: Styles are the grammar of the art. Once buildings are classified by pointed arches or concrete slabs, 'architectural' comes to mean 'belonging to that grammar' rather than to any single building.
senses.whyCN: 风格是建筑艺术的语法。一旦建筑按尖拱或混凝土板被分类，architectural 就表示“属于那套语法”，而不是属于某一座建筑。

senses.title: Of drawings and models: the design on paper
senses.titleCN: 图纸与模型的：纸上的设计
senses.definition: relating to drawings, models or plans that specify how a building is to be made
senses.definitionCN: 与规定建筑如何建造的图纸、模型或方案有关
senses.example: The architectural drawings show a stair that the model omits.
senses.exampleCN: 建筑图纸上画了一部楼梯，模型里却漏掉了。
senses.why: The design exists before the building. Paper and card carry the art in advance, so the adjective attaches to the instruments that translate intention into construction.
senses.whyCN: 设计先于建筑存在。纸张和卡纸提前承载了这门艺术，因此形容词也附着于把意图转成施工的那些工具。

senses.title: Figurative framework: the architecture of an institution
senses.titleCN: 比喻性框架：制度的结构
senses.definition: relating to the underlying structural framework of an organisation, law or system, not to physical buildings
senses.definitionCN: 与组织、法律或系统的底层结构框架有关，而非物理建筑
senses.example: The constitutional settlement has an architectural logic that the reforms ignored.
senses.exampleCN: 宪制安排有一套建筑式的逻辑，而改革忽视了它。
senses.why: A building is a frame that carries loads; an institution is a frame that carries rights and duties. The same structural image lets architectural describe any carefully designed framework.
senses.whyCN: 建筑是承重的框架；制度是承载权利与义务的框架。同一幅结构意象让 architectural 可以形容任何精心设计的框架。

senses.title: Computing: the architecture of hardware and software
senses.titleCN: 计算机：硬件与软件的体系结构
senses.definition: relating to the layered design of a computer system, its instruction set or its software structure
senses.definitionCN: 与计算机系统的分层设计、指令集或软件结构有关
senses.example: An architectural flaw let one process read another's memory.
senses.exampleCN: 一个体系结构缺陷让一个进程能读取另一个进程的内存。
senses.why: Computer design borrowed the builder's word: processors, caches and layers are arranged like floors and load-bearing walls. Architectural therefore marks the plan rather than the code.
senses.whyCN: 计算机设计借用了建造者的词：处理器、缓存与层次像楼层和承重墙一样被安排。因此 architectural 标记的是“设计图”，而不是代码本身。

senses.title: Landscape architecture: designed outdoor space
senses.titleCN: 景观建筑：被设计的室外空间
senses.definition: relating to the planned arrangement of gardens, parks and outdoor spaces
senses.definitionCN: 与花园、公园及室外空间的规划布局有关
senses.example: The garden's architectural planting frames the view rather than filling it.
senses.exampleCN: 花园里建筑式的种植框住了景致，而不是填满它。
senses.why: Landscape architecture treats plants, paths and walls as building elements. Architectural here means that outdoor space is composed with the same structure, scale and rhythm as a facade.
senses.whyCN: 景观建筑把植物、路径和墙当作建筑元素。这里的 architectural 意为室外空间以与立面相同的结构、尺度与节奏被组织起来。

senses.title: Photography: buildings as the subject
senses.titleCN: 摄影：以建筑为题材
senses.definition: describing photographs that treat buildings, their lines and volumes as the main subject
senses.definitionCN: 指以建筑、其线条与体量为主要题材的照片
senses.example: Her architectural photographs flatten a cathedral into geometry.
senses.exampleCN: 她的建筑摄影把一座大教堂压平成几何图形。
senses.why: If the art is the subject, the photograph that studies it is architectural. The adjective moves from the object to the way the object is pictured.
senses.whyCN: 如果这门艺术是题材，研究它的照片也就是 architectural。形容词从对象转移到对象的观看方式。

senses.title: Heritage: buildings protected as evidence
senses.titleCN: 遗产：作为证据受保护的建筑
senses.definition: relating to buildings and structures valued and protected for their historical or aesthetic significance
senses.definitionCN: 与因历史或美学价值而受珍视和保护的建筑与构筑物有关
senses.example: The whole district was listed as architectural heritage.
senses.exampleCN: 整个街区被列为建筑遗产。
senses.why: When a building is valued as evidence of an art and a period, protection attaches to its architectural character. The adjective then names what the law and the museum preserve.
senses.whyCN: 当一座建筑作为某门艺术与某个时期的证据而被珍视，保护就附着于它的建筑特征。形容词于是命名法律与博物馆所保存的东西。

senses.title: Architectural acoustics: sound shaped by a space
senses.titleCN: 建筑声学：被空间塑造的声音
senses.definition: relating to the behaviour of sound in a designed room or building
senses.definitionCN: 与声音在被设计的房间或建筑中的行为有关
senses.example: The hall's architectural acoustics favour a string quartet over a lecture.
senses.exampleCN: 这座大厅的建筑声学更适合弦乐四重奏，而不是讲座。
senses.why: A building does not only carry loads; it also carries sound. Once surfaces and volumes are designed as part of the art, architectural extends to how a space sounds.
senses.whyCN: 建筑不只承重，也承载声音。一旦表面与体量被当作艺术的一部分来设计，architectural 就延伸到“空间听起来如何”。

intro.en: Architectural is a transparent derivative: architecture + -al, recorded in 1759. The whole family runs back through Latin architectura to Greek arkhitekton, 'chief builder', where arkhi- means chief and tekton means builder. That arkhi- is not the archaeo- of archaeology.
intro.cn: architectural 是透明的派生词：architecture + -al，记录于 1759 年。整个词族经由拉丁语 architectura 追到希腊语 arkhitekton“首席建造者”，其中 arkhi- 意为首席，tekton 意为建造者。这个 arkhi- 不是 archaeology 的 archaeo-。

items.en: Architecture enters English in the 1560s as 'the art of building', from French architecture and Latin architectura. Architect follows in the same decade from French architecte.
items.cn: architecture 于 1560 年代以“建筑的艺术”进入英语，来自法语 architecture 和拉丁语 architectura。architect 也在同一时期从法语 architecte 进入。

items.en: Latin architectus goes back to Greek arkhitekton 'master builder, director of works', a compound of arkhi- 'chief' (related to archon 'ruler') and tekton 'builder, carpenter'.
items.cn: 拉丁语 architectus 可追到希腊语 arkhitekton“首席建造者、工程主管”，由 arkhi-“首席”（与 archon“统治者”相关）和 tekton“建造者、木匠”复合而成。

items.en: By the 1610s architecture also names the building itself as something built according to architectural principles, not only the art.
items.cn: 到 1610 年代，architecture 也指按建筑原理建造的建筑物本身，而不再只指这门艺术。

items.en: Architectural is first recorded in 1759 as architecture + -al, the Latin adjective suffix -alis. It makes the discipline usable as a modifier.
items.cn: architectural 于 1759 年首次记录，由 architecture + -al（拉丁形容词后缀 -alis）构成。它使这门学科可以作为修饰语使用。

items.en: The arkhi- of architect means 'chief'; the archaeo- of archaeology means 'ancient'. They are different Greek stems and the two families are unrelated in meaning.
items.cn: architect 的 arkhi- 意为“首席”；archaeology 的 archaeo- 意为“古老”。它们是不同的希腊词干，两个词族在意义上并无关联。

items.en: From the 20c architectural extends to computing, landscape design, photography and heritage law, always keeping the idea of a designed frame.
items.cn: 20 世纪以后，architectural 扩展到计算机、景观设计、摄影与遗产法，始终保留“被设计的框架”这一观念。

note.en: The first group separates the base words from a dangerous look-alike with a different Greek stem; the second separates adjectives that also describe structure.
note.cn: 第一组区分基础词与一个词干不同的危险形似词；第二组区分同样描述结构的形容词。

entries.definition: The person who designs buildings. Architectural is the adjective from the abstract noun architecture, not from this person noun.
entries.definitionCN: 设计建筑的人。architectural 来自抽象名词 architecture，而不是这个指人的名词。

entries.definition: The art of building, or the buildings produced by it. Add -al to this noun to get architectural.
entries.definitionCN: 建筑的艺术，或由此产生的建筑。给这个名词加 -al 就得到 architectural。

entries.definition: Relating to archaeology. It shares the arch- look but comes from arkhaios 'ancient', not from arkhi- 'chief'.
entries.definitionCN: 与考古学有关的。它同样以 arch- 开头，但来自 arkhaios“古老”，不是 arkhi-“首席”。

entries.definition: Relating to the load-bearing frame or to the arrangement of parts. It stresses how something holds together, while architectural stresses design.
entries.definitionCN: 与承重框架或部件安排有关。它强调事物如何支撑，而 architectural 强调设计。

entries.definition: Relating to the process of constructing rather than to the finished design.
entries.definitionCN: 与建造过程有关，而不是与完成后的设计有关。

entries.definition: Relating to architecture as a system, or to a unified organising structure in art or thought. It is more technical than architectural.
entries.definitionCN: 与作为体系的建筑术有关，或与艺术、思想中的统一组织结构有关。它比 architectural 更技术化。

normalIntro.en: The links are real: architecture + -al, the Greek arkhi- 'chief' plus tekton 'builder', and the contrast with archaeological.
normalIntro.cn: 这些联想是真实的：architecture + -al，希腊语 arkhi-“首席”加 tekton“建造者”，以及与 archaeological 的对照。

normal.en: architecture + -al = architectural. The noun names the art; the adjective describes anything that belongs to it.
normal.cn: architecture + -al = architectural。名词命名艺术，形容词描述属于这门艺术的一切。

normal.en: architect = arkhi- 'chief' + tekton 'builder': a chief builder, not an old builder. That separates it from archaeology.
normal.cn: architect = arkhi-“首席”+ tekton“建造者”：首席建造者，不是古老的建造者。这条就把它与 archaeology 分开。

normal.en: The four everyday frames are architectural design, style, history and drawings.
normal.cn: 四个日常搭配是 architectural design、style、history 与 drawings。

normal.en: The figurative branch keeps the image of a frame: constitutions and software both have architecture before they have walls.
normal.cn: 比喻分支保留“框架”意象：宪法与软件都先有 architecture，才有“墙”。

normal.en: In a city, architectural quality is what survives the estate agent's description: proportion, structure and detail.
normal.cn: 在城市里，architectural 品质就是房产广告词褪去后仍留下的东西：比例、结构与细部。

abstract.en: Draw a floor plan over a photograph: the same building exists twice, once as design and once as mass.
abstract.cn: 在照片上叠一张平面图：同一座建筑存在两次，一次作为设计，一次作为体量。

abstract.en: Think of a skeleton inside a body: architectural is the frame that lets the surface stand.
abstract.cn: 想象身体里的骨架：architectural 就是让表面得以站立的框架。

abstract.en: The word always points to intention: something architectural was arranged by someone, not merely piled up.
abstract.cn: 这个词始终指向意图：被称为 architectural 的东西是被人安排过的，而不只是堆起来的。

examples.en: The museum's architectural value lies in its concrete shell, not its exhibits.
examples.cn: 这座博物馆的建筑价值在于它的混凝土外壳，而不在展品。

examples.en: They hired a photographer to record the architectural details before restoration.
examples.cn: 他们请了一位摄影师在修复前记录建筑细部。

examples.en: The software has an architectural problem that no patch can fix.
examples.cn: 这个软件有一个任何补丁都修不好的体系结构问题。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「阿基泰克扯罗」——阿基泰克在桌上扯罗蓝图，一笔画出拱门和梁柱 → architectural 建筑的、建筑设计的

root: 由 architecture + -al（拉丁 -alis）构成，1759 年首次记录；architecture 出自拉丁 architectura，再往前是希腊 arkhitekton“首席建造者”= arkhi-“首席”+ tekton“建造者”。

sensesIntro.en: Ten senses of architectural all describe something arranged by design: a profession, a building judged by its art, a style, a drawing, a constitutional frame, a computer system, a garden, a photograph, protected heritage, and the sound of a room.
sensesIntro.cn: architectural 的十个义项都在描述“被设计安排之物”：职业、按艺术标准评判的建筑、风格、图纸、宪制框架、计算机系统、花园、照片、受保护的遗产，以及一个房间的声音。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a blueprint weighted by a ruler, lines becoming arches, columns and beams.
core.cn: 核心意象：一张用尺压住的蓝图，线条变成拱、柱与梁。

branches.en: THE DESIGN CORE: the profession and its drawings, where the building exists before it is built.
branches.cn: 设计核心：职业与其图纸，建筑在建成之前已存在于此。

branches.en: THE BUILT RESULT: a structure judged by architectural rules, and a style that classifies it.
branches.cn: 建成结果：按建筑规则评判的构筑物，以及对它进行分类的风格。

branches.en: FRAMES WITHOUT WALLS: institutions and computer systems inherit the builder's structural image.
branches.cn: 没有墙的框架：制度与计算机系统继承了建造者的结构意象。

branches.en: OUTDOOR AND PICTURED: gardens composed like facades, and buildings turned into photographs.
branches.cn: 室外与影像：像立面一样构图的园林，以及被拍成照片的建筑。

branches.en: PROTECTED AND PERFORMED: heritage status preserves a building's character, and acoustics shows that character is also heard.
branches.cn: 保护与体验：遗产身份保存建筑的特征，声学则表明这种特征也能被听见。

intro.en: Architectural stacks three layers: Greek arkhi- 'chief' + tekton 'builder' gave arkhitekton, Latin made architectus and architectura, French passed architecture to English, and English added the adjective suffix -al in 1759.
intro.cn: architectural 叠了三层：希腊语 arkhi-“首席”+ tekton“建造者”给出 arkhitekton，拉丁语造出 architectus 与 architectura，法语把 architecture 传给英语，英语又在 1759 年加上形容词后缀 -al。

latinIntro.en: Latin architectus and architectura are borrowings from Greek arkhitekton. The suffix -alis simply means 'pertaining to', and it is the same suffix seen in archival and archaeological.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语 architectus 与 architectura 是借自希腊语 arkhitekton 的词。-alis 后缀只表示“与……有关”，它与 archival、archaeological 中的后缀相同。

items.structure: archi- (chief) + tect (builder); Greek arkhitekton via Latin architectus
items.meaning: a person who designs buildings; also to design or plan
items.meaningCN: 建筑师；设计者；设计、规划（动词）
items.example: She was the architect of both the building and the deal.
items.exampleCN: 她既是这座建筑的设计者，也是这笔交易的策划者。

items.meaning: the art of building; buildings; the structure of a system
items.meaningCN: 建筑学；建筑；体系结构（-ure 构成结果或艺术名词）
items.example: The architecture of the old town grew around one square.
items.exampleCN: 老城的建筑布局是围绕一个广场生长起来的。

items.meaning: relating to architecture or to a designed structure
items.meaningCN: 建筑的；建筑设计的；结构上的（-al 构成形容词）
items.example: The plan preserves the architectural character of the street.
items.exampleCN: 该方案保留了这条街的建筑特征。

items.meaning: in architectural terms; by architectural means
items.meaningCN: 在建筑上；从建筑角度（-ly 构成副词）
items.example: The two blocks are architecturally unrelated.
items.exampleCN: 这两栋楼在建筑上毫无关联。

items.meaning: relating to architecture as a system, or to a unifying structure
items.meaningCN: 建筑术的；体系结构的；有统一构架的（-onic 构成形容词）
items.example: The essay has an architectonic clarity.
items.exampleCN: 这篇文章有一种建筑式的清晰结构。

items.meaning: the science of architecture, or the systematic arrangement of knowledge
items.meaningCN: 建筑术；知识体系学（-s 构成抽象名词）
items.example: Kant wrote of the architectonics of pure reason.
items.exampleCN: 康德论述过纯粹理性的体系结构。

items.meaning: chief, first in rank, principal
items.meaningCN: 希腊语构词成分：首席、位次第一、主要的
items.example: Archi- appears in architect, archbishop and archipelago.
items.exampleCN: archi- 出现在 architect、archbishop 与 archipelago 中。

items.meaning: builder, carpenter, craftsman
items.meaningCN: 希腊语名词：建造者、木匠、工匠
items.example: Tekton is the second half of arkhitekton, the source of architect.
items.exampleCN: tekton 是 arkhitekton 的后半部分，也就是 architect 的来源。

latinEntries.meaningCN: 拉丁语名词，来自希腊语：首席建造者、工匠头
拉丁语名词：建筑的艺术
希腊语前缀：首席、主要、第一
希腊语名词：建造者、木匠

definition_zh: 档案；档案馆；档案库；存档资料；（动词）把……归档、存档
definition_en: a collection of historical records preserved as evidence, the place that holds them, or a store of data; as a verb, to file or preserve something in such a collection
core_image: 一排贴着年份标签的灰色档案盒，盒口露出纸页边缘
scene: A vault room holds rows of grey boxes labelled by year; one box is open on a table beside a laptop copying its scans. The vault is the company's archive, and every box in it is kept as evidence.
sceneCN: 这里 archive 是「保存作证据的历史记录集合」（第 1 个义项：档案集合）；句意：这间库房是公司的档案库，每只盒子都作为证据保存。图中可辨识物件：档案盒、年份标签、纸页、库房铁门、台灯、笔记本电脑。

pos.zh: 档案；档案馆；档案库；存档资料

forms.label: 过去分词（动词，完成／被动）

档案主义；以档案为导向的实践
